Sports.title: I try to manage like Jurgen Klopp - but an ex-Liverpool and Man City coach taught me more
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: I try to manage like Jurgen Klopp - but an ex-Liverpool and Man City coach taught me more

EXCLUSIVE: Craig Fagan has enjoyed a fine start to life in management after replacing Wolves icon George Elokobi at non-league Maidstone United in the summer

View 4 Images Former Premier League forward Craig Fagan (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

Starting a first managerial role is widely considered one of the toughest transitions in football. Arsene Wenger, Diego Simeone, Antonio Conte and Bobby Robson are among the high-profile coaches to have struggled in their maiden jobs.

‌



‌



But former Premier League forward Craig Fagan has taken to the managerial scene like a duck to water, and is thriving in his first senior position after he was appointed as first-team manager at National League South side Maidstone United in April. The 43-year-old spent three years as assistant to George Elokobi at the Kent club before getting the top role at the end of last season.

‌



Since becoming the main man, Fagan has helped propel Maidstone to the top of the table, winning six, drawing one and losing three of his first 10 league matches, picking up 19 points in the process. Although the Stones crashed out of the FA Cup at the first hurdle, losing to Isthmian League Premier side Cray Wanderers, Fagan's start to life as a manager has still been a success.

‌



Reflecting on his first six months in the job, Fagan, who retired from professional football in 2015 after a 13-year playing career, told The Mirror: "Enjoyable; you get less sleep being a manager because your mind is always going, but I've enjoyed every minute so far.

"Similar in terms of assistant manager, but the only difference now is decisions and the results lie on me more than what it is as an assistant manager, but I'm enjoying every minute of it so far."

"Disappointing to be out of the FA Cup, of course," Fagan added, when asked about his assessment of the season so far with Maidstone top of the National League South. "Our club has always done well since I've been here in terms of getting through the rounds, so it was a disappointment this season.

‌



"But the league position I would say we're doing well, maybe ahead of schedule in terms of our budget compared to some of the others in the league, but the players have done well. We've had a bit of a blip, lost the last two in the league, but we need to get back to what they've done.

"I think we've kind of been a victim of our own success, and I've said this to the players, they've gained belief from doing well in the first month or so, won a lot of games, and then we stopped doing what brought us joy in the last two games, and that's part of management, getting everybody back to basics and getting everybody doing the things that brought us joy again."

View 4 Images Craig Fagan during his time as a player at Hull City (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Fagan's Maidstone side embodies what he was like as a player: hard-working, high-energy and direct. They like to get the ball forward, out wide with speed, put crosses into the box and have shots at goal. Out of possession, the Stones press with intensity and aim to win the ball back as soon as possible.

Maidstone have also managed to score in all 10 league matches this season - the only team in the division to have reached that feat so far. Fagan has implemented an attacking approach which has benefited the front players, with striker Tom Leahy joint-second in the top goalscorers list with five this campaign.

"I like to see hard work, not ridiculous, running past people to close the goalkeeper down or nothing silly like that," Fagan said on his side's style of football. "Supporters pay their money and want to see hard-working and attractive football at times. For myself, it's what I want the players to be doing.

‌



"They get paid by the football club, they should at least work hard in terms of closing down and pressing. I like to press on the front, I like to be aggressive in the way that we press. Maybe it does pass over a little bit.

"Like I said, I've had to work hard so I don't see why other players can't do so. Talent only takes you so far, you need determination and hard work with both."

Fagan's style is thought to be similar to Jurgen Klopp's 'rock and roll football' seen at Liverpool, with players pressing from the front, working hard to win the ball back and not messing around when in possession, getting it out wide with purpose and having lots of efforts.

‌



And Fagan, who played for Hull City, Derby County and Birmingham City, among others, in his playing career, admitted he is a "big fan" of Klopp and his former assistant Pep Lijnders, saying he studied them both and how they transformed Liverpool into a counter-pressing, relentless machine.

View 4 Images Craig Fagan looks up to Jurgen Klopp (Image: Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty Images)

Asked if there are any managers he has modelled his style to, Fagan said: "The best way I'd explain it is that us football coaches and managers are all thieves. We try to steal from the best managers and the best coaches. Obviously, managers I've played for, I've taken some bits and some bits I definitely don't want to use in terms of managers which I didn't agree with some of the stuff they did.

‌



"But when I look at the styles I've played, I was a big fan of Liverpool when Jurgen Klopp was there in terms of the way they like to attack quickly, play football at the right times. He's someone I've studied, the way they play.

"I was on my A License with Pep Lijnders, so I like the way he's been in the way of his coaching manner and the way he goes about stuff. But for me, again, a team based on hard work that plays football in the right areas, that can get the ball wide and can attack with and attack in freedom. Because like I said to you before, fans want to see attacking football and they want to see exciting football.

"I think sometimes now the way the modern game's gone, because of Pep [Guardiola], of course, he's changed England in the way that people want to play football. But I'm not one that wants to get wide players into wide areas that don’t cross the football. I've played in both areas as a wide player and as a front man, and sometimes I watch some of the Premier League games and I don't know how some of the forwards do it without moaning, being starved of crosses going in the box.

‌



"Everybody has their own style, but my style is I want to get the ball wide so I get crosses in the box. I want players to have freedom if they feel that they can get shot off and it means a tap-in for a centre-forward. That would be something I would want as a centre forward. It means you have to do less work and score 10 goals from that. That's my kind of style."

View 4 Images Craig Fagan was a hard-working forward (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

After retiring 11 years ago, Fagan went straight into coaching. He earned his UEFA A License badge in 2018 where he came across ex-Liverpool and Manchester City assistant Lijnders.

‌



Sharing his experience of learning from Lijnders, Fagan said: "He was excellent and he was pretty open in terms of how he went about things. He had a great career going from there, from the A licence. He's similar to how he was. Very open, very passionate, wants to develop players, knew who he was.

"Some of the stuff he's done, especially with Jurgen Klopp, with their sessions, is some of the stuff which I simply tried to bring in, as well as other coaches of course. He was just someone that was on my A Licence, which I look up to now still. I know he's not in the game at the moment, but he's had a great career and someone you aspire to be."

Fagan, who scored 58 goals in 357 appearances during his senior career, coached Hull City's Under 23s, Southend United and Welling United before finding his feet at Maidstone.

Article continues below

But, having lost twice on the bounce to Cray and Truro City, Maidstone and Fagan are hoping to get back on the winning trail when they travel to Horsham on Saturday afternoon.

Sports.title: Carrick must share burden of Man Utd's underperformance with his players
Sports.content:
"We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it." A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.

Stuck in the mire of Manchester United's worst start to a league season for 40 years, the manager appeared lost for legitimate reasons. His margin for error is shrinking by the week.

Why were his side outplayed at home by the Premier League's bottom club? Why can't they hold onto leads? Why do they seem incapable of playing against 10 men?

Image: Michael Carrick looks on during Man Utd's draw with Tottenham

All of these are fair questions to put to the man himself and many were asked of Carrick in the wake of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Spurs. None were answered with enough detail to satisfy, though, only really serving to hold a mirror up to what was delivered on the pitch: inadequacy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from Manchester United's match against Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League

Clearly the manager can only accept so much of the blame. His players are yet to offer a single complete performance, only bit-part displays of individualism and self-direction. Where is the cohesiveness that shaped the backend of last year? What happened to the clarity that turned a collapsed season into a third-place finish?

Fans who turn up to Old Trafford every week are back to being unsure. They do not know what to expect from one game to the next, only how to voice their dissatisfaction at what transpires. Three separate choruses of boos could be heard from the terraces on Saturday.

"I think the fans will stay with the project," reflected Gary Neville from Old Trafford. "I don't think the boos are against Michael Carrick for one minute. But what I would say is, they're turning quite quickly."

When United needed a calm voice to steer the ship at the beginning of this year, they turned to a man whose entire playing career was built on it. That version of Manchester United feels far removed from the side that have begun this season, though.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville feels the midfield partnership of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo lacks dynamism and is not suited to the Premier League

In midfield is where the problems are most evident. And yet, that is the department that received the biggest injection of cash this summer, a complete overhaul in terms of personnel and profiles. The Kobbie Mainoo-Youri Tielemans axis is not working. Andrey Santos is barely getting a look in.

Hopes that Carlos Baleba can hit the ground running after an injury-hit start were audible; his introduction after an hour lifted the whole stadium. Almost every touch was positive and he took care of the ball, completing 16 of 18 passes and creating as many chances as Bruno Fernandes managed all game (2).

Still, the space and freedom with which Spurs operated presents issues that cannot be solved by one midfielder. United were carved open time after time, gaps appearing in a myriad of ways. The visitors were able to win possession in the final third five times in the first half alone. Five of United's work-shy starters did not go away for international duty over the break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dominic Solanke snatched a late equaliser for 10-man Spurs

And it was not just the aggressiveness of Spurs' press that was effective. They picked holes in United with the ball, too, using slick one-touch combinations to move through the thirds with pace and purpose. Savio attempted 10 dribbles. He only completed half but the recurrence was evidence of his belief that United could be got at. He was right.

Then there are concerns over the mentality of a side who repeatedly fail to beat 10 men. Yet again, United were outrun and outpaced - this time by a team who played with a man less for 21 minutes, including stoppage time.

"If we're ahead in the game, we have to see it out," says Carrick. That much is obvious. What is less clear is how some of these patterns of missteps are going to be addressed.

"Football is character," concluded opposition boss Roberto De Zerbi. United must find some character from somewhere, or risk being eaten up by the competition. If the last few weeks have taught us anything, it's that the Premier League is in no mood to be handing out sympathy.

Sports.title: Van Gerwen dumped out of Swiss Darts Trophy as nightmare year goes on
Sports.content:
Michael van Gerwen's nightmare year went from bad to worse as he was dumped out of the Swiss Darts Trophy in his opening match by Mensur Suljovic 6-4 on Saturday night.

Suljovic led 5-2 before Van Gerwen threatened a comeback but three missed darts to force a decider allowed Suljovic to take advantage.

It was Suljovic's fourth straight win over Van Gerwen and the fifth time in six tournaments that the Dutchman has exited after one match.

Van Gerwen's woes continue

Defeat in Basel marks the first time Michael van Gerwen has lost his opening match in FOUR European Tour events in the same season since its inception in 2012



European Darts Trophy ❌



German Darts Grand Prix ❌



Flanders Darts Trophy ❌



Swiss Darts Trophy ❌



Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Colin Lloyd discusses Van Gerwen's ongoing struggles

Luke Humphries, Gian van Veen and Jonny Clayton all advanced to Finals Day as ten seeds crashed out on a remarkable day of action in Basel.

Newly crowned World Grand Prix champion Humphries was among the headline acts on Day Two at the St. Jakobshalle, where he prevailed against Kevin Doets.

Despite racing 3-0 ahead with 122 and 121 checkouts, Humphries was forced to survive a furious fightback from Doets, defying the Dutchman's 105.64 average to triumph in a breathless decider.

"I was really pleased with that performance," reflected Humphries, who averaged almost 103 and pinned 67% of his attempts at double.

"I felt like I was the better player for most of the game, but Kevin was really strong at the end there, so I had to really work my socks off."

European Champion Van Veen also impressed on Swiss soil, producing a hat-trick of ton-plus checkouts to whitewash a shell-shocked Niko Springer in just under ten minutes.

Clayton, meanwhile, stole the show with an irrepressible display against Maik Kuivenhoven, averaging 108.81 and landing two bullseye finishes to kick off his title bid in style.

The Welshman will take on Rob Cross for a place in the quarter-finals, after the former world champion halted Luke Woodhouse's mid-match fightback to close out a battling 6-4 victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Stephen Bunting looks back on that viral interview with Raymond van Barneveld at Ally Pally

There will be a new champion crowned at the St Jakobshalle on Sunday evening, as former champions Stephen Bunting and Martin Schindler crashed out on a day of upsets in Basel.

Swedish star Jeffrey de Graaf put in a clinical display of doubling to account for reigning champion Bunting, while Schindler was swept aside by Tom Bissell, who will feature at Finals Day for the first time in his European Tour career.

Dirk van Duijvenbode recorded a fifth straight win against James Wade to end the left-hander's bid for back-to-back European Tour titles, and a resurgent Michael Smith now awaits the Dutchman in the last 16.

The 2023 world champion delivered one of his best performances of the year to seal a 6-4 against Jermaine Wattimena, converting consecutive 116, 124 and 144 checkouts in the process.

Sports.title: NFL Gameday Guide: Jags and Eagles land in London
Sports.content:
The Jacksonville Jaguars return to London this week to play what will mark their 15th and 16th regular-season games in England's capital since 2013, featuring as part of the league's 44th and 45th games in the UK since 2007 as well as a record slate of nine international matchups in 2026.

It will see Jags punter Logan Cooke play in an NFL-record 10th international game to surpass former Jacksonville offensive lineman Tyler Shatley, per ESPN stats.

But this has a different feel to that of the Jags teams from years gone by, who have monopolised London without ever truly inserting themselves among football's Super Bowl contenders. The 2017 team that stunned the NFL to reach the AFC Championship Game, perhaps, being the exception to that rule.

This time they arrive to take on the Philadelphia Eagles behind a true MVP candidate in Trevor Lawrence and a head coach in Liam Coen knocking on the door of the elite. It is not a team brimming with star names, but instead an expertly-drilled reflection of their coach's vision for contention.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Philadelphia Eagles at the Chicago Bears from Week 3 of the NFL season

The Jags are 3-1 and purring at the top of the AFC South, their one blemish a defeat to the Denver Broncos in which they can been control before letting the game slip away.

Momentum is on their side after back-to-back statement wins over the New England Patriots and Cincinnati Bengals, in contrast to an opponent battling to steady a ship rocked by injury, retirement and consecutive losses. There is an overwhelming case of deja vu for the Eagles, whose soaring expectations can occasionally make for a gloomier fan outlook than is actually the case.

The last time the Eagles faced the Jaguars, Saquon Barkley conjured one of the greatest plays in NFL history with his reverse hurdle over Jacksonville cornerback Jarrian Jones back in November 2024.

"Everybody DM'd me like I'm supposed to be mad or something," Jones said on Wednesday. "I don't give a damn. He made a good play. It is what it is."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Eagles running back Saquon Barkley hurdle a defender backwards in an incredible play from last season

Barkley's availability for Sunday is in doubt after the running back exited Week Four's defeat to the Los Angeles Rams with a hamstring injury. The Eagles had already been missing leading wide receiver DeVonta Smith due to a hamstring issue, the former Heisman Trophy winner having become Jalen Hurts' unequivocal top target this offseason following the marquee departure of AJ Brown.

This week meanwhile saw stalwart offensive tackle Lane Johnson announce his shock retirement to focus on his mental health, before center Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens. What's more, wide receiver Hollywood Brown, edge rusher Jonathan Greenard and linebacker Jihaad Campbell all missed practice this week through injury.

On paper, it is a decimated Eagles team so far failing to demonstrate the kind of offensive resurgence expected under Sean Mannion after he replaced Kevin Patullo as offensive coordinator in the offseason. Philly's offense enters Sunday's game at Tottenham averaging the fourth-fewest yards per game, second-fewest passing yards per game, 26th in scoring and 29th in EPA/play.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jason Bell believes Trevor Lawrence is showing a 'maturity' that has changed 'everything' for the Jacksonville Jaguars

Jalen Hurts also continues to be one of the most divisive quarterbacks in football as critics wrestle over his true value, who is suffering in a system lacking serious punch on the ground and the consistent presence of a Brown on the outside - with the greatest of respect to the always-reliable hands of Smith.

The Jags have their identity. The Eagles are still searching desperately for theirs.

Nick Sirianni's side have elected to fly in just 36 hours before kickoff in London, following a similar plan to that of Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams when they travelled in on the eve of their dominant win over the Jaguars at Wembley.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Dallas Cowboys from Week 5 of the NFL season

Things to watch live on Sky:

Philadelphia Eagles @ Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium - KO 2.30pm - LIVE from 2pm on Sky Sports NFL and Sky Sports+:

The Jags might have finally found their answer as to how best they use Travis Hunter. Both he and they started this partnership with the best intentions of revolutionising football with a full-time two-way player, Hunter having famously starred at receiver and corner in college. To drift from as much wouldn't be to concede defeat, but instead recognise Hunter's potential to become one of the premier defensive backs in football. Right now, that looks like where his future lies. Hunter played 71 defensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Bengals and gave up just four catches for 30 yards while seeing an interception nullified by a penalty up front. Receiver packages can still be in play from time to time, but the signs are there of Hunter finally making his mark in the NFL, on defense.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Atlanta Falcons at Green Bay Packers from Week 3 of the NFL season

Chicago Bears @ Green Bay Packers - KO 6pm - Exclusively LIVE from 6pm on Sky Sports NFL, Sky Sports Football and part on Sky Sports Main Event:

Ben Johnson's Chicago Bears offense enters Sunday's rivalry matchup boasting the No 1-ranked rushing attack in football behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, who lead a ground unit averaging 196.3 yards per game. It has become the perfect remedy to the loss of starting quarterback Caleb Williams, teeing up Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent for success in his absence. Bagent will start again on Sunday as Chicago arrive 3-1 against a Packers side yet to convince after a 2-2 start. Matt LaFleur's offense ranks dead last in offense amid the absence of Josh Jacobs due to his off-field legal problems, while they are also averaging a fifth-fewest points per game.

Minnesota Vikings @ New Orleans Saints - KO 6pm - LIVE from 6pm on Sky Sports+:

Tyler Shough is braced for one of the defining acid tests of his young NFL career as the New Orleans Saints quarterback comes up against a Brian Flores defense that has spearheaded the Minnesota Vikings to a 4-0 start this season. The Vikings are ranked third in pressures with 72, according to Pro Football Focus, while leading the league in points allowed. Dallas Turner is ranked second with 5.5 sacks behind only Buffalo's Greg Rousseau amid what is shaping up as a breakout season, thriving in a defense that leads the NFL by a distance with a blitz rate of almost 70 per cent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Philadelphia Eagles' Darius Cooper makes a sensational catch for a touchdown in his team's clash with the Los Angeles Rams

San Francisco 49ers @ Seattle Seahawks - KO 9.25pm - Exclusively LIVE from 9.15pm on Sky Sports NFL, Sky Sports Football, and part on Sky Sports Main Event:

If the San Francisco 49ers are to be serious Super Bowl contenders, they need this version of George Kittle for an entire undisrupted season. The way he moved on Sunday's 56-yard touchdown catch-and-run, you would not believe he is just coming off a season-ending torn Achilles. It was Kittle at his electric best, executing a perfect blitz-crushing Kyle Shanahan call to underline everything that makes this 49ers offense so innovative and so dangerous when everybody is healthy. Kittle has 16 catches for 244 yards and four touchdowns so far in 2026 as part of a 49ers attack ranked seventh in yards and third in scoring.

Detroit Lions @ Arizona Cardinals - KO 9.25pm - Exclusively LIVE from 9.25pm on Sky Sports Football:

The Cardinals are coming off last weekend's 36-24 defeat to the Giants, during which Jacoby Brissett threw three interceptions while both start running back Jeremiyah Love and tight end Trey McBride were largely bottled up as the focal points of their offense. Sunday welcomes two of the NFL's most porous defenses, the Lions allowing a second-most 31.8 points per game to the Cardinals' fourth-most 29.3. Jared Goff has been clean even if not spectacular over the first month of the campaign, 109 of 161 passing for a second-most 1,214 yards and nine touchdowns to zero interceptions. He is the only quarterback ever in NFL history to have 1,200-plus passing yards with zero turnovers through four games of a season while not having a winning record, according to Opta Stats. The Lions come into Sunday 2-2 after losing 32-26 to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday night.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New England Patriots' Efton Chism's late 23-yard touchdown was the difference in their clash with the Buffalo Bills

Baltimore Ravens @ Atlanta Falcons - KO 1.20am (Monday) - LIVE from 1.10am (Monday) on Sky Sports NFL and Sky Sports Main Event:

The Atlanta Falcons look a completely different proposition to the team that began the season 0-2 behind backup quarterback Cooper Rush. Michael Penix Jr has flourished on his return from injury in victories over the Packers and Saints, completing 73.3 per cent of his passes for 479 yards and two touchdowns. With some stability at quarterback has come deserved reward for Bijan Robinson, who is second only to Kansas City's Kenneth Walker III with 614 yards from scrimmage through the first month. That includes 339 yards and four touchdowns on the ground over the last two weeks alone. Lamar Jackson availability is meanwhile in question after the ankle injury he suffered against the Tennessee Titans in Week Four, with Tyler Huntley in line to start should the two-time MVP miss out. Declan Doyle is still perhaps in second gear with his Ravens offense, which itself looks a completely different threat with Zay Flowers in the lineup as a field-flipping aerial complement to Jackson and Derrick Henry on the ground. The Ravens are averaging the fifth-most yards and fifth-most rushing yards per game after a 3-1 start.

Sports.title: Neville's Man Utd warning: 'Get a grip or face worrying few weeks'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville warned Manchester United could be in for a "worrying few weeks" if their players don't "get a grip" on their season after they were booed in their draw with Tottenham.

Michael Carrick's side's poor start to the campaign continued as Dominic Solanke's 92nd-minute goal rescued a point for the 10-man visitors at Old Trafford on Saturday.

There were boos from the home fans, both at half-time and full-time, as United extended their winless run to four games in all competitions, keeping them 12th in the Premier League.

They now face a daunting run of fixtures, starting with a Champions League away game against Atletico Madrid on Tuesday before Sunday's Premier League trip to Elland Road to face Leeds, live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player FREE TO WATCH: Highlights from the game between Man Utd and Spurs

Speaking on The Gary Neville Podcast, Neville questioned the midfield pairing of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo and said the side's plight could worsen if their players do not show improvement.

"Tielemans and Mainoo, I think we've seen enough of it now," Neville said.

"I'm not calling time on it because that's probably too drastic, but I've seen enough to think that's not a midfield that's dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.

"I think they are both good players individually. But sometimes you just have players that don't quite knit together or don't quite suit each other.

"I think when [Carlos] Baleba came on with Mainoo, it looked like there was a lot more energy.

Image: Spurs missed a succession of chances to go ahead before Man Utd's opener

"There's going to have to be something done in there, and the rest of them are going to have to get a grip because they are going to Diego Simeone's Atletico Madrid and Elland Road.

"If you're not quite right there from a mental and physical perspective, you're going to get found out.

"They've got a couple of days to recover, pick themselves up from this and get going, because if they don't get going it's going to be a worrying few weeks."

'Fans are turning quite quickly'

Neville felt the boos inside Old Trafford were not aimed at head coach Carrick but described the performance as "worrying" and said supporters are picking up on a lack of effort and energy from the players.

"It was worrying because I think the three-week break was the reset moment," he added. "This was the start of a big period of eight games in 28 days.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking after Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Tottenham at Old Trafford, Gary Neville questioned the energy and enthusiasm of Michael Carrick's side

"What I really would have expected today from Manchester United was a really enthusiastic, energetic performance from minute one.

"I didn't see an enthusiastic, energetic performance from those red shirts for an hour, and Spurs should have been three or four-nil up.

"I think the fans will stay with the project. I don't think the boos are against Michael Carrick for one minute. But what I would say is they're turning quite quickly.

"Manchester United fans are incredibly loyal, beyond loyal, to their managers and to their players, but what they won't accept is a lack of energy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville feels the midfield partnership of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo lacks dynamism and is not up to the required standard

"They won't accept a lack of what they deem to be effort. I don't like saying effort but the reality is they're not running enough, they're not showing enough tenacity, determination, fighting spirit. They're just not.

"They booed after 22 minutes, they booed at half-time and they booed at the end. That tells you that they're really despondent with what they're watching.

"My daughter comes and watches every single week. She texted me at half-time, 'What's that?' My daughter's 16 years of age. You can't kid or con a football fan. No matter who they are, they know what they're watching.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Manchester United defender Harry Maguire was seen saying 'bye bye' and waving Rodrigo Bentancur off the pitch after his red card

"I don't mind winning here, don't mind losing here, but there's got to be a massive amount of effort and it can't be boring, simple as that.

"You can have a shootout and lose 4-2 and think, 'OK, well at least we saw a Manchester United that went forward with verve and all those things that you'd expect'.

Image: Bryan Mbeumo's goal was cancelled out by Dominic Solanke

"But what we're seeing at the moment is a team that looks like they're curling up in a ball. For some of them right now, it looks like the club is getting a bit big for them.

"A lot of them played well last season here, but it just looks like now it's coming on top for them a little bit and it's starting to just get to them.

"It did a little bit under Ruben Amorim towards the end where they just started to go a little bit like that.

"So look, Michael Carrick has got to get something out of them, the boos I don't think are against him, but the pressure's on him, the questions are obviously always with the manager and you just hope they can come out of it in these next few weeks."

Sports.title: Sherrock, Hayter qualify for Worlds as Greaves sweeps up on Women's Series
Sports.content:
Fallon Sherrock and Gemma Hayter have qualified for the 2027 PDC World Championship as Beau Greaves won Events 21-22 at the Women's Series in Wigan on Saturday.

'The Queen of the Palace' will return to the place where she wrote history in 2020, after she confirmed her spot in the top five of the Women's Series.

Sherrock became the first (and only) woman to pick up wins at Alexandra Palace, beating Ted Evetts and Mensur Suljovic before losing to Chris Dobey.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fallon Sherrock became the first woman to defeat a man at a World Championship with victory over Ted Evetts

She has since returned five times but came up fruitless against the likes of Steve Beaton, Ricky Evans, Jermaine Wattimena, Ryan Meikle and Dave Chisnall.

She will make her seventh appearance in December, despite only picking up one title so far on the Women's Series.

Hayter's run to the Event 22 final was enough to confirm her World Championship return.

Hayter qualified after reaching her third final of the year; she is now confirmed to finish in the top five on the Women's Series Order of Merit, hence booking her spot at a second World Championship.

She lost on debut to Josh Rock last year but took a set in a good performance.

She also picked up the WDF World Masters Title in 2026, as well as her first win at the Women's World Matchplay.

Hayter will be joined at Alexandra Palace by Lisa Ashton, Sherrock and Greaves, with Vicky Pruim currently in pole position to claim the final qualification spot via the PDC Women's Series rankings.

'Beau 'n' Arrow' breezed to the Event 21 title in emphatic style, conceding just five legs in scooping her 14th title of the campaign.

Sports.title: Ten-man Spurs claim dramatic draw at Old Trafford as Man Utd booed off
Sports.content:
Tottenham rescued an unlikely point at Manchester United after fighting back to draw 1-1 with 10 men - but their search for a Premier League win extends into another unwelcome week.

The point at least lifts Spurs off the foot of the table, but Roberto De Zerbi's side remain marooned in the relegation zone, without a league victory since May.

Their predicament can be summed up by three cases of extreme wastefulness and one of ill-discipline, with Dominic Solanke particularly guilty of spurning the chances that might have seen his side take a comfortable first-half lead.

Instead, it was Bryan Mbeumo who broke the deadlock in the 73rd minute, combining with Matheus Cunha in the box and turning smartly to guide a clinical finish across Antonin Kinsky.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mbeumo fired Manchester United ahead

Spurs spent most of the game in the ascendancy but were hurtling towards their fourth loss of an already chaotic campaign, made worse by a moment of madness from Rodrigo Bentancur, who saw red for a headbutt motion towards Luke Shaw five minutes after the goal. The incident sparked a touchline brawl between both benches.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rodrigo Bentancur saw red for a headbutt on Luke Shaw

As emotions ran high, De Zerbi's mission looked hopeless. But Spurs did not give up, and were rewarded with a leveller in stoppage time when Solanke glanced a header past a static Senne Lammens.

Neither manager is likely to be satisfied with the outcome.

Man Utd were booed off the pitch at half time and full time, stuck in the midst of their worst start to a season for 40 years. Spurs' plight, meanwhile, is arguably more damning still. After the points were shared, it's perhaps a result that leaves more questions than answers for both.

Man Utd's poor start Man Utd have won six points from their opening six games of the season, their fewest at this stage of a league campaign since 1986-87.

The key moments from Old Trafford...

Image: Dominic Solanke celebrates after scoring a late equaliser

3: MISS! Lucas Bergvall pounces on a poor Lammens pass to put Solanke through on goal, but the striker can't punish the mistake.

21: HUGE CHANCE! Savio sets up Kudus, who hooks a first-time shot wide of Lammens' right-hand post.

34: SHOT! Mbeumo feeds Amad on the counter, but his low shot is easily saved by Kinsky.

42: CHANCE! Solanke plays in Conor Gallagher, who just needs to pull the trigger but he takes too long and allows Lammens to save.

49: CHANCE! Spurs pass up another chance as Savio drives into the box and rolls the ball back into the six-yard box but Shaw clears.

51: OVER! Savio gets to the byline and crosses for Solanke, who balloons over from six yards out.

73: GOAL! Mbeumo scores smart opener on the turn, beating Kinsky with a clean, low drive.

90+2: GOAL! Martinez is distracted as Sandro Tonali's cross comes in, losing sight of the ball and allowing Solanke to glance a header home.

Carrick with soul-searching to do after 'worrying' performance

Sky Sports' Gary Neville:

"Tottenham deserved a point. That was a really important moment for Solanke. He'd missed some big chances and was captain for the first time.

"They were the better team by far. If they'd left without a point, it would have been terrible for them.

"Michael Carrick is left with a lot to think about. It was a worrying day in terms of the level of performance and a big week ahead."

Man Utd devoid of structure and ideas

Sky Sports' Jamie Redknapp:

"I do not see enough connections in that midfield and they look devoid of any confidence, ideas, or patterns of play, playing out the back.

"Tottenham were just much better than them in every department, but that is a theme this season.

"Their energy levels are not good enough and they look loose going forward; there was no real structure.

"The squad is not good or strong enough and Michael [Carrick] needs help in that respect."

Carrick admits Man Utd were 'off it'

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick:

"We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it.

"I'm not happy with the amount of points, I'm not hiding from that. We need to put things in a positive direction quickly.

"We have to be more streetwise and stubborn in the moment. It doesn't change my belief, or confidence in the players. We can be a really good team.

"We don't want to start games like that, it was challenging. They worked through it, got themselves in a good position, and couldn't see the game out. That's the most disappointing thing.

"I don't feel let down bty players making mistakes but we've all got to help each other be better."

De Zerbi pleased with different Spurs character

Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi:

"We did not deserve to lose, for sure. Today, for the first time we showed we're a team. We played for team-mates, stayed inside of the game in every situation. We attack and defend as a team.

"Suffer together. We have to find the balance between confidence, and to be hungry in training and in games.

"For a long time Tottenham played without this character, now I'm the coach, I want to see this character every week. With the quality, with character, the right energy, I think we're going to win many games and score many goals."
