Sports.title: Floyd Schofield vs Lucas Bahdi Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Tristan Kalkreuth (18-1, 13 KOs) stopped previously unbeaten Ivan Rosado (12-1, 9 KOs) at 0:44 of the third round in cruiserweight action. Kalkreuth used his height and reach to control the scheduled ten-round fight, leaving the shorter Rosado struggling to get his offense going.

The 24-year-old pressed the action and overwhelmed Rosado with his power. Rosado could not adequately defend himself as Kalkreuth continued the attack early in round three. The referee stepped in with Rosado still on his feet, ending a one-sided contest. Rosado’s unbeaten record offered little protection against the larger Kalkreuth, who dictated the fight throughout.

Heavyweight Joshua Edwards (8-0, 7 KOs) stopped Craig Lewis (15-10-1, 8 KOs) at the start of the third round of their scheduled eight-round bout. The 2024 U.S. Olympian controlled the action against the 42-year-old veteran, forcing him onto the defensive.

Edwards landed a combination late in the second round that hurt Lewis and brought the fight toward its finish. Lewis could not continue because of an injury, prompting the stoppage at the beginning of round three. The injury’s exact nature was not specified in the early ringside account. Edwards needed just two completed rounds to register his seventh stoppage victory.

Grant Flores (14-0, 10 KOs) stopped Mikey Dahlman (19-3, 17 KOs) in the second round of their scheduled eight-round light middleweight bout. Flores controlled the action with his size and punching power, putting the veteran under pressure early.

A hard left hook to the liver hurt Dahlman badly in round two and opened the door for the finish. Flores followed with a sustained attack as Dahlman struggled to recover from the body shot. With Dahlman unable to halt the assault, the referee stepped in to stop the fight. The 21-year-old Flores needed fewer than two rounds to secure his tenth knockout.

Minimumweight Naomy Valle (16-1, 9 KOs) defeated Sheyla Moreno Castillo (5-2-1) by unanimous decision over eight rounds in her professional U.S. debut. The judges scored it 78-73, 78-72, and 77-74 for Valle. Valle controlled most of the early action with her jab and right hand, landing the cleaner punches as Moreno pressed forward.

A right hand in the third round hurt Moreno, but the Mexican fighter kept coming and made Valle work throughout. The final two rounds became scrappier, with Valle losing a point in the eighth for excessive holding after repeated warnings. The deduction came too late to threaten Valle’s lead, which she had built through her more accurate punching over the first six rounds.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Seeks His First World Title
Sports.content:
Floyd “Kid Austin” Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs) has the opportunity tonight to capture the WBA lightweight world title at the Wintrust Arena in Chicago, when he faces undefeated fighter “Prince” Lucas Bahdi (20-0, 15 KOs). This is what Schofield has fought his entire life for: a world title opportunity.

He started boxing at a young age with his trainer and father, Floyd Schofield Sr. He’s dedicated his entire life to boxing, and it is his lifelong dedication and commitment to the sport that he believes will be the difference tonight. Floyd has criticized Bahdi’s resume, stating he has limited experience.

Telling The Spit Bucket Podcast, “He seems like a good dude. I respect him because I see him with his kids on Instagram all the time. A fighter and a father that’s there for the kids, I’m going to respect him either way, but I think fighter to fighter like he knows he doesn’t have more skill than me.”

Bahdi came onto the big stage after his vicious knockout of Ashton “H20” Sylve on the Jake Paul-Mike Perry undercard in July of 2024. A fight Lucas was losing, being outlanded in all six rounds before scoring the knockout that ended it all.

Sylve outlanded Bahdi in every round, outlanding him 101 to 38 in total punches with H20 landing 46 percent of his power punches (Compubox). If Lucas is as reckless defensively against Schofield as he was against Sylve, it may be a very early night for him.

As for Kid Austin, he quickly stopped Tevin Farmer in his last match, ending it in 78 seconds. Schofield surprised many with his performance by being so dominant over Farmer, who was believed to be a boxer who would truly test him.

Floyd has been training extremely hard for this match, despite some minor setbacks at yesterday’s official weigh-in, having missed weight by 6 ounces on his first attempt. He was able to redeem himself on the second attempt by meeting the lightweight limit of 135 pounds.

Bahdi had no problems making weight, coming in a full pound under at 134 pounds. Lucas then took to trolling Floyd on social media by posting a video of himself on Instagram saying it was easy to make weight and then eating a donut.

Weight shouldn’t be an issue inside the ring and may actually play to Schofield’s advantage, who will seek to utilize his full set of skills of speed, power, and experience. Similar to Sylve, he’ll look to outbox Bahdi by controlling the range and overwhelm him with tactical pressure.

Given Kid Austin’s experience and overall physical attributes, he may be too much to handle for Bahdi, who may not have an answer defensively to stop Schofield’s offensive firepower.

Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Jr. Prioritizes Activity Over Opponent Quality
Sports.content:
Robert Garcia wants Vergil Ortiz Jr. back in the ring, even if that means accepting an opponent who does little to satisfy fans waiting for the Jaron Ennis fight.

Keith Thurman is the likely opponent for Ortiz’s proposed December 5 return on the David Benavidez card. Talks appear promising, though the fight has yet to be finalized. Ortiz is scheduled to begin training camp next week.

“I don’t care whatever people say. I just need Vergil back in,” Garcia said. “He’s been out for a year. … It’s going to be 13 months basically. So, that’s too much.”

That explains the willingness to take Thurman. Garcia’s priority is getting Ortiz through a training camp and into a fight. Looking for someone who offers more prestige could bring another delay, leaving Vergil inactive into next year.

Thurman would give Ortiz a recognizable opponent, but beating him would leave the bigger questions unanswered. Fans want to see Vergil against the strongest fighters around his weight. A return bout can restore activity without delivering that test.

Garcia accepts the criticism. He believes the cost of waiting has become greater than the benefit of holding out for a better opponent.

“If we try to switch up, find somebody else or maybe a bigger fight, a fight that means a little bit more, then it might take longer,” he said.

The same frustration is behind the team’s decision to campaign at 160 pounds. Garcia expects Ennis to pursue Josh Kelly and then potentially Sebastian Fundora, a sequence he believes could leave Ortiz waiting another year.

He understands Ennis’s interest in unification, while maintaining that Vergil would present a harder fight. Ortiz’s team is choosing to move forward rather than keep cutting to 154 for an opportunity Garcia cannot count on.

Getting Ortiz active is a reasonable immediate goal. After that, the urgency needs to extend to finding stronger opposition. Thurman can end the layoff; he cannot replace the fights that made fans eager to see Vergil return.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Believes He Can Break Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley believes Daniel Dubois’ decision to take a knee in their first fight revealed a weakness he could exploit again, saying that he needed to inflict enough punishment to bring it out.

Wardley pointed to the third-round knockdown, when Dubois backed up before dropping to one knee after taking an overhand right. He viewed that sequence differently from the first knockdown, where he felt his punch connected more cleanly.

“He started to kind of back up and then chose to take a knee. It was just an overhand right. It was the same one I did in the first round,” said Wardley to DAZN.

That right hand gives Wardley something more concrete to work with than questions about Dubois’ heart. Dubois has a strong jab, but Wardley described using the overhand counter to make him think twice about throwing it.

“A way to take away someone’s jab is to let them know that a shot will be coming straight behind it,” Wardley said.

If Dubois hesitates with his jab, he could give Wardley more opportunities to close the distance. The challenge for Dubois is to keep using that weapon without leaving himself open to the same right hand. Abandoning it would make it harder to control where the fight takes place.

Wardley’s interpretation of the knee is more debatable. A hurt fighter can take a count to recover without wanting out of the contest. Wardley nevertheless believes there is a point at which Dubois can be persuaded to surrender.

“I just knew I needed to do enough to bring it out. But that still wasn’t enough for me. I still needed a bit more,” said Wardley.

The practical task is reproducing the punishment that led to that moment. Wardley has identified a punch that worked and a reaction he believes he can force again. Dubois needs an answer to the counter before he can prevent Wardley from testing that theory.

Sports.title: Naoya Inoue Prepares With Bam Rodriguez In Mind
Sports.content:
Naoya Inoue says he is preparing with Jesse “Bam” Rodriguez in mind, keeping attention on a potential fight between two of boxing’s leading pound-for-pound fighters.

“Yes, I’m preparing with Jesse ‘Bam’ Rodriguez in mind,” Inoue said, according to a quote shared by Source of Boxing.

That falls short of a fight announcement, but it gives fans something more concrete than another expression of interest. Inoue is thinking about Bam as an opponent while preparing for his next appearance.

The appeal is easy to understand. Neither bantamweight nor super bantamweight has an abundance of big names, leaving these two as the obvious pairing for a fight capable of drawing attention beyond followers of the lighter divisions.

Inoue has already cleaned out the 122-pound division, collecting all four belts and beating the opponents put in front of him. Bam is working toward doing the same at 118. Bringing them together would give Inoue a fresh challenge and Rodriguez an opportunity to turn his success across the lower weights into the biggest victory of his career.

There are still questions about the timing. Inoue’s agent previously identified March 2027 as the deadline for the fight, with a move to featherweight an alternative if it cannot be arranged. That timetable predates this latest quote.

For Bam, the challenge extends beyond adding four pounds. His footwork and ability to attack from changing angles could make Inoue work harder to find his target. However, Rodriguez would need to maintain that approach against a bigger puncher who can punish him whenever he stays within range too long.

That is what makes the pairing interesting. Bam has the skill to give Inoue something different to solve, while Inoue would test whether Rodriguez’s offense remains as effective against an elite fighter at 122.

Fans have good reason to want this one. Another defense against a lesser-known challenger would be difficult to sell with Bam available. Inoue’s comments keep the possibility alive, but an agreement is still needed before anticipation becomes a date on the calendar.

Sports.title: Jack Catterall Demands His Turn Against Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall insists his title fight with Teofimo Lopez must come next, while Teofimo’s manager Keith Connolly left the outcome open with a brief response on X: “Let’s see how it all plays out.”

The comments follow FazSportz’s report that Teofimo has appealed the WBA’s September 22 order to face Catterall, seeking permission to pursue bigger fights. The October 22 negotiation deadline is approaching.

“Was awarded a voluntary title shot coming off a loss. Im next,” Catterall wrote. “I’ve got no doubts the WBA will honour what they said and agreed before I boxed Giyasov. More waiting around but it is what it is.”

Connolly’s response stopped short of promising that Catterall would get the fight. It also offered no explanation of how Teofimo’s team expects the dispute to end, leaving Catterall waiting while the champion pursues an exception.

The WBA’s published ruling supports Catterall’s account of the arrangement. When Rolando Romero was elevated to super champion at welterweight, the organization allowed him one optional defense, with the Giyasov-Catterall winner due to face him afterward. Teofimo defeated Romero on August 22 and inherited that obligation.

Teofimo’s appeal seeks permission to pursue bigger fights. That may make commercial sense for his team, but Catterall completed the route the WBA established. Allowing another opponent would mean extending his wait after the optional defense had already been used.

Catterall’s reference to Teofimo receiving a title shot coming off a loss sharpens his complaint. Teofimo received an opportunity without having to rebuild first. Catterall now wants the opportunity attached to his own win over Giyasov.

The sides have until close of business, Eastern Time, on October 22 to reach an agreement. If negotiations fail or either side withdraws, the WBA Championship Committee may order a purse bid with its president’s approval. That is a possible next step, rather than an automatic event on deadline day.

Teofimo could relinquish the belt to pursue another opponent. Keeping it while avoiding Catterall, however, would require the WBA to change the conditions it had already attached to the title.

Sports.title: Osleys Iglesias Wants Canelo Or Mbilli Winner
Sports.content:
Osleys Iglesias wants a unification against the winner of Canelo Alvarez’s October 31 fight with Christian Mbilli. Getting that fight could prove harder than defending his IBF title. Canelo has bigger commercial options, while Mbilli could be drawn into a lucrative rematch if he wins.

“I hope the winner [of Canelo-Mbilli] faces me. I’d like my next fight to be a unification,” Iglesias said after stopping Oliver Zaren in Quebec on Thursday.

The seventh-round stoppage lifted Iglesias to 16-0 with 15 knockouts. Those numbers help explain the difficulty of finding a willing opponent. He brings a world title, southpaw skills and heavy power, but lacks the name recognition that would turn a Canelo fight into a major event.

Canelo would be risking more than another points defeat. Iglesias has the power to hurt him and force a punishing fight, with a stoppage a serious possibility. Another belt might not be enough compensation when better-known opponents could offer more money and a better chance of winning.

Hamzah Sheeraz and Chris Eubank Jr. would give Canelo fresh opponents with British interest behind them. Neither is a guaranteed victory, but his team could view both as less dangerous choices than Iglesias.

Canelo also has a remaining fight under his agreement with Turki Alalshikh’s boxing operation. What Alalshikh wants to fund will influence the selection, leaving Iglesias competing against names that could sell a bigger show.

Mbilli appears more likely to accept a unification, but beating Canelo could change his immediate plans. A rematch would be difficult to turn down financially, provided Canelo wanted another attempt. His defeats against Floyd Mayweather and Dmitry Bivol did not produce second meetings.

If Canelo moves on, Mbilli against Iglesias would offer plenty in the ring. Mbilli’s relentless pressure would test the Cuban, while also bringing him within range of dangerous southpaw counters.

That is Iglesias’ best opening. A Canelo victory could leave him making another defense while the Mexican pursues a more profitable opponent.

Sports.title: Amir Khan Rules Out December Manny Pacquiao Fight
Sports.content:
Amir Khan is interested in facing Manny Pacquiao, but says he would not be ready for December 11. His admission leaves the proposed comeback dependent on more than agreeing on a payday, with the former light welterweight champion approaching five years out of the ring.

“That’s a rumor,” Khan told Metro about appearing on the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua undercard. “Even if it was for that fight night, I wouldn’t be ready for it, and I don’t think Manny would be either. “We’ve both been traveling, and we’re obviously not back in camp. It’s only about nine weeks away. I don’t know where that came from.”

Khan says talks are taking place and that he is happy with the money and location discussed. That establishes interest, but no signed fight or date has been announced.

The preparation question is particularly significant for Khan. He has not fought since Kell Brook stopped him in February 2022, and his last victory over a leading opponent came against Chris Algieri in 2015.

A longer camp could help Khan recover his conditioning. Whether he can regain the timing and reactions needed against Pacquiao is harder to judge. His best boxing depended on fast combinations and getting out before opponents could answer. Returning after years away would test both parts of that approach.

Pacquiao has been inactive too, but his July 2025 draw with Mario Barrios provides more recent evidence that he can compete over 12 rounds. Khan would enter negotiations without a comparable performance to point to since his retirement.

That difference makes a return fight worth considering before Khan commits to Pacquiao. Sparring can help him prepare, but an actual bout would offer a clearer picture of what remains.

Khan has always wanted the matchup, and the proposed terms appear attractive. His decision to dismiss December is sensible. The next question is whether additional time produces a prepared fighter or simply delays a difficult comeback.

Adding Pacquiao against Khan, who hasn’t fought since Brook stopped him in 2022, would turn the Cardiff card into an expensive nostalgia show. Fury–Joshua is already years overdue, and the proposed Jai Opetaia–Deontay Wilder fight features a faded former champion who turns 41 before December 11. Another pairing built around aging stars would leave the event trading heavily on what these fighters used to be.

Ghana News.title: Power restoration fault suspected in Kumasi Central Market fire
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana National Fire Service is investigating a suspected power-restoration fault as a possible trigger for a fire that swept through part of the Kumasi Central Market near the Aboabo station.

Ashanti Regional Fire Commander ACFO I Peter Tetteh said preliminary eyewitness accounts indicated that the fire started shortly after electricity returned following a brief outage.

He disclosed this during an inspection of the fire-ravaged area with the Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, Ashanti Regional Minister Dr Frank Amoakohene and Kumasi Mayor Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi.

“From what we heard, eyewitnesses said there was a light out. In three minutes, the light came back on, and that is when they saw the fire,” he said.

The account has not yet been established as the definitive cause of the outbreak, with investigations still ongoing.

Mr Tetteh said traders who had received basic fire safety training attempted to put out the initial flames using portable fire extinguishers before firefighters arrived.

Their efforts, however, were overtaken by the rapid spread of the fire.

He said the first fire appliance from Asokore Mampong arrived at the scene at 8:39 pm, after which crews established containment lines to prevent the flames from spreading to other sections of the market.

A total of five appliances were deployed, comprising four fire tenders and one water tanker.

“We didn't have a problem with water at all yesterday,” Mr Tetteh said, indicating that water supply was not a constraint during the operation.

Despite the available water supply and police presence, the Fire Commander said congestion and obstructions caused by traders trying to retrieve their belongings made it difficult for crews to manoeuvre around the market.

He said the conditions complicated efforts to access affected areas and contain the blaze.

“There were a lot of obstructions yesterday. Even the police were here, but it was very, very difficult over here,” he said.

Investigations into the precise cause of the fire and assessments of the total financial losses are continuing.

Ghana News.title: The 7-foot giant of Ngleshie Amanfro: Seven-foot Ghanaian Ephraim Saawa dreams of joining the national basketball team
Ghana News.content:
In Ngleshie Amanfro, a bustling community in the Ga South Municipality, you don't need to know his name to know him.

You just look up.

At 7.0 feet tall, Ephraim Sincero Ma-c Saawa is impossible to miss.

Trotro mates call him to the front seat. Children stop and stare. Adults pull out their phones for a quick picture.

Strangers on the streets from Amanfro through to Kasoa stop him to ask the same question: "How tall are you?" For many, that attention would be a burden.

For Ephraim, it could be a destiny he cannot do away with.

The young Senior High School graduate wants to turn the curious looks into cheers in a basketball arena.

His ultimate dream is simple but audacious: to wear the red, gold and green of Ghana, step onto the international basketball court, and bring home a trophy for his country. "I want to join Ghana's national basketball team, compete in international tournaments and help win a trophy for the country," he told MyJoyOnline in an interview that captures both his humility and his hunger.

Ephraim is not yet a household name in Ghanaian sports. He has no national caps, no league titles, no endorsement deals. But in Ngleshie Amanfro, he is already a local celebrity — the towering pride of the community whose physical gift many believe could become Ghana's sporting advantage.

He comes from Nandom Piina in the Upper West Region, but his story is taking shape in Greater Accra.

He completed Abakrampa Senior High School in 2025 in the Central Region, where he studied Business.

While his mates were focused on football — the default passion in almost every Ghanaian second cycle school — Ephraim's eyes were on the basket.

It was not always basketball. At basic school, he was a volleyball player. His height made him natural at the net. But by the time he got to Senior High School, his heart had switched courts. "By the time I reached senior high school, my dream was to play basketball rather than volleyball," he recalled.

The problem was that his school had no basketball court.

While Abakrampa SHS chalked up successes in athletics and football, basketball was a sport played in his imagination and wherever he could find students from other schools to train with. "First, I need to learn to play basketball very well.

That way, if I get the opportunity to join the national team, I will be able to perform well and help the team," he said — a statement that shows he understands that height alone does not make a baller.

That structured learning has now begun. For the past two months, Ephraim has been training with the Magic Basket Ball Academy, based at Tudu close to the Accra Technical University.

The opportunity came through his father, who refused to let his son's potential go to waste. “My father took me to meet the coach and spoke to him about training me," he explained.

At Magic, he is learning to convert his natural attributes the long legs that power high vertical jumps for rebounds, the long strides that allow quick first steps for drives to the basket into real basketball Footwork, positioning, shooting, and defending. His role model is no surprise:

French phenomenon Victor Wembanyama, the 7-foot-4-inch NBA superstar who has redefined what a big man can do.

Ephraim does not just admire Wembanyama's height; he admires how he uses it."I admire how he plays, especially his defensive skills.

That is why he is my role model," he said. He points to Wembanyama's shot-blocking, his rebounding dominance, and his selfless support for teammates as the blueprint he wants to follow.

So strong is his admiration that he openly appeals for a chance to meet Wembanyama one day, mentioning Ghanaian businessman Ibrahim Mahama as someone he hopes could help make that dream encounter possible.

For now, he is willing to join any professional team that will give him a chance to learn, to grow, and to contribute to winning tournaments and league titles. A Celebrity Without Trying.

His challenge is how to get good training kits.

Away from the court, Ephraim's life is a lesson in living tall literally and figuratively — in a world built for average height.

He says the fascination with his height started as early as basic school. Teachers and pupils alike were amazed. At Abakrampa SHS, he was officially the tallest student on campus.

Today, a simple walk to buy something in Ngleshie Amanfro becomes a meet-and-greet."Some people laugh, while others are surprised.

Some approach me to take pictures or ask for my phone number, and we become friends," he said with a smile. Many in the community now call him the tallest boy in Accra, but he is quick to deflect the title with disarming humility. “I cannot say that because I have not seen everyone in Accra. I believe there may be people who are taller than me," he said.

But the fame has its frustrations, especially with transportation.

Ghana's ubiquitous trotros were not designed with 7-foot passengers in mind. “If I sit at the back, I sometimes experience leg pain by the time I reach my destination. That is why I usually sit in front," he explained.

It has become a daily negotiation.

If the front seat is taken, he politely asks the driver's mate to intervene and explain his condition to the occupant.

Some passengers understand and swap seats.

Others refuse, and Ephraim simply waits for the next car.

He wants public transport to be more accommodating and for drivers and mates to be more empathetic for people like him and others.

"They should explain our difficulties to other passengers so that people understand why sitting at the back can be uncomfortable for us," he appealed. Beyond The Court: Coding And Community.

What makes Ephraim's story compelling is that basketball is only one half of his ambition. While he works at a printing press in Ngleshie Amanfro to make ends meet, he is preparing to pursue university education in Computer Science. He wants to become a software engineer. His motivation is not just personal advancement. He is worried about how young Ghanaians are using technology. He says he has seen many students rely completely on Artificial Intelligence to do assignments without actually learning. “I would like to create software that helps children and young people understand the world better and respond to what is happening around them," he said. He also dreams of establishing small businesses to support himself and his family.

More importantly, he wants to turn his visibility into a vehicle for positive change. In a community where many young people are at risk of falling into gangs and social vices, he believes his towering presence can carry a towering message. "I would like to encourage them to focus on their lives and their future rather than engage in social vices," he said.

From the streets of Amanfro where he is stopped for selfies, to the dusty court at Tudu where he is learning to block and rebound, to the printing press where he works and the future computer lab where he hopes to code, Ephraim Sincero Ma-c Saawa is walking — tall — towards two futures at once.

One is in Silicon Valley-inspired dreams of software that educates Ghanaian children. The other is in a Ghana jersey, hearing the national anthem before a big game, ready to jump for the opening tip-off.

For Ghana basketball, which has long searched for its next big man to compete with Nigeria, Senegal and Angola on the continent, the giant of Ngleshie Amanfro might just be worth a look.

Ghana News.title: Government promises support for Kumasi Central Market fire victims
Ghana News.content:
The government has assured traders affected by a fire at Kumasi Central Market of possible state support, with the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) expected to assess the damage and determine the assistance required.

Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs Mahama Ayariga gave the assurance during an emergency visit to the scene with Ashanti Regional Minister Dr Frank Amoakohene and Kumasi Mayor Richard Ofori Agyemang Boadi.

The visit followed a directive from the President to assess the situation after the blaze destroyed 15 shops before being contained by firefighters.

Addressing affected traders, Mr Ayariga conveyed the President’s sympathies and said the government would consider available options to help them recover from their losses.

“We will put our heads together to see how we can lift you out of this unfortunate situation,” he said.

“When we get the report from NADMO, we will explore every opportunity that exists to support the victims.”

Mr Ayariga said the government, in coordination with the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA), had agreed to allow affected shop owners to temporarily restore their trading spaces ahead of the Christmas season, provided the areas meet structural safety requirements.

KMA engineers are to conduct urgent structural integrity tests on the affected sections before traders can return to their shops.

The assessment is expected to help determine whether the affected spaces can safely accommodate trading activities while relief arrangements are considered.

The Minister also announced that construction works on Phase Two of the Kejetia Market project, which have stalled, would resume shortly.

He said the project was intended to help address market congestion, although no specific date for the resumption was provided in the statement.

The proposed restart comes as traders and authorities assess the impact of the latest fire and consider measures to restore affected businesses ahead of the busy Christmas trading period.

Ghana News.title: Vibes The Movie: Big Ghun’s Ghanaian film earns five nominations at 2026 REFFA
Ghana News.content:
Ghanaian filmmaker Nicholas “Big Ghun” Nartey’s Vibes The Movie has secured five nominations at the 2026 Regal Film Festival and Awards (REFFA), adding to the film’s growing list of international recognitions.

The PB Studios Africa production has been nominated for Best Comedy Film, Best Ghanaian Film, Best Debut Film, Achievement in Sound and Achievement in Soundtrack.

The nominations were announced at an event at the Accra Marriott Hotel on Friday, October 9, 2026. Ghana’s National Film Authority had publicised the event as an unveiling of nominees celebrating African stories, talent and creativity.

Nartey is identified alongside the film in the Best Debut Film, Achievement in Sound and Achievement in Soundtrack categories.

The nominations recognise different aspects of the production, from its comic storytelling and Ghanaian identity to its music and sound. The recognition for sound and soundtrack also highlights the film’s musical dimension.

Written and directed by Big Ghun, Vibes The Movie follows two friends whose attempts to escape poorly paid and humiliating jobs lead them into a series of unpredictable business ventures.

Blending comedy, rap and emotional drama, the film explores friendship, ambition and the pressures of trying to build a better life.

Big Ghun and Jeffrey Nortey lead the cast, which also features Clemento Suarez, Aaron Adatsi, Feli Nuna, Giovani Caleb and Krymi Music, alongside other actors and personalities.

Produced by PB Studios Africa, the film expands the world of Obolo Tui and Lil Pui into a feature-length story rooted in Ghanaian life.

The REFFA nominations follow an eventful year for the production. Vibes The Movie received an Outstanding Achievement Award at the February 2026 session of the American Motion Pictures Festival and later won Best Comic Film at the 2026 Ghana Comedy Awards.

The film was also nominated for Best African Film and Best Ghallywood Film at the 2026 Toronto International Nollywood Film Festival in Canada.

Its latest recognition comes days after news of its availability on Amazon Prime Video in the United States and the United Kingdom. The release gives Ghanaian audiences abroad and other international viewers another way to watch the film, with a wider rollout expected, according to the production team.

REFFA celebrates filmmaking across Africa and the diaspora through awards, screenings, industry discussions and opportunities for creative exchange. Its 2026 theme, “Reimagining Africa: Stories beyond Borders,” centres on connecting African stories with wider audiences.

The five nominations add to the film’s record of awards and festival recognition as Big Ghun and PB Studios Africa seek to expand its reach beyond Ghana.

Ghana News.title: MamaCare CEO warns unresolved conflicts among health workers could undermine maternal and neonatal care
Ghana News.content:
Maternal and Child Health Expert and Chief Executive Officer of MamaCare by Racheal, Mrs Racheal Hesse Matey, has warned that unresolved conflicts among obstetric care providers can undermine teamwork and compromise care for pregnant women and newborns.

Speaking at the Annual Health Conference at the Korle-Bu Nursing and Midwifery Training College, she said disagreements among health workers and failure to follow agreed clinical protocols could lead to misdiagnosis, inappropriate interventions and poor coordination.

“Sometimes, if there is conflict among the internal people and it is not resolved, the protocols that are supposed to guide us are not followed. This person is saying this, that person is saying that, and we are not coming to one agreement,” she said.

Mrs Hesse Matey said tensions among staff working the same shift could affect patient care, urging health facilities and training institutions to prioritise teamwork, communication and prompt conflict resolution.

She also called on midwives to continually improve their professional knowledge and skills to meet the expectations of increasingly informed patients.

She noted that many women research pregnancy and childbirth throughout their pregnancies, making it important for health professionals to have the knowledge and competence required to provide appropriate care.

“Before they come to the hospital, they know the condition they are going through. Right from pregnancy, the woman is already reading about what is happening from week to week, month to month. So she is well informed,” she said.

“And if you don't have the knowledge to care for your patients, then we are talking about maternal mortality.”

Mrs Hesse Matey further stressed that quality healthcare should not depend on a patient’s social background, financial status or appearance, insisting that every patient deserves appropriate and respectful care.

She also cautioned midwives and trainees against excessive mobile phone and social media use while on duty, stressing the importance of remaining attentive to patients.

Her remarks formed part of discussions at the conference on maternal and neonatal mortality, with an emphasis on the role of clinical competence, professional conduct and teamwork in improving outcomes for mothers and newborns.

Ghana News.title: Health professionals urged to translate medical knowledge into practice to save mothers
Ghana News.content:
Obstetrician-gynaecologist Dr Elikem Oklu has raised concerns about the continued loss of mothers and newborns to preventable causes, saying gaps between medical knowledge and clinical practice remain a challenge in Ghana’s healthcare system.

Speaking at an annual health conference at the Korle Bu Nursing and Midwifery Training College, he questioned why maternal and neonatal deaths persist despite the availability of medical expertise, drugs and health facilities.

“Why are women still dying in the midst of all this knowledge? It's because for most of us, we do not make a connection between what we know and what we do,” Dr Oklu said.

His comments come as Ghana continues to grapple with maternal mortality and concerns about the quality of care provided to pregnant women and nursing mothers.

Figures from the Ministry of Health put Ghana’s maternal mortality ratio at approximately 234 deaths per 100,000 live births, while institutional maternal deaths stood at 965 in 2025.

Dr Oklu said improving outcomes requires health professionals to apply their training consistently, particularly when responding to emergencies.

He also highlighted the importance of attitude and institutional culture, noting that empathy and communication can make a difference even when treatment does not result in a positive outcome.

He urged health workers to communicate openly on the wards, make appropriate referrals and renew their commitment to professional duty.

University of Ghana School of Law lecturer Rachel Haizel has meanwhile argued that medical facilities and health professionals are not sued often enough over alleged medical negligence.

She said limited litigation could weaken accountability for poor professional conduct in some health facilities.

“We are not suing them enough. If you see the kind of treatment that some of these health practitioners give to their patients, it's horrible,” she said.

Ms Haizel stressed that healthcare professionals owe patients a duty of care and must exercise reasonable care and skill in line with the standards expected of their profession.

The concerns raised at the conference place renewed attention on clinical practice, patient safety and accountability as Ghana works to reduce preventable maternal and neonatal deaths.

Ghana News.title: Conflicts among care providers linked to maternal, neonatal deaths – Expert
Ghana News.content:
Maternal and child health expert and Chief Executive Officer of MamaCare by Racheal, Mrs Racheal Hesse Matey, has warned that unresolved conflicts among obstetric care providers are indirectly contributing to maternal and neonatal deaths.

Speaking at the Annual Health Conference on Maternal and Neonatal Mortality at the Korle-Bu Nursing and Midwifery Training College, she explained that internal disagreements and failure to adhere to agreed protocols among caregivers on duty could result in misdiagnosis, inappropriate interventions and poor coordination, with patients bearing the consequences.

“Sometimes, if there is conflict among the internal people and it is not resolved, the protocols that are supposed to guide us are not followed. This person is saying this, that person is saying that, and we are not coming to one agreement,” she said.

She explained that when staff working the same shift are not on good terms, patient care suffers, stressing that interpersonal conflicts must be resolved promptly.

She therefore called on health facilities and training institutions to prioritise teamwork, communication and conflict resolution as part of efforts to reduce preventable maternal deaths.

Mrs Hesse Matey also underscored the need for midwives to strengthen their professional knowledge and skills to meet the expectations of increasingly informed patients.

“Before they come to the hospital, they know the condition they are going through. Right from pregnancy, the woman is already reading about what is happening from week to week, month to month. So she is well informed. She is even reading about what is going to happen in labour,” she said.

“And if you don't have the knowledge to care for your patients, then we are talking about maternal mortality,” she added.

She further stressed the need for equitable healthcare delivery, insisting that every patient deserves quality care regardless of their social background, financial status, or appearance.

Mrs Hesse Matey also cautioned trainees against excessive use of mobile phones and social media while on duty, stressing that every moment spent with a patient counts.

Ghana News.title: GIS marks 10th TIME conference, champions improved teaching practices
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana International School (GIS) has marked the 10th anniversary of its TIME Educators’ Conference, an initiative aimed at strengthening teaching practices and improving learning outcomes.

Held on Saturday, October 10, 2026, at the GIS Secondary School campus in Cantonments, Accra, the conference was organised under the theme, “10 Years of Impact: Transforming Education, One Teacher at a TIME.”

TIME stands for Transform, Inspire, Motivate and Educate. The initiative brings educators together to share practical teaching methods, exchange ideas and strengthen their professional skills.

Delivering the keynote address, founding dean of the University of Ghana’s School of Education and Leadership, Professor Jonathan Fletcher, highlighted improvements in teaching standards over the past decade.

“In 2017, when we developed National Teachers’ Standards, at that time I could not say that more than 10% of teachers could actually teach to those standards. At least 68% of our teachers can do that,” he said.

Professor Fletcher credited the conference with helping to spread improved teaching practices across the country.

“The idea of TIME is a great thing… the way teaching is done in this school is being propagated and so gradually teachers in this institution are actually infecting, as it were, teachers in this country,” he said.

On the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI), Professor Fletcher described it as a valuable tool for teaching and learning but stressed the need for ethical use and academic integrity.

He said educators must ensure that learners understand work produced with AI rather than simply presenting it as their own.

The Principal and Head of School at GIS, Nadia O. Bruce-Müller, said the conference began in October 2016 as an in-house initiative designed to give teachers an opportunity to learn from one another.

She explained that the initiative was created partly because not every teacher could travel abroad to attend professional development conferences.

The conference started with about 30 presenters from GIS but has since grown to attract more than 1,000 participants and nearly 100 presenters, including educators from other parts of Ghana and abroad. This year’s programme also featured two senior student presenters.

Mrs Bruce-Müller said the changing needs of learners and developments in education make continuous professional development essential.

“Our students are changing; the educational landscape ecosystem is changing. We can’t do it the same way we used to do it,” she said.

She explained that the theme, “Transforming Education, One Teacher at a TIME,” reflects the belief that every teacher can take at least one practical lesson from the conference back to the classroom and use it to improve learning.

GIS also provides about 100 to 200 free registrations or sponsored places for teachers from public and private schools to participate in the annual conference.

The 10th edition reaffirmed the conference’s focus on lifelong learning, collaboration and the adoption of effective teaching methods to meet the changing demands of education.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Ebola spreads in eastern DRC as Kenya confirms imported case
World.content:
New cases in eastern DRC and a fatal imported infection in Kenya highlight the challenges of containing Ebola.

Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo – The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has spread to another health zone in the east, while a fatal imported case in Kenya has underscored the risk of cross-border transmission.

The World Health Organization (WHO) said in an October 8 update that Alimbongo health zone in North Kivu province had reported cases for the first time. As of October 6, four confirmed cases, including two deaths, had been recorded there.

The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a species of Ebola virus. According to the WHO, cases had been reported in 64 health zones across seven provinces in the DRC. Ituri remained the worst-affected province in cumulative cases, while North Kivu was accounting for a growing share of newly confirmed infections.

As of October 6, the WHO had recorded 8,728 confirmed cases and 4,205 confirmed deaths in the DRC. A further 2,269 people had recovered, and the crude case fatality ratio stood at 48.2 percent.

Kenya confirms imported case

Kenya confirmed its first imported case of Bundibugyo virus disease on October 6, according to the WHO. The patient, a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the DRC, fell ill there and received treatment at several health facilities before travelling to Kenya through Uganda.

The patient travelled by road to Kampala, Uganda, before flying to Nairobi, arriving on October 3. The patient was isolated in hospital and tested positive for the virus. Despite supportive treatment, the patient died on October 5, the WHO said.



Kenyan authorities identified 28 contacts, including family members and healthcare workers. The WHO also reported efforts to trace passengers and crew members from the flight to Nairobi.

Public health measures have been initiated in Kenya and Uganda, including contact tracing and enhanced surveillance.

On October 8, preliminary laboratory results for a suspected Ebola case in Kenya’s Wajir County came back negative, according to the county governor. The result eased concerns about a possible second case, although monitoring continued.

The imported infection has underscored the importance of surveillance and coordination between neighbouring countries. Identifying exposed people and monitoring them for symptoms are central to detecting infections early and interrupting further transmission.

Treatment capacity under pressure

In the DRC, the response is facing mounting pressure from limited treatment capacity, insecurity and difficulties securing cooperation from some communities.

Daniel Makasi Levergénois, founder of Watoto Radio, said insecurity and misinformation were undermining efforts to contain the outbreak. In Beni and Butembo, both in North Kivu, rumours and misconceptions about Ebola had contributed to reluctance among some residents to cooperate with response teams, he said.

In an October 5 update, medical charity Doctors Without Borders, known by its French initials MSF, said North Kivu accounted for nearly 40 percent of newly confirmed cases nationwide, up from 24 percent at the end of August.

MSF also reported that, as of September 28, 34 percent of confirmed Ebola patients were being treated in non-specialised health facilities. Dedicated treatment centres lacked sufficient beds, while delays in diagnosis meant some patients were being treated outside facilities equipped to manage Ebola.

The organisation warned that many of these facilities lacked the resources and expertise needed to manage the disease, increasing the risk of transmission among patients and healthcare workers.

“For weeks, treatment capacity has stretched to its limit,” said Stephanie Hoffmann, coordinator of MSF’s Ebola treatment centre in Butembo.

“Because there are not enough beds available, we are sometimes forced to refer confirmed Ebola patients elsewhere, despite the significant risk this poses to the wider community. In addition, standards of care in some peripheral facilities do not always meet the requirements for Ebola treatment. This is extremely concerning.”



Mistrust threatens containment efforts

Alberto Lusenge, a community leader in Beni, said the failure to stop transmission early in Ituri province, followed by new cases and attacks on response workers in Beni and Butembo, had deepened public concern.

Lusenge warned that mistrust could discourage residents from reporting symptoms or cooperating with health workers. He said North Kivu could become a greater focus of the outbreak if authorities failed to secure stronger cooperation from local communities.

The WHO said response teams were following up 23,741 of the 29,535 identified contacts as of October 4, equivalent to 80.4 percent – below the response target of at least 85 percent.

Contact tracing allows health authorities to identify people who may have been exposed, monitor them for symptoms and detect infections early. Gaps in follow-up can make it harder to identify and interrupt chains of transmission.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has called for a community-centred response, including active case finding, systematic contact tracing, daily follow-up of exposed people and sustained engagement with local communities.

A history of deadly outbreaks

The DRC’s 2018–2020 Ebola outbreak, caused by a different virus species, killed nearly 2,300 people. The current outbreak presents distinct challenges: According to the WHO, there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for Bundibugyo virus disease.

Early detection, supportive care and infection prevention therefore remain central to the response. But as infections spread into additional health zones and treatment facilities struggle to accommodate patients, health authorities face the dual challenge of containing transmission and maintaining public trust.

Jean Kaseya, director-general of Africa CDC, has stressed the importance of rapidly identifying and monitoring people exposed to the virus.

“To bring this outbreak under control, we need to know where every contact is, track them and quickly identify anyone showing symptoms before they pass the virus on to their family, their community or across borders. We will only bring this outbreak under control once the last chain of transmission has been broken,” Kaseya said in a news release seen by Al Jazeera.
