World.title: Liverpool vs Man City: the top five clashes between Premier League giants
World.content:
Liverpool face Manchester City on Sunday in what has become a battle between the dominant EPL teams of recent times.

Share What are the top five clashes between Liverpool and Manchester City? on social media

The rivalry between Manchester City and Liverpool will be renewed when they meet in Sunday’s supercharged Premier League clash at Anfield.

History suggests Liverpool are often favourites in this fixture, but recent form heavily favours the Manchester club.

City, who have dominated headlines in recent weeks over serious financial breach charges, lead the league’s points table with 15 points – six ahead of Liverpool, who are sixth in the standings.

Sunday’s match will be the 202nd fixture between the teams across all competitions, with Liverpool firmly leading the head-to-head with 95 victories, while City have won 53 matches with 53 drawn.

As Enzo Maresca faces off with Andoni Iraola this weekend, Al Jazeera looks back at the top five clashes over the years:

Liverpool 4-3 Manchester City (January 14, 2018 – Premier League)

Our list begins with this seven-goal league thriller from eight years ago.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain gave Liverpool an early lead that night at Anfield before Roberto Firmino, Sadio Mane and Mohamed Salah scored in a rousing eight-minute spell in the second half to build a staggering 4-1 lead.

But Man City struck twice in the final six minutes through Bernardo Silva and Ilkay Gundogan, forcing Liverpool to hold on for a nervous finish.

That result not only strengthened Liverpool’s top-four bid but also ended City’s unbeaten run that season.

Nonetheless, City went on to lift the title that term with a record-breaking 100 points, while Liverpool came fourth.

Liverpool 3-2 Manchester City (April 13, 2014 – Premier League)

This game goes further back in history and it’s another laden with goals.



On the 25th anniversary of the Hillsborough disaster when 97 Liverpool supporters died, a 10-man Liverpool side beat City 3-2 in a dramatic title-race clash.

Early goals by Raheem Sterling and Martin Skrtel put Liverpool in control, but City fought back through David Silva and a Glen Johnson own goal before Philippe Coutinho struck the winner for Liverpool 12 minutes from time.

Coutinho pounced on a loose clearance by City’s Vincent Kompany in the box, drilling the ball into the bottom corner as Anfield went wild for the ‘Little Magician’.

The victory marked a huge step towards Liverpool’s title charge, but ultimately it was City who won the league that season, finishing two points ahead of the Merseyside club.

Manchester City 2-1 Liverpool (January 3, 2019 – Premier League)

The next game on our list sees City on the winning side.

Sergio Aguero had given City the lead with his first-half strike before Firmino equalised four minutes from the hour -mark.

But Leroy Sane won the three vital points for the hosts, scoring the winner in the 72nd minute.

After a quick counterattack, Sterling picked out the onrushing Sane on the left side, just outside the box, before the German’s left-footed shot hit the inside of the post and the ball rolled into the bottom corner.

With that, Liverpool suffered their first loss of the season, ending a 20-game unbeaten streak.

City also went on to reduce Liverpool’s lead at the top to four points and eventually lifted the trophy, beating the Reds by just one point.

Liverpool 3-1 Manchester City (November 10, 2019 – Premier League)

This match goes back to the season that was the first to be affected by the COVID-19 pandemic.

Goals from Fabinho, Salah and Mane guided the Reds to a hugely impressive 3-1 home win over the title holders.

The match is best remembered by Liverpool fans for Fabinho’s stunning goal, as the Brazilian launched the ball into the net from about 25 yards (23 metres) out.

The result also opened up an eight-point lead at the top of the table and went down as a defining moment in Liverpool’s campaign as they ended their 30-year quest to win the league.

That season, Liverpool finished with 99 points, a whopping 18 points ahead of second-placed City.

Liverpool 3-0 Manchester City (April 4, 2018 – Champions League quarterfinal, first leg)

Our top five list ends with a Champions League clash.



Liverpool fired three goals in the opening half-hour, ripping through their opponents in the first leg of this UCL quarterfinal clash.

Once again, Salah, Mane and Oxlade-Chamberlain were among the scorers as Liverpool took control of the knockout tie.

Oxlade-Chamberlain’s fierce finish – a thundering strike from outside the box – was the highlight of this fixture.

Liverpool went on to reach the final, where they fell to Real Madrid.

World.title: WHO says no plague case registered after Russian lab worker’s death
World.content:
The WHO says the lack of a confirmed diagnosis remains a key uncertainty, with no sign of ongoing transmission.

Share WHO says no plague case registered after Russian lab worker’s death on social media

The World Health Organization (WHO) has said it still does not know what caused the pneumonia that killed a laboratory worker at a Russian plague research institute and that no case of plague has been registered.

Russia’s state health regulator told the WHO that tests on the worker and people who had been in contact with her were negative for the dangerous pathogens they tested for, the United Nations health agency said in a statement on Saturday.

Her contacts still showed no symptoms, and no further linked cases of severe pneumonia had been found, the WHO added.

“Based on the information provided… WHO has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission associated with this event. A key uncertainty remains the absence of a confirmed diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker,” it said.

What happened?

The worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on October 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and stoking public health fears on social media.

Russian media named her as Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old laboratory technician at the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, in the Siberian region of Irkutsk.

Pneumonic plague, a lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, which is usually found in small mammals and their fleas, was suspected early on.

The governor of neighbouring Buryatia said the woman had “died, maybe of the plague”.

Russia’s health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said she had been diagnosed with “pneumonia of unknown aetiology”.



Russian authorities said the worker was appropriately vaccinated and that no microorganisms linked to her work were found in her body. They say post-mortem tests did not detect plague.

On Thursday, Russia said it had completed health checks on all her contacts and had given the WHO all the information.

A local official said on October 6 that 60 percent of those placed in quarantine had already been released.

WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus asked Russia on Wednesday to respond to media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause. Russia dismissed the reports as “false information”.

The United States has also called on Russia for transparency.

Global health officials have been extra alert to deadly pneumonia cases of unknown cause since the COVID-19 pandemic, which began with a cluster of fast-spreading, fatal respiratory illness in China.

The cause of individual pneumonia cases often cannot be determined.

World.title: Yemeni government’s military says its forces advancing against Houthis
World.content:
Saudi-backed forces say 1,150 Houthis killed in operations against the Iran-aligned group over the past 24 hours.

Share Yemeni government’s military says its forces advancing against Houthis on social media

How much worse can Yemen's humanitarian crisis become?

The military of Yemen’s internationally recognised government says it has killed hundreds of Houthi fighters in targeted operations over the past 24 hours.

Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili, the spokesman for Yemeni government forces, said at least 1,150 Houthis were killed in almost 2,000 targeted operations across the country as part of operation “Dawn of Yemen”.

He said the army had destroyed Houthi ammunition dumps and at least 180 combat, transport and supply vehicles operated by the Houthis, adding that ground forces “continued to advance their assault”.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the information.

An attack on King Khalid International airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh, on Saturday killed and injured several people and led to flights being cancelled.

When asked if the United States would join strikes against the Houthis after the attack, President Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that he “will make a decision soon”.

Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from Yemen on Saturday, said the Houthis had yet to claim responsibility for the latest attack.

But the Iran-backed group has warned aviation companies to avoid using Saudi airspace, saying any aircraft operating there – except over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina – is a target.

Mawry said the Houthis were preparing to fight the war on multiple fronts, including against the participation of international actors, such as Pakistan.

“The Houthis say that if Pakistan engages in any military activities against them on behalf of Saudi Arabia, then they will be treated in the same fashion as the Saudis are currently being dealt with,” Mawry said.



There are plans to launch ballistic missiles towards Pakistan and attack Pakistan-flagged vessels in the Red and Arabian seas, he added.

“The fighting is spreading on multiple fronts, but it is a situation that will keep escalating,” Baraa Shiban, an associate fellow in international security and Yemen expert at the London-based Royal United Services Institute think tank, told Al Jazeera, adding that the violence will not be “dying down” anytime soon.

“There is no mediation happening this time – there [are] no regional or local mediators that are able to cool down the situation,” he said.

The Saudi-backed Yemeni forces are advancing on the Houthis in a bid to recapture areas around the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a critical trade route for global shipping into and out of the Red Sea.

Battles are now raging around the strategic southern Yemeni cities of Mocha and Dhubab, which are on the Red Sea coast and strategically important for control of Bab al-Mandeb.

The Houthis, who have controlled Sanaa and parts of northwestern Yemen since 2014, seized the area in September, effectively taking control of the strait, although both sides claim control of the shipping lanes.

World.title: Real Madrid beat Villarreal 1-0 but Vinicius sent off for hair pull
World.content:
Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior sent off for pulling Villarreal player’s hair in 1-0 La Liga victory.

Share Real Madrid beat Villarreal 1-0 but Vinicius sent off for hair pull on social media

Yan Diomande earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinicius Junior was sent off for hair-pulling.

Brazil international Vinicius, on as a substitute, scored, but his goal was disallowed. He was then dismissed after a VAR review showed he had pulled the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba.

Jose Mourinho’s Madrid battled through the final stages with 10 men but held on to win and go provisionally third.

Champions Barca lead La Liga after a 3-0 win over Getafe, while Atletico Madrid are five points behind in second after they edged Alaves 2-1.

Striker Kylian Mbappe was fit to start the match for Madrid at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break.

There was a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from other supporters.

Mbappe, a candidate for the Ballon d’Or trophy later this month, was Madrid’s most threatening player in the first half, although he had little competition.

Mourinho started with out-of-form winger Vinicius on the bench, following his trips to Australia and India with Brazil during the international break.

Madrid improved defensively, giving Villarreal few chances of note, but struggled to build much in attack themselves in a drab opening half.

Mbappe struck the post from Alvaro Carreras’s layoff as Madrid pushed Villarreal back early on.



Villarreal soon gained a foothold and restricted Madrid’s opportunities, until Mbappe forced a good save from Peter Gulacsi.

There was some more mild whistling for Madrid’s display from their fans at half-time, but they were soon able to celebrate summer arrival Diomande’s first goal for the club.

The Ivorian winger, Madrid’s record 140 million euro ($157m) signing, produced a sharp low finish into the far corner after good work from Federico Valverde to play him in.

Vinicius thought he had doubled Madrid’s lead after Jude Bellingham charged in down the left and cut the ball back for him.

However, the winger’s joy turned to anger after referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was called to watch Vinicius’s hair pull on Saliba in the buildup by VAR and sent off the Brazilian, voiding the goal.

Madrid’s Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who had made a couple of smart saves earlier in the half, produced an acrobatic stop to thwart Carlos Romero.

Mbappe was denied again by Hungarian goalkeeper Gulasci as the forward left the Bernabeu frustrated in his hunt for goals, although his team were able to clinch three important points to stay on Barca’s trail.

World.title: Hundreds of doctors demand World Medical Association suspend Israel
World.content:
Hundreds of doctors have gathered outside the World Medical Association (WMA) summit in the Netherlands, calling for the suspension of the Israeli Medical Association (IMA) from the grouping of physicians.

On Saturday, 81 healthcare workers removed their scrubs and hung them in a line facing the WMA assembly in Rotterdam, each bearing the name of a Palestinian healthcare worker currently held in illegal Israeli detention.

It was part of a protest against the continued membership of the Israeli association in the WMA, “despite them breaching almost every ethical principle in the WMA’s Code of Medical Ethics”, the IMA Out! coalition that organised the demonstration said in a statement.

“These scrubs should not be empty. Our colleagues belong with their patients, not in Israeli prisons. Today, we literally placed their names at the WMA’s doorstep,” said Mejrem Ahmetaj, a general practitioner and member of IMA Out!.

Since October 2023, Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza has killed more than 1,700 Palestinian healthcare workers and destroyed nearly all the hospitals and healthcare facilities in the enclave.

The campaign accused the Israeli medical association of remaining silent as Palestinian healthcare has been systematically destroyed.

“The IMA is not a bystander. It defends these attacks and blocks international condemnation while Palestinian healthcare is being destroyed. That is not medical neutrality. That is complicity,” added Ahmetaj.

At a meeting of international doctors, medical leaders and human rights activists during the WMA summit on Thursday, the destruction of Palestinian healthcare and the responsibility of the international medical community were discussed, the campaign said.



“Our Palestinian colleagues are being killed and imprisoned, where they are starved and tortured. Their hospitals have been destroyed and patients driven out or murdered. The IMA has said and done nothing about these war crimes against health workers, patients and hospitals,” said a statement by Jonathan Fluxman on behalf of IMA OUT!.

“Thirty years of WMA dialogue with the IMA has done nothing but give the IMA a sense of impunity … It is time for national medical associations and the WMA to speak out and take action. Break your ties with the IMA and suspend the IMA from the WMA now,” he added.

The IMA OUT! campaign said it delivered a petition calling for the IMA’s suspension, signed by more than 6,500 health workers from around the world.

They also demanded accountability for the complicity of Israeli doctors in the starvation, torture and medical neglect of Palestinian prisoners.

Among those held by Israel is Dr Hussam Abu Safia, head of Gaza’s Kamal Adwan Hospital, whose unlawful detention has prompted an international outcry.

He was briefly held at the notorious Sde Teiman detention camp and has been subject to torture and medical neglect. Doctors protesting in Rotterdam held up placards demanding his release.

Abu Safia’s son Elyas, addressing a meeting organised by the campaign, said, “My father and all Palestinian detainees must be treated in accordance with medical ethics, and doctors must abide by the Hippocratic oath they have taken. Care cannot be given based on whose life is deemed worthy.”

World.title: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia.

The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.

"He'd better damn well stop," Trump said, before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal".

Global fuel supplies, including diesel, have been severely limited by the war against Iran launched by the US and Israel, which led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil products usually flows.

Russia - a major producer - and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes on each other's energy infrastructure and transport facilities, further straining energy markets.

"We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," Trump continued.

"He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does."

Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev described Trump's intervention as "iconic and historic", saying that Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace".

The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April.

Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war.

He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia.

World.title: Twelve killed in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh
World.content:
At least 12 people have been killed and 309 injured in an attack on an airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, local authorities say, days after Yemen's Houthis claimed similar strikes.

The deaths included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. Operations at King Khalid International Airport have been suspended.

A Saudi-led military coalition has vowed to respond to the attack, which it has blamed on the Houthis and called a "war crime".

Fighting has recently escalated between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who control most of the country.

On Saturday, a projectile also fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam in eastern Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition said.

The attacks come a day after authorities said three Saudis including a pilot were killed in two attacks on the airport by the Iran-backed Houthis the day prior. Another three people were killed in Houthi attacks on two Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October.

In Saturday's statement, the Saudi civil aviation authority said some of the injured in were "in critical condition".

It said damage to the airport was being assessed.

An eyewitness who said they had been in the domestic terminal told the news agency that they had seen gate 401 hit and "injured [people] in front of my eyes", adding: "Everyone was running."

More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to news agency Reuters, citing an eyewitness.

Saudi-led coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki later said the attack on one of the passenger terminals resulted in deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport staff.

He described the attack as a "full-fledged war crime".

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said strongly condemned recent attacks on Saudi Arabia as he confirmed an American citizen was killed in the strikes.

Western embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens away from the airport. The UK Foreign Office told British nationals to avoid the area "until the airport is secure".

Several Gulf airlines said they had cancelled their flights to and from the airport, with Kuwait Airways citing the "security situation" there.

All flights to Riyadh have either been diverted or cancelled, aviation tracker Flightradar shows.

The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war.

The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive.

That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.

A Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government.

A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.

But the informal truce began to unravel in July.

The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

They said they were retaliating against what they described as a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on the airport in Yemen's capital Sanaa, which is controlled by the Houthis.

World.title: Young men live in fear of being snatched off the streets and sold to Myanmar's army
World.content:
You do not stay out after dark if you're young and able-bodied in Hpa-An, the capital of Myanmar's southern Karen state. In recent months this has become conventional wisdom.

But Zaw Min has no choice.

"I worry, but I have to go out to work," says the 26-year-old tuk tuk driver, who asked that his real name be omitted out of fear for his safety. "My family call me all the time and remind me not to drive passengers too far; to be careful who I take as a passenger... I have to be vigilant all the time.

"People are panicked and frightened," he explains. "Some people I know have been taken."

Locals say plain-clothed members and supporters of the Myanmar junta have been roaming the streets of Hpa-An, arbitrarily arresting people in their teens, 20s and 30s and forcing them into military service.

According to leaked documents seen by BBC Burmese, authorities have been ordered to aggressively fulfil the military's recruitment quotas across jurisdictions, bolstering the junta's ranks as it endures a war of attrition against ethnic militias, pro-democracy groups and civilian-led resistance movements.

Zaw Min is the only one among his siblings who is at the age of recruitment. Many other "kids" his age have fled, he says â to Thailand, or the homes of relatives further afield. Those who remain are often under strict instructions from their parents: be home before dusk.

Myanmar has been locked in a bloody civil war since February 2021, when its own military launched a coup d'etat and ousted democratically elected leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

Three years later, following a string of humiliating losses, plummeting morale and soaring rates of desertion, the junta enacted a mandatory conscription law that required all men aged 18 to 35 and women aged 18 to 27 to serve at least two years under military command. Those who refuse face up to five years in prison.

The enactment of the law "represents one of the most severe and impactful actions taken against the entire civilian population since the military coup", according to Maj Naung Yoe, military affairs official at the Myanmar Defense and Security Institute (MDSI) and a former military officer who defected and joined the anti-coup Civil Disobedience Movement.

World.title: Russian glide bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia kills at least 20 people
World.content:
Russia has attacked the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs, killing at least 20 people including four children, local officials said.

The glide bombs hit residential buildings in the southern city on Saturday morning. At least 32 others were injured in the attack, with more still missing and believed to be under the rubble.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the attacks on Zaporizhzhia were Russia expressing "its thanks" for a deal announced by US President Donald Trump last night easing sanctions on Moscow to import Russian diesel.

He added that 13 other regions had come under attack overnight, arguing this demonstrated Russia took "any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting".

Photos and videos from the site of one of the strikes in Zaporizhzhia show an apartment block mostly destroyed.

"The ground floor was hit, and the floors above just collapsed," acting Mayor Regina Harchenko told Ukrainian television from the scene.

She said more than 80 workers were involved in ongoing search and rescue operations which are expected to continue throughout the day.

The rescuers regularly stop to listen for any noises made by survivors who could be under the rubble.

Harchenko said Russia had struck at "our very heart" and "our littlest ones" were among those killed, adding that their deaths were "awful grief for their families. For the city."

Zaporizhzhia is a major regional centre with more than 700,000 residents. It is located less than 10 miles (16km) from the front line and is frequently attacked by Russian drones and missiles.

World.title: US murderer Christa Pike discharged from hospital 10 days after failed execution
World.content:
US death row inmate Christa Pike has been discharged from hospital following her botched execution at the end of last month, her lawyers have said.

Pike, 50, has been sent back to the prison where she has spent the last 30 years and is continuing to receive medical care, according to a statement from her lawyers on Saturday.

She survived two lethal injections of the drug pentobarbital on 30 September, which left her in a critical condition.

Pike regained consciousness earlier this week and began speaking - stunning experts, medical staff and her lawyers.

Her case is now in uncharted territory as she is thought to be the only person to have survived an execution attempt by lethal injection.

World.title: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
World.content:
Four people have died and hundreds of thousands are without power after Hurricane Isaias battered parts of the southern US with powerful winds and heavy rain.

Officials reported two deaths each in the states of Alabama and Florida, which included people who were killed when trees fell on their houses.

An estimated 500,000 people in total were without power in several states as of Saturday evening, according to tracker PowerOutage.

Isaias made landfall in Florida late on Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105mph (168km/h) before being downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone.

The storm felled trees and ripped the roofs off buildings. Alabama, Florida and Georgia all declared states of emergency ahead of its arrival, while both Florida and Alabama issued mandatory evacuation orders to thousands of people.

Meanwhile, Hurricane Simon is bearing down on Mexico's Pacific coast and has strengthened to category four. It is expected to make landfall sometime overnight.

Tropical Storm Rachel, also in the Pacific Ocean, is expected to hit southern California later on Saturday.

World.title: Expedition hopes to find aviator Amelia Earhart's plane on remote island
World.content:
A team of researchers are on their way to a remote island to inspect what they think could be the wreckage of famed aviator Amelia Earhart's plane.

The group, from the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) and Purdue University, are expected to arrive at Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific Ocean by Monday in the hopes of solving the mystery of her disappearance.

The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation on her fate.

The team are aiming to find what has been called the Taraia Object, first spotted sitting on the edge of a lagoon off Nikumaroro in satellite imagery in 2020.

Purdue University said the object had since been confirmed to have been visible in aerial photography of the area dating back to 1938.

The researchers are currently roughly halfway through their journey to the remote atoll aboard the Marin Mainiku, a Kiribati National Shipping Line vessel.

They departed the capital of Kiribati on Wednesday to begin the 830-mile journey to Nikumaroro, which is also part of the multi-island country.

When they eventually arrive, they will have to navigate through a narrow gap created in the atoll's reef by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited.

"Finding Amelia Earhart's Electra aircraft would be the discovery of a lifetime," Richard Pettigrew, head of the ALI and the expedition lead, said.

World.title: Headmaster detained after BBC investigation into alleged sexual abuse of students
World.content:
Central to the BBC Eye investigation were former students Ziadatur Rahmah, known as Zia, and Sukma Rohana Fajar.

They launched their own investigation after Zia told a former classmate, Yusron Azzahidi, that the headteacher had sexually assaulted her when she was 17. The pair had been star pupils at the school.

By the time Zia confided in Yusron, she was studying in Cairo, Egypt, while he was in Jakarta.

Yusron suggested they gather evidence to support Zia's allegation. Speaking to former classmates, they spoke to Sukma, who alleges that Abah attempted to rape her at the school.

Yusron compiled a seven-page document detailing the allegations, and they gave it to representatives of Nahdlatul Wathan Diniyah Islamiyah (NWDI), the organisation that ran the school.

Thinking the school would support them, the students say that instead, they were pressured to withdraw their accusations.

In a secretly recorded phone call, Abah pleaded with Yusron to protect him and his reputation.

"Cover the shame of your teacher. Everyone makes mistakes, my child," Abah said.

Abah also contacted Zia, who secretly recorded their conversation and shared it with the BBC.

In the recording, Abah is heard apologising, but pleads with her to remain silent.

Following the BBC investigation, Abah held a news conference where he denied all the allegations. He did not deny that the voice heard in the recorded calls was his, but said the recordings were not confessions.

Sukma told the BBC she had been forced to sign a document saying her allegations were lies. She later secretly recorded a conversation with Abah's wife, known to students as Umi. In the recording, Umi tells Sukma that the document was intended to protect "her good name".

The former students eventually resumed their efforts to seek justice, with support from lawyer Joko Jumadi, who has experience in similar cases.

World.title: Abia 2027: The naysayers can rant but can’t erase, By Ferdinand Ekeoma
World.content:
The photo you are seeing here was Isi Gate, Umuahia, before Governor Alex Otti assumed office.

The same sorry spectacle greeted Abians at every other junction and corner. Contrary to the Igbo adage “Ihe Oma na Anya Gbaba Ndu” (There is a covenant between the eyes and good things), in the past, what existed was “Ihe Ojo na Anya Gbaba Ndu” (There was a covenant between the eyes and bad things), and our people accepted their fate with equanimity during the period under review.

This spectacle diminished the standing of every Abian at home and in the diaspora. It buried our dignity in the mud. It made Abia and Abians objects of caricature.

The majority of opposition elements, especially the embittered ones vilifying the present government and the Governor on a daily basis today, are not doing so because they want good governance. No! They are doing it because the era of iniquity they profiteered from, and which they desperately want to return, has become a laughable illusion. They know this reality, but they are afraid to acknowledge it.

The noise is not about good governance. If it were, they would have pushed for it when they had the opportunity to do so.

Alternatively, they would have been humble enough to acknowledge the massive changes that have happened in Abia under Governor Alex Otti’s watch. It is about their stomachs. It is about our common patrimony which they controlled and squandered with impunity when they called the shots. It is about the audacity of shamelessness. It is about lack of repentance, and of course, it is about self-inflicted deceit.

As the election year draws closer, we will not fall prey to the strategy of distraction, which the noise makers are pushing through disinformation. We will not keep ourselves busy responding to stage-managed false narratives or explaining things to those who are deaf to the truth. Instead, we will occupy ourselves with the task of telling our story, which is both factual and verifiable.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

We will be presenting verifiable facts of our achievements, while humbly acknowledging areas of shortcomings and explaining measures being put in place to improve on them.

In 2023, Governor Alex Otti made promises to Ndi Abia. They believed him because of his character, capacity and accomplishments, and subsequently voted him in. Today, he and his team will be showing the things that have been achieved. Luckily, our people are smart, intelligent and discerning. They are telling the story even more than the government itself, because they were the biggest victims of the poor governance of the past. They can feel the difference and they are telling it.

The countdown begins!

*Ferdinand Ekeoma is the Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to the Governor Alex Otti of Abia State

World.title: VIDEO: Sporadic shootings as thugs attack NDC supporters in Enugu
World.content:
There was outrage on Saturday in Enugu State when some suspected political thugs attacked supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the state.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the attack began earlier on Saturday when some NDC supporters attempted to gather at the Akanu Ibiam International Airport, Emene, but were dispersed by the hoodlums.

The supporters were at the airport to welcome the NDC governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chinyeaka Ohaa, when the incident happened.

Mr Ohaa landed at the airport ahead of the NDC’s governorship campaign flag-off on Saturday.

Video clips obtained by this newspaper showed several NDC supporters scampering for safety amid sporadic shootings by the attackers.

In one of the clips, a suspected thug was spotted hitting an NDC supporter with a plank, injuring him in front of Air Force Base near the airport in Enugu State.

The clip showed a man in army uniform standing near the suspected thug, but he did nothing to stop the attack.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Shortly before the thug attacked the victim, some NDC supporters were heard beckoning to the man in army uniform that another thug had surfaced, but he appeared unconcerned.

“Come up a bit, let’s know how we can take you to the hospital,” one of the supporters urged the injured victim, whose head was already gushing blood.

Some NDC supporters were heard in another clip lamenting that their vehicles were damaged by the attackers.

PREMIUM TIMES obtained a video clip showing vehicles with damaged windscreens.

Some NDC supporters were heard accusing police and army personnel of complicity in the attacks. But this newspaper could not independently verify the claims.

From Airport to NDC secretariat

When the NDC supporters finally gathered at the party’s secretariat in Enugu for the campaign flag off, the suspected thugs also attacked them at the venue.

“Stay where you are,” some party leaders were heard advising the frightened supporters as gunshots rent the air.

PREMIUM TIMES also obtained another video clip showing some supporters running out of the venue in confusion.

The clip showed some police operatives shooting at those believed to be the political thugs near the NDC secretariat while supporters scampered for safety.

“You people did it at the airport, we kept quiet, now we are starting it again here in our party office,” an angry NDC member was heard lamenting in a separate clip.

At the NDC secretariat, venue of the campaign flag-off, some scattered chairs and disorganised canopies bore signs of a disrupted political gathering.

Police silent

When contacted, the police spokesperson in Enugu State, Daniel Ndukwe, requested to be reached via WhatsApp.

But Mr Ndukwe, a superintendent of police, had not responded to an enquiry forwarded to him on WhatsApp as of the time of filing this report.

Not the first time

This is not the first time suspected political thugs have attacked NDC supporters and those of other parties in Enugu State.

On 12 September, for instance, some hoodlums attacked and disrupted an NDC meeting in Ndiuno-Obuoffia Community in Nkanu West Local Government Area of the state.

Within the same period, suspected thugs carried out another attack at St. Joseph Primary School in Agbani within the same council area where hoodlums also destroyed canopies and chairs meant for a Peoples Democratic Party’s rally.

The police in Enugu State later ordered an investigation into the attacks.

World.title: Gov Otti accompanies Vice-President Shettima to Ethiopia
World.content:
Governor of Abia State, Alex Otti, joined the Vice-President Kashim Shettima as he led the Nigerian delegation to the inaugural Nigeria-Ethiopia Nutrition Leadership Exchange Forum (also called the Pearl Exchange Forum) in Addis Ababa, which ran from 7 October to 9 October.

Special Adviser on Media and Publicity to Mr Otti, Ferdinand Ekeoma, disclosed this in a statement issued on 10 October in Umuahia, Abia State.

The objective of the visit was government-to-government learning on nutrition delivery, using Ethiopia’s Seqota Declaration – its commitment to end stunting in children under two by 2030 – as a model for Nigeria’s Nutrition 774 (N774) Initiative which was endorsed at the 148th National Economic Council meeting.

The delegation, which departed Abuja on 6 October, was received by Nigeria’s Ambassador to Ethiopia and Permanent Representative to the AU, Nasir Aminu, and senior Ethiopian officials.

Mr Shettima-led delegation held a bilateral meeting with the Deputy Prime Minister of Ethiopia Temesgen Tiruneh on strengthening Nigeria-Ethiopia cooperation in agriculture, trade, food security and aviation.

Key activities at the event included policy sessions on building a federal-state-local compact for nutrition

The Nigerian delegation made a field visit to a wheat farm and banana plantation in Oromia Region, the Bounty of the Basket Training Centre, households in Mojo town, and Jabdu Motors in Bishoftu.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times

World.title: 2027: Enugu teachers endorse Mbah, Tinubu for enhanced welfare, education funding
World.content:
Thousands of teachers in both public and private schools in Enugu State have endorsed the Governor of the State, Peter Mbah, for a second term, citing improved teachers’ welfare, increased education funding, promotions and other interventions.

The teachers also endorsed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, whose economic reforms, Mbah said, had made more resources available to states to embark on massive projects such as the construction of over 267 Smart Green Schools across all the 260 political wards of Enugu State.

The teachers made their position known through an estimated 12,000 of their members, who marched through parts of Enugu metropolis before holding an endorsement rally at Okpara Square, Enugu, on Saturday under the auspices of Teachers for Grassroots Movement (TGM), a Government House statement disclosed on Saturday.

The Chairman of the Enugu State chapter of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Theophilus Odo, in his speech, described Mbah as a God-sent leader, reeling out the steps taken by the governor to address the challenges that had bedevilled the education sector in the state before now.

“On behalf of the NUT, I want to say that we are happy today because God has given us a caring governor, Peter Mbah.

“He was instrumental to the domestication of the harmonised retirement benefits for the teachers even before he became governor.

“The building of over 260 Smart Green Schools is a very positive change. Our teachers and children can now compete favourably with their peers in other places.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“He has started recruiting thousands of teachers, and he is also building smart teachers by ensuring that they attend symposiums and other training programmes to gain more knowledge.

“There are no outstanding promotions, and our salaries are coming at the appropriate time.

“So, we, the teachers, are endorsing our governor for a second term in office. The votes of our teachers are only for Governor Mbah,” Odo stated.

On his part, the Chairman of the National Association of Proprietors of Private Schools (NAPPS) in Enugu State, Nelson Agu, said private school teachers were joining such a rally in the state for the first time ever to encourage what he described as Mbah’s revolution in the education sector.

He noted that the introduction of Smart Green Schools had challenged private schools in the state to improve.

“When you came and started the idea of over 260 Smart Green Schools, we thought we were out of service. But we went and upgraded our schools to meet the required standards.

“Importantly, the idea of allocating 33 per cent of the budget to the education sector for three consecutive years is something to laud your administration for,” Agu told Mbah.

The Chairman of the Trade Union Congress (TUC) in the state, Simeon Akaeme, said the Mbah administration had restored the dignity of teachers and made life better through huge investments in infrastructure and social services.

The Director-General of the Teachers for Grassroots Movement, Dr Nwakaego Aja, described education as a springboard to liberation, self-reliance and economic development amid the systemic collapse experienced by the nation.

Aja assured him of the total support of the over 30,000 teachers in the state.

“Through experiential learning and innovation, you brought answers to the quest by our nationalists, elevating education to a catalyst for economic development,” she asserted.

“We, the teachers, are not ingrates. We see what you are doing. You promised disruptive innovation, and you have delivered disruptive innovation. That is why we are here.

“We promise you this: we will take your good news to the communities, to the staff rooms, to every market, to every polling unit, and we will deliver. Our vote is for the All Progressives Congress (APC) from bottom to top,” she stressed.

The Commissioner for Education and patron of TGM, Professor Ndubueze Mbah, said the endorsement by the teachers in their thousands was a tip of the iceberg of the support coming his way and that of the President ahead of the 2027 general election.

He added, “On behalf of every teacher gathered here today, I have one message, and that is to thank you for believing and investing in the vision that it is through education that Enugu State will attain greater heights. You have committed so many resources to giving every Enugu child a future.”

In his remarks, Governor Mbah said the endorsement meant so much to him beyond the 2027 polls, as the future his administration wanted to build for the state depended on education and the teachers.

“Today’s endorsement carries a particular significance, and that is because everything we do, all the promises we have made, all the projections we have made — growing Enugu’s economy, becoming one of the top three states in terms of GDP, making Enugu State the number one state in terms of investment, business, living and tourism — are in the hands of our teachers.

“That is why it appears as if we are insane about education when you consider what we are doing in the sector —building over 7,000 classrooms. And we are not talking about the details because we do not talk about 464 furniture items, we do not talk about 25,000 desktop computers, we do not talk about over 5,000 tablets or the free feeding and uniforms, among others.

“For us, it is about transformation —transforming an education system. And that whole transformation, whether we fail or succeed, would lie largely in your hands.

“That is why, when I say that I see you and I value you, it comes from the depths of my heart because I understand what you go through to inculcate this knowledge into our children so that we can become that great state. So, we love you and appreciate you dearly,” he emphasised.

The wife of the Governor, Mrs Nkechinyere Mbah, who was represented by the Commissioner for Children, Gender Affairs and Social Development, Mrs Ngozi Enih, said the endorsement was a great reward for a government that had made education the cornerstone of its development agenda.

The event attracted senior government officials, political and community leaders, among others.

World.title: Pantami reacts after INEC omits his name from Gombe governorship candidates list
World.content:
The former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Pantami, has reacted to the omission of his name on the list of Gombe governorship candidates released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) on Saturday.

INEC listed 16 candidates for the 6 February 2027 election in Gombe State.

The list includes Bala Tinka of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Jamilu Gwamna of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and Babayo Kumo of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC).

There are also Zubairu Halilu of the Labour Party, Lamela Silas of the APM, Ibrahim Abubakar of the PRP and Adamu Ma’aji of the SDP, among others.

However, Mr Pantami, who was on the provisional list published on 29 August, did not make the new list.

He had earlier emerged as a PDP candidate after dumping APC on 19 May; before Ahmed Mailantarki, one of the aspirants, challenged Mr Pantami’s nomination in court.

The Federal High Court nullified it and ordered a fresh primary election, which Mr Pantami won again.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Reaction

The PDP leadership and the Pantamiyya Movement in Gombe State have issued a press statement addressing the omission of Mr Pantami’s name.

The statement, published on Mr Pantami’s verified Facebook page, attributed the setback to internal and external political opponents seeking to frustrate their political objectives.

The statement ,signed by one of the party leaders, Suleiman Mohammed, urged supporters to remain calm, resolute, and focused on ongoing mobilisation efforts.

He said legal and liaison teams were actively engaging with party organs and INEC to rectify the omission within the legally permitted timeframe, expressing confidence that the issue is a temporary hurdle that will be resolved successfully.

Read the statement by Mr Muhammed below.

PRESS STATEMENT!

Our attention has been drawn to the non-publication of the name of our candidate from the fresh primary election of 29th September, 2026, as ordered by the Federal High Court, Professor Isa Ali Ibrahim (Pantami), CON, PhD, FCIIS, FBCS, FNCS, in the list released by INEC, and we understand the concerns this has raised among our teeming supporters in the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the Pantamiyya Movement across Gombe State and beyond.

We wish to assure all our supporters to remain calm, steadfast, and hopeful. This is a temporary challenge and a normal part of the electoral process, not a final determination, in sha Allah. We are aware of the people working behind the scenes to frustrate good and responsible leadership in Gombe State, but our legal and liaison teams are already engaging with the relevant organs of the party and INEC to ensure full compliance and rectification within the window provided by law. By the grace of Allah, this matter will be resolved.

We urge our supporters to continue their mobilisation and to remain focused on our collective ideology of service to humanity. The PDP and Pantamiyya Movement remain strong, united, and committed to the rescue and emancipation of our people. No distraction will derail our course, in sha Allah.

May Allah bless Gombe State and may Allah bless the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

Professor Suleiman Mohammed Gombe,

10th October, 2026

World.title: INEC excludes Ogun PDP’s Adebutu, running mate from final governorship candidates list
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has excluded Ladi Adebutu, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, and his running mate from its final list of candidates for the 6 February 2027 governorship election.

According to the INEC’s final list of governorship candidates reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES, the exclusion of Mr Adebutu leaves the PDP governorship ticket absent from the 13 candidates listed by the commission for the election, raising questions about the party’s participation in the contest.

The list, signed by INEC Secretary Rose Oriaran-Anthony, contains candidates from 13 political parties. The list also includes African Democratic Congress (ADC) governorship candidate, Lawal Adebisi, and his running mate, Olutayo Florence, following court order.

What could be the the problem

The development comes amid questions about the PDP candidate’s eligibility to run for next year’s elections, following allegations by civil society groups that his name was missing from the party’s membership register submitted to INEC.

The two civil society groups, Ogun Democratic Accountability Forum be 23rd and Elections Integrity Watch had raised concerns about Mr Adebutu’s absence from the party’s register and demanded for his disqualification in the governorship election race.

Elections Integrity Watch said a certified true copy of the PDP membership register it obtained from INEC did not contain Mr Adebutu’s name, raising questions about the documentation supporting his candidacy.

Although INEC had yet to publicly explain the omission of Mr Adebutu and his running mate as of the time of filing this report.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Electoral Act 2026 outlines a procedure for political parties whose candidates’ names are missing from INEC’s published list.

Section 32(1) requires the commission to publish the names and addresses of all candidates standing nominated at least 60 days before an election.

Under Section 32(2), a registered political party that discovers its candidate’s name is missing must notify INEC in writing within 14 days of publication. The notification must be signed by the party’s national chairman and secretary and supported by an affidavit.

The provisions establish a formal process for notifying INEC about an omitted candidate. However, the precise implications for the PDP ticket depends on the circumstances surrounding the omission and any subsequent action by the party or the commission.

Although the party had not publicly indicated if it had formally notified INEC of the omission or whether it intended to challenge the published list.

Other candidates on the list

Apart from the ADC and the All Progressives Congress (APC), whose candidate is Adeola Olamilekan, a serving Nigerian senator, the published list includes candidates from several other parties.

They are Okewole Shuaib of Party A; Awofala Awoniyi of the Action Alliance (AA); Anifowose Kayode of the Action Democratic Party (ADP); Babajide Mathew of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM); and Layi Halima of the Action Peoples Party (APP).

Others are Adenuga Dreher of the Boot Party (BP); Dasaolu Olamilekan of the National Democratic Party (NDP); Akinbola Hammed of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP); Fayoyin Ezekiel of the National Rescue Movement (NRM); Ola Willams of the Social Democratic Party (SDP); and Johnson Cyrus of the Young Progressives Party (YPP).

Ogun State is among the 28 states scheduled to hold governorship elections on 6 February 2027, alongside elections into their respective Houses of Assembly.

INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan had earlier announced that 21 of the country’s 22 registered political parties nominated 936 governorship and deputy governorship candidates across the 28 states holding elections in 2027. The parties also nominated 9,692 candidates for State Houses of Assembly elections.

World.title: INEC lists 16 candidates for Gombe governorship race, omits PDP’s Pantami
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has omitted Isa Ibrahim Pantami from its final list of candidates for the 2027 Gombe State governorship election, raising questions about the former minister of Communications and digital economy’s participation in the race.

INEC’s document does not state why Mr Pantami was omitted or explain the absence of the PDP from the list.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The major candidates listed include Gwamna Isyaku of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Bala Tinka of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), and Muazu Halilu of the Labour Party (LP).

Further clarification from INEC and the PDP is expected to determine the implications of the final list for Pantami’s political ambition.

World.title: UK migrant workers wear chains, sing Asa’s ‘Jailer’ to protest proposed visa reforms
World.content:
Migrant workers in the United Kingdom wore chains and sang Nigerian singer Asa’s ‘Jailer’ during a protest against proposed changes to immigration rules that could make workers wait up to 15 years before qualifying for permanent settlement.

The demonstration was held on Monday, 28 September, outside the Labour Party conference in Liverpool, as migrant workers and their supporters opposed proposed changes to the UK’s settlement system.

Videos posted by UNISON, the UK’s largest trade union, showed protesters wearing chains and singing ‘Jailer’, which was released in 2007 by Nigerian singer Bukola Elemide, popularly known as Asa, as part of her self-titled debut album.

In a post on its Instagram page, UNISON said the migrant workers sang ‘Jailer’ because of its themes of “oppression, power and refusing to accept being treated as a prisoner.”

UNISON said more than 400 people participated in the protest, with many “symbolically wearing balls and chains”.

The union explained that the visa rules can tie workers to a particular employer, meaning that “leaving an exploitative workplace or speaking out” could affect their right to remain in the UK and their families’ futures.

Reason for protest

The demonstration was organised as part of UNISON’s Fair Visa Campaign, which is calling on the UK government to abandon proposed changes to settlement rules.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Under plans from Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, care staff, NHS employees and lower-paid public service workers will have to wait 15 years to qualify to settle in the UK, instead of the current five,” UNISON noted on its website.

UNISON wants the five-year qualifying period retained for skilled workers. It is also calling for a “sector-wide visa sponsorship system” for social care workers, which it says would reduce workers’ vulnerability to exploitation.

Speaking at the protest, UNISON General Secretary, Andrea Egan said migrant workers should not be blamed for failures to invest in public services.

“The NHS, social care and other essential services rely on the hard work of migrant staff,” Ms Egan said, according to the union.

She accused the government of replacing the previous five-year settlement expectation with “the threat of 15 years of insecurity and exploitation” and called for the proposals to be dropped.

Nigerians among major care-worker groups

The proposed changes are significant for Nigerians because the country has been one of the leading sources of workers recruited through the UK’s Health and Care Worker visa route.

UK Home Office statistics show that 18,143 Nigerian nationals were granted visas to work as care workers and home carers in 2023.

Nigerian nationals, alongside migrants from India and Zimbabwe, accounted for 58 per cent of visas granted for care worker and home carer jobs that year, according to the Home Office.

Government considers changes

The protest came amid opposition to the proposed settlement changes from some Labour figures and trade unions.

According to The Guardian, Home Secretary, Shabana Mahmood signalled on 28 September that she was considering watering down plans that would make it harder for some foreign workers to obtain permanent residence in the UK.

Speaking at the Labour Party conference in Liverpool, Ms Mahmood acknowledged that some people had described elements of the reforms as unfair.

She said the government would “come to a position that balances fairness for those who came here legally, and fairness to British citizens.”

The Guardian reported that her comments followed pressure from Labour cabinet colleagues, including Angela Rayner, as well as UNISON General Secretary Andrea Egan, who had urged the government to drop the proposed changes to indefinite leave to remain.

The newspaper also reported that no final decision had been made on the proposals.
