World.title: US gunman shoots dead 7 relatives, family friend
World.content:
A 45-year-old man shot and killed seven relatives and a family friend at a home in Pennsylvania before apparently taking his own life, authorities said Saturday.

The victims in the city of Erie included two young children and a woman who was eight months pregnant.

Police responded Friday evening to reports of shots fired and discovered two women dead in the street, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah told reporters.

Video evidence showed the pair arriving at the residence appearing distressed, then attempting to contact neighbors and enter the house, Lorah said.

The gunman exited the house, shot them, and returned inside, he said.

The man barricaded himself inside the home as police surrounded the building and ordered him to exit. He was later found inside with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, Lorah said.

The shooter and seven of his victims were related, Lorah said. The eighth victim was a family friend.

Dead inside the home were a five-year-old boy and a one-year-old girl. The others were men and women ranging in age from 19 to 51. One of the women was eight months pregnant.

Local news outlet Erie News Now said responding officers were being offered counseling over the horrifying incident.

“Many people across our community are hurting today: the neighbors who witnessed what happened, the families and friends of those who were killed, the officers and first responders who answered these calls, and others struggling to make sense of something so terrible,” Erie Mayor Daria Devlin told reporters Saturday.

“We cannot undo what happened last night, and we cannot take away the grief that these families are carrying, but we can make sure that they don’t have to carry it alone,” she said.

Mass shootings occur frequently in the United States, where guns vastly outnumber people and efforts to increase firearm restrictions face steep political and legal hurdles.

AFP

World.title: Benue: Suspected herdsmen kill nine in fresh Ukum attacks
World.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi

At least nine persons have reportedly been killed in fresh attacks by suspected armed herdsmen on Tse-Nyaku, Tse-Biliji and adjoining communities in Mbatian Council Ward of Ngenev, Ukum Local Government Area of Benue State.

Several others were reportedly injured, while an unspecified number of residents were said to be missing following the attacks, which began at about 11pm on Friday.

A local source, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the assailants invaded the communities in large numbers, shooting sporadically and forcing residents to flee their homes.

According to the source, nine bodies had so far been recovered from the affected communities.

“The attackers came in large numbers and started shooting in the communities. Luckily, many people managed to escape, except for the nine who have been confirmed dead for now because their corpses have been recovered.

“However, it is very likely that the number could increase because many people have not been seen, and no one knows whether they were killed or escaped to other communities.

“Our people discovered that one of armed herdsmen is in possession of the phones of one of the victims and he has been using it to make and receive calls.

“The attacked communities have also already been deserted. It is a very sad day for our people. The Sankera axis of Benue has become a shadow of itself due to the level of insecurity,” he said.

Reacting to the incident, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate for Ukum I (Ngenev) State Constituency in the Benue State House of Assembly, Livinus Tyodoo, described the invasion as “one attack too many.”

In a statement he personally signed, Tyodoo said he received disturbing reports of the deadly attacks on the communities on Friday night and in the early hours of Saturday.

He said the attacks, allegedly carried out by suspected herdsmen militia, had reportedly claimed more than nine lives, adding that several bodies had been recovered while other residents remained missing and some survivors sustained varying degrees of injuries.

“This is one attack too many. I unequivocally condemn the senseless killing, displacement and continued persecution of innocent citizens in their ancestral homes.

“The people of Ukum I (Ngenev) deserve to live in peace, cultivate their farmlands and pursue their legitimate means of livelihood without the constant fear of violence.

“Human civilisation has evolved beyond the Hobbesian state of nature, where life was characterised by insecurity and the constant fear of violent death. In the 21st century, the sanctity of human life must remain paramount, and no community should be abandoned to the mercy of armed assailants,” he said.

Tyodoo stressed that the incident should not be politicised, urging the authorities to take urgent and decisive action to prevent further bloodshed.

“This is not the time for politics or the exchange of blame. It is a time for urgent, coordinated and decisive action,” he said.

He called on the Benue State Government, Ukum Local Government Council and relevant security agencies to strengthen security operations in the affected communities and other vulnerable areas of the local government.

According to him, beyond issuing statements and ordering investigations, the government must ensure effective intelligence gathering, proactive security deployments, the arrest and prosecution of those responsible, and concrete measures to prevent further attacks.

“Our people must be able to return to their ancestral homes, reclaim their farmlands and carry on with their daily activities without fear. The protection of lives and property is a fundamental responsibility of government, and the people of Ukum deserve nothing less,” he added.

The PDP candidate also expressed condolences to the families of those reportedly killed, while praying for the safe return of missing persons and the speedy recovery of the injured.

“I pray for the peaceful repose of the souls of the departed, comfort for the bereaved families, the safe return of anyone still missing, and a speedy recovery for those who sustained injuries.

“May God comfort our grieving communities, protect our people and restore lasting peace to Ngenev, Ukum and Benue State at large. The time for urgent action is now. Our people deserve security, justice and lasting peace,” he said.

When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, said he was yet to receive a report on the incident.

World.title: PSG ease to Ligue 1 win before Manchester City test
World.content:
PSG’s Georgian forward #07 Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (C) celebrates Paris Saint-Germain’s victory with teammates at the end of the French L1 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and Le Mans FC at the Parc des Princes stadium in Paris on October 10, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP)

Paris Saint-Germain were comfortable 3-1 winners against Le Mans on Saturday before they look ahead to a tougher test away to Manchester City in the Champions League next week.

Their third win in a row after a slow start to the season came despite resting a host of players.

PSG went ahead through a first-half spot kick from centre-back Lucas Beraldo but Louis Mafouta brought Le Mans level at the Parc des Princes nine minutes after half-time.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia spent the first half on the bench but he put PSG ahead on 61 minutes, just two minutes after he was brought on, before Maghnes Akliouche wrapped up the win seven minutes later.

PSG move up to fifth before the back-to-back European champions travel to City, who are reeling after being found guilty of dozens of Premier League spending infractions, on Wednesday.

Monaco missed a chance to open up a two-point lead at the top as they were held to a 2-2 home draw by Toulouse.

They lead Lille by a single point after the northern side beat Le Havre 1-0 at home.

World.title: Ogun PDP urges calm over Adebutu’s omission from INEC list
World.content:
Adebutu

By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta

The Ogun State chapter of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has called on its members and supporters to remain calm following the omission of its governorship candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, from a list published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), expressing confidence that the issue would be resolved ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The opposition party alleged that the development was the result of pressure from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), which it accused of being apprehensive about the PDP’s chances in the forthcoming election.

The party, however, maintained that Adebutu remained a bona fide member of the PDP, insisting that he had fulfilled the party’s membership registration requirements within the stipulated period.

In a statement issued by its Publicity Secretary, Arc. Kayode Adebayo, the PDP said, participated in the party’s digital membership registration exercise, during which his membership card was printed and verified before being submitted to INEC within the prescribed timeframe.

“We state emphatically that our candidate, Hon. Oladipupo Adebutu, has never left the Peoples Democratic Party at any time. He duly registered as a member of the party within the designated period of the digital registration exercise, and his membership card was printed, verified and submitted to INEC at the stipulated time,” the statement said.

The party attributed the omission to what it described as political interference, alleging that the APC was seeking to undermine its chances ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

“The omission of our candidate’s name from INEC’s list is a consequence of the undue pressure allegedly mounted on the commission by the ruling party out of fear of losing the election to our party,” Adebayo stated.

The PDP, however, expressed optimism that Adebutu’s name would be included in the relevant list of candidates, reaffirming its commitment to participating in the 2027 governorship election.

It urged the people of Ogun State not to be distracted by the development, calling on its members and supporters to remain focused on their political objectives and continue mobilising for the forthcoming election.

“While we urge the good people of Ogun State not to be perturbed or distracted from our collective resolve to vote out the APC, we remain resolute, unfazed and unwaveringly confident that our candidate is marching towards a decisive victory in the 2027 governorship election,” the statement added.

The opposition party further maintained that the development would not diminish what it described as the determination of the people of Ogun State to demand better governance and positive change.

“No amount of desperate manipulation, political witch-hunts or calculated distractions can alter the mandate of the people of Ogun State, who are overwhelmingly eager for true leadership and positive change,” the PDP said.

Reiterating its appeal for calm, the party urged its members, supporters and other stakeholders to remain steadfast and undeterred as it intensifies its political activities ahead of the election.

“Once again, we call on all our teeming supporters, party faithful and the general public to remain steadfast, vigilant and unintimidated as the unstoppable movement to rescue Ogun State and bring relief to our people continues to gain momentum,” the statement said.

World.title: Real Madrid edge Villarreal, Vinicius sent off for hair pull
World.content:
Real Madrid’s Brazilian forward #07 Vinicius Junior (C) is restrained by teammates as he argues with referee Isidro Escuderos after receiving a red card during the Spanish league football match between Real Madrid CF and Villarreal CF at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on October 10, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP)

Yan Diomande earned Real Madrid a tight 1-0 victory over Villarreal on Saturday to keep them six points behind La Liga leaders Barcelona, even though winger Vinicius Junior was sent off for hair-pulling.

Brazil international Vinicius, on as a substitute, scored but his goal was disallowed and then he was dismissed after a VAR review showed he pulled the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba.

Jose Mourinho’s Madrid battled through the final stages with 10 men but held on to win and go provisionally third.

Champions Barca lead La Liga after a 3-0 win over Getafe, while Atletico Madrid are five points behind in second after they edged Alaves 2-1.

Striker Kylian Mbappe was fit to start the match for Madrid at their Santiago Bernabeu stadium after suffering a knee problem playing for France during the international break.

There were a smattering of whistles for the superstar forward, with some fans believing he has been unprofessional in recent weeks, but also applause from other supporters.

Mbappe, a candidate for the Ballon d’Or trophy later this month, was Madrid’s most threatening player in the first half, although he had little competition.

Mourinho started with out-of-form winger Vinicius on the bench, following his trips to Australia and India with Brazil during the international break.

Madrid improved defensively, giving Villarreal few chances of note, but struggled to build much in attack themselves in a drab opening half.

Mbappe struck the post from Alvaro Carreras’s lay-off as Madrid pushed Villarreal back early on.

Villarreal soon gained a foothold and restricted Madrid’s opportunities, until Mbappe forced a good save from Peter Gulacsi.

There was some more mild whistling for Madrid’s display from their fans at half-time, but soon they were able to celebrate summer arrival Diomande’s first goal for the club.

The Ivorian winger, Madrid’s record 140-million-euro ($157 million) signing, produced a sharp low finish into the far corner after good work from Federico Valverde to play him in.

Vinicius thought he had doubled Madrid’s lead after Jude Bellingham charged in down the left and cut the ball back for him.

However the winger’s joy turned to anger after referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was called to watch Vinicius’s hair pull on Saliba in the build-up by VAR and sent off the Brazilian, voiding his goal.

Madrid’s Belgian goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, who had made a couple of smart saves earlier in the half, produced an acrobatic stop to thwart Carlos Romero.

Mbappe was denied again by Hungarian goalkeeper Gulasci as the forward left the Bernabeu frustrated in his hunt for goals, although his team were able to clinch three important points to stay on Barca’s trail.

World.title: Regina Daniels marks 25th birthday in wheelchair
World.content:
Nollywood actress Regina Daniels has disclosed that she has endured months of severe pain and difficulty walking, revealing that her condition has left her dependent on a wheelchair.

The actress shared the update in a video posted on her Instagram page on Saturday to celebrate her 25th birthday, using the opportunity to explain her absence from social media.

Daniels, a mother of two, said what initially appeared to be a minor health problem gradually worsened, leaving her unable to move freely and sometimes preventing her from walking.

“I know many of you may be surprised seeing me in a wheelchair. Well, welcome to another chapter of my life. Let me walk you through what my life has been since many of you have asked questions about my absence,” she said.

Recounting how her condition deteriorated, Daniels said she began experiencing more serious symptoms after hosting a children’s day carnival.

“For several months now, I have lost my freedom to move around as I please. It started as something minor, very minor, but eventually led to this.

“But things took a major turn after the last public gathering I hosted, my children’s day carnival. One test after another, I jokingly started calling myself a lab rat. The pain became excruciating. Sometimes I can walk, and sometimes I can’t move. I cried,” she added.

The actress expressed gratitude for the progress she said she had made in her recovery, noting that recent developments had encouraged her to speak publicly about her health.

“Well, me sitting here today, in front of this camera, sharing this with y’all, it’s because there’s been some really significant developments in my recovery. And I say, thank you, Lord,” she said.

Daniels also described the emotional difficulties associated with her condition, particularly having to rely on others for assistance with routine activities.

Despite the challenges, she said her faith in God had helped her through the experience and expressed hope for healing and peace.

The actress further disclosed that she had moved closer to her loved ones, especially her children, whom she described as being particularly dear to her.

She said she initially rented the property she moved into but later developed an interest in owning it.

Daniels married businessman and politician Ned Nwoko in 2019, and the couple have two children. Their relationship has since been marked by a public and contentious separation.

World.title: Tinubu’ll take Nigeria from reforms to prosperity if re-elected – First Lady
World.content:
First Lady Sen Oluremi Tinubu says President Bola Tinubu will move Nigeria from economic reforms to prosperity if re-elected for a second term in 2027.

Tinubu said this on Saturday in Lafia at the North-Central Mega Rally organised by the All Progressives Congress (APC) to mobilise support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima.

The First Lady urged party members to take the campaign to communities across the region and mobilise voters for the party’s candidates.

She highlighted some achievements of the Tinubu administration across various sectors, saying continuity was necessary to sustain the gains.

“President Tinubu is a man who believes in the unity, security and prosperity of our nation.

“The Independence Day message of Mr President was titled ‘From Reforms to Prosperity’.

“Therefore, Mr President is saying that they are going to reform the sector, but now is the time for prosperity, and we can see our economy is stabilising.

“Foreign exchange is going down, and investors are coming back to Nigeria, our farmers too. You can see all our governors here; they are doing infrastructural development like no other time before.

“I have been in the Senate for 12 years. This is the best time I will see the government fixing roads and building a lot of infrastructure,” she said.

Tinubu also cited the administration’s food support programme, saying it was designed to provide nutritious food for children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.

“As you see now, we have just finished the food bank programme, where we are helping every child and mothers who are pregnant and also breastfeeding.

“This is to ensure that they can have more nutritious food, and also the children that are malnourished can get treatment and also get food to grow healthy,” she said.

She added that students were also benefiting from the administration’s education funding initiatives.

The First Lady urged party members to communicate the administration’s policies and programmes to Nigerians in their respective states.

She described Tinubu as a leader willing to take difficult decisions, expressing confidence that his policies would strengthen the economy and improve security.

She said the administration would continue to pursue a stronger economy, safer communities and a greater Nigeria if returned to office.

The First Lady also said the APC women’s wing had united its campaign efforts to promote a common message and goal ahead of the 2027 general elections.

She said the party’s campaign would focus on its programmes and policies without resorting to hate speech or actions capable of undermining national unity.

“Therefore, vote for continuity, vote for capacity, vote for prosperity, and vote for the re-election of Mr President and all the candidates of APC from top to bottom,” she said.

The rally was hosted by Gov. Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa, with governors and other political leaders from the North-Central region in attendance. (NAN)

World.title: The Political Somersaults on Petrol Subsidy
World.content:
Postscript by Waziri Adio

Let me say this upfront: there was the need for a swift and consequential policy response by the President Bola Tinubu administration to mitigate the predictable negative effects of the global energy crisis on Nigerian households and small businesses. The reasons were obvious enough. Most Nigerians were still reeling from reform-induced high prices and their country, as an oil-producer, stood to reap some windfall (no matter how small) from the increase in oil prices arising from the after-shocks of the US-Israel war on Iran.

The Tinubu government missed a trick by not isolating the oil windfall and by failing to use at least a part of it to provide concrete and meaningful reliefs to most Nigerians who have had to endure a concentrated and lingering cost-of-living crisis since the removal of petrol subsidy and the depreciation of the Naira in mid-2023. This built on an earlier error of not isolating savings from petrol subsidy removal and earmarking some part of it to a relief programme that is visible to all and easily trackable. The administration is about committing a third avoidable error: commencing the reversal of the removal of petrol subsidy, its signature reform that has significantly contributed to fiscal stability and, in a way, boosted energy security.

It is equally important to state upfront that the issue is not about whether reliefs should be offered or not. This set of reliefs should have been rolled out at least six months ago, and the government did not need to borrow or struggle to find the extra money for them. It just needed to use some of the oil windfall to cushion the effect of the energy shock on the vulnerable. I argued this position on this page on 22 March 2026 in a piece titled “The Oil Windfall This Time.” The issue is also not about ideological opposition to subsidy or about not expecting the government to respond to electoral pressures. My issue is that government’s response is as wrong-headed as the position of the opposition candidates who were previously in support of subsidy removal.

The Minister of Finance, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, made a passionate case for why petrol subsidy must not be reversed on Thursday, then announced some measures that effectively translate to restoring petrol subsidy. In addition to his speech at the press conference, Oyedele issued a statement on Friday and appeared on a TV interview programme to provide further clarification. The national oil company and some presidential spokespersons have also chimed in. It is not subsidy, they say. It is margin discount and price modulation, they insist. The more clarification they provide, the more unconvincing they sound.

Oyedele disclosed ten things that the government is doing or considering implementing, but only three stand out for me. One, NNPCL will sell petrol at discounted price for one month at the first instance in its filling stations, with “priority to public transporters.” Oyedele and others have said NNPCL would absorb the cost in reduced margins, that the increase in demand might even offset the cost of the discount, and that it would not affect the dividends to the Federation from the national oil company (as if the company has been paying dividends anyway). Most crucially, they also said the reduced or eliminated margin is not subsidy because it has no revenue or budget implication for the government. It is rich that such an argument could issue from the finance minister. Suffice to say that the discount is not cost-free in any way and that NNPCL is owned 100% by the Federation. Anyone with a faint familiarity with the history of the national oil company will never put NNPCL in such a tempting situation. Prioritising transporters assumes that the transporters will automatically pass on the benefits of the discounted petrol to commuters in reduced fares and making the discount time-bound suggests that even this N66 per litre discount can be stopped two months to a tight general election. It is doubtful both assumptions will hold.

The second and third standout interventions are linked: forward sale of crude to local oil refiners and price modulation (which, by the way, was into the petrol pricing lexicon in 2016 by Dr. Ibe Kachikwu when he was the Minister of State for Petroleum). Forward sales would ensure price stability for the oil refiners and is thus not a bad idea with the hope that they will transfer the stability to consumers. This might just end up as a transfer of surplus. Price modulation is intended to keep the refiners honest but it is at best a price cap which can turn into a form of price control. The potentially negative impact of price control on supply and price is well known.

Oyedele said: “The government is negotiating a ceiling of N1,350 a litre on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol, to keep pump prices stable. Where costs rise above the ceiling, refiners and importers will carry the shortfall and recover it later, when crude prices or the exchange rate allow, without breaching the ceiling. This is neither a subsidy nor a price control: it is designed to smooth prices over time rather than suppressing them.”

There is a lot to unpack here. First, the operative word is “negotiating.” Why do you need to announce what is not yet finalised? Second, this only kicks in when the ex-gantry price or the landing cost goes above N1,350. The ex-gantry price or landing cost is not the final price paid by consumers. The retailers will still add their margins. This modulation is to ensure that the wholesale price does not go beyond N1,350 per litre and that when the price goes above that cap, the refiners and importers are expected to absorb the difference until when they can recoup their previous loss.

This is where it starts getting interesting. Why should the refiner or importer bear the difference? What happens if ex-gantry price or landing cost stays elevated above N1,350 per litre for a long time, say a year or more? You are basically asking them to give credit without interest and without certainty of time to consumers because government has decreed it. And when the landing cost falls below N1,350 per litre, how do you monitor how much should be recouped by the refiners and importers or how they will spread out the recovery? And when refiners and importers are made to sell below cost, how can you say that is not subsidy or price control?

It is also worth stating that we have been here before, just that the last time we were honest enough to call it by its plain name: subsidy. In January 2006, the Federal Government established the Petroleum Support Fund (PSF), managed by the Petroleum Products Pricing Regulatory Agency (PPPRA) in coordination with the Petroleum Equalisation Fund (PEF), both of which are now defunct. The PSF was designed to stabilise the price of petrol, with the shortfall funded by the three tiers of government. The subsidy scheme cost N257.36 billion or about $2 billion in 2006. It is public knowledge how that experiment ended, but suffice to restate that in 2011, we appropriated N240 billion for petrol subsidy while we spent at least N1.7trillion (I deliberately used at least because the parliamentary investigation put the final cost at N2.59 trillion).

The Oyedele iteration is asking the refiners and importers, and not the government, to bear the shortfall this time. Shifting the burden might be seen as a safeguard. But who sets up a business to absorb avoidable loss with the hope of recouping it later? How realistic is this proposal and at what cost? Why will a company that is located in an export free zone refining and selling a globally competitive product be the one to bear the shortfall and why should importers continue to commit their valuable capital to import to sell below cost? Who monitors the shortfall and what prevents the monitors and the entities being monitored from colluding? Assuming such monitoring capacity exists, is this a good use of state capacity? And if the refiners and the importers refuse to play ball, what can you do and where do you end up? With NNPCL in its sweetest spot as the sole importer?

Beyond these issues, the most critical thing is that the announced interventions are unlikely to move the needle in terms of the costs of transport, food and other essential things that most Nigerians still struggle with. The interventions are at turns tokenistic and problematic. They could use more rigour. Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, who set the tone on the petrol subsidy debate, has had so much fun pooh-poohing the measures announced by the Tinubu administration. Atiku has succeeded in turning petrol subsidy to the main campaign issue of the 2027 presidential election cycle. Since he offered to restore the subsidy during an interview on August 19, every other presidential candidate has had to respond to the politically attractive but fiscally reckless proposal by the flagbearer of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). Clearly, the issue must be polling well.

Mr Peter Obi, the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), initially said he would not restore the subsidy but would manage the gains and the process better. In a recent interview with BBC, he walked that back, saying he would tackle the corruption first, then restore the subsidy. The idea of tackling the corruption of subsidy by touting personal integrity is not new. We all know what happened the last time. It is better to eliminate the perverse incentives for corruption than rely on the body language of one man, even if he is an “in-charge” president.

Mr Donald Duke, the candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), upped the ante when he offered to reduce the price of petrol to N300 per litre. He said he would offer 600, 000 barrels of crude oil to local refiners, then sell the remaining one million barrels per day. It is comically sad that Duke does not know or pretends not to know that not all the oil produced in the country belongs to the Federation. Yet he was a governor who received money from the Federation Account to run his state for eight years. It goes to show that many in top leadership position know quite little about the operation of the oil sector that used to be the mainstay of the economy or of the Federation Account.

On his part, Tinubu swiftly dismissed Atiku’s proposal but the policy measures by his government fall in the same mould, even if it has more meat. Atiku’s proposal is not the genius idea that the former Vice President thinks it is, as I wrote here on 23 August in an article titled “Back to the Petrol Subsidy Question.” Atiku and his team have said he is promising something new, which is “production subsidy”, and that he would “follow the barrel.” This word-play may fool the uninitiated or those who have not been paying enough attention to our oil sector.

Atiku has a right to flip-flop on petrol subsidy. But there is nothing new in production subsidy. That was what we did when our four refineries were still working and even the military governments found it difficult to police the subsidy regime or contain its suffocating pressure on the country’s finances. Assuming that the problem with petrol subsidy in Nigeria will be fixed by where the subsidy happens is an extravagant assumption. For one, it does not eliminate the cost. Atiku has not disclosed the cost of his proposal, the implication of this for the still fragile finances of the three tiers of government, what the trade-offs will be, where he will find the barrels, and how he will address unintended consequences. The onus is on him to further elevate the debate by showing the details.

Without a doubt, Nigeria needed the bold reforms implemented by Tinubu. These reforms have dragged the country from the edge of the precipice to a stable ground. For instance, Nigeria reaped more of the burdens than the benefits of the global energy crisis that followed Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Nigeria suffered high prices, was the only oil producing country that did not earn a windfall from oil prices that went as high as $139, and ended up with a record petrol subsidy bill of $10 billion. In 2026, when another global energy crisis came calling, Nigeria was in a more resilient position. It had eliminated petrol subsidy (which allowed local refiners to come on stream and be competitive) and is in a position to earn an oil windfall.

But the macro stability restored by the reforms has been at a high cost at the micro level, the kind not experienced in generations. The Tinubu administration has not covered itself in glory in taking seriously the predictable consequences of implementing difficult reforms by providing adequate and coordinated succour from the gains of the reforms to the generality of Nigerians, especially the most vulnerable. The pass-through of the shock from the Middle East provided a second chance, especially because it also came with the promise of a windfall.

The oil price benchmark in our 2026 budget is $64.85 per barrel of crude oil. Brent crude has sold for an average $93.77 per barrel since February 28 when the US and Israel started the war in Iran. That means that we should have earned about $29 more than we had budgeted for each barrel of oil belonging to the Federation. Yes, our oil production has been below the production benchmark of 1.84 million barrels per day and not all the barrels belong to the Federation. But isolating the windfall and earmarking portions of it to provide succour to citizens would have served all concerned better. Not that it would have totally eliminated the appeal of populism but most Nigerians would have coped better with the shocks.

It is important to protect these reforms, otherwise Nigeria would soon be back on the fiscal brink (which will make the poor even more vulnerable) and all the suffering would have been for nothing. But part of the programme for protecting the reforms will be to consciously expand the constituency for reforms by reducing the burden on the citizens, especially the poorest. Providing targeted reliefs to Nigerians in ways that will directly bring down the prices of food, transport, medication etc., is the way to go.

The policy levers for doing this can include a six-month duty waiver on key food items that we don’t produce enough of, voucher-based subsidised inputs for farmers, subsidised public transport, energy vouchers to civil servants, diesel vouchers transporters and small businesses, and one-off cash transfers to the vulnerable possibly through the states. These subsidies will be at a cost to government in either forgone or diminished revenue, will be protested by some, and will not be distortion-free. But the cost can be capped, the sharp practices can be contained, and the benefits can go directly to address the most pressing needs of households and firms.

World.title: Asari Dokubo N2.7tn Pipeline Bombshell
World.content:
Niger Delta figure Asari Dokubo has reignited one of Nigeria’s most sensitive conversations, alleging that pipeline surveillance arrangements tied to the Olu of Warri and businessman Osahon Idahosa are worth far more than the contract held by former militant leader Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo.

In a viral broadcast, Dokubo put the figure at N2.7 trillion annually, though he initially described it as a monthly sum before correcting himself on camera. That inconsistency has already drawn scrutiny from observers tracking the claim.

Dokubo made the comments while defending Tompolo, whose contract with Tantita Security Services has faced persistent public criticism. He questioned why that scrutiny has not extended equally to other beneficiaries of pipeline-related arrangements.

He also named businessman Arthur Eze as a former holder of a pipeline-related contract and claimed to have seen a vessel linked to former Abia State Governor Orji Uzor Kalu operating in Niger Delta waters.

None of these claims came with supporting documentation. Dokubo presented no contracts, payment records or official paperwork alongside the broadcast, and stated he has no personal involvement in the pipeline arrangements himself.

Expectedly, the Olu of Warri’s camp responded swiftly. His representative to NNPC Limited, Prince Collins Edema, dismissed the allegations as completely false and challenged Dokubo to produce concrete evidence backing the N2.7 trillion figure.

Independent analysts have raised their own doubts. Tompolo’s publicised contract has previously been valued around N48 billion, a figure vastly smaller than Dokubo’s claim, leading some to question whether he conflated raw oil production value with actual security fees.

Dokubo also floated ethnic favouritism as an explanation, suggesting Tompolo faces disproportionate scrutiny because of his Ijaw background while Bini and Itsekiri figures escape similar attention. But that is more speculation than fact, some observers quickly point out.

Other observers see tactical positioning rather than ethnic grievance. In other words, it is possible that former militant leaders are just pressuring the Tinubu administration to redistribute pipeline protection contracts among a wider pool of beneficiaries.

Leaving aside the drama, some questions do float to the surface, such as how much Nigeria truly spends protecting its pipelines, who profits from that spending, and why private contractors rather than state security forces still carry the responsibility.

World.title: Aiyedatiwa Remarks Fuel Fresh Questions Over Political Feud in Ondo
World.content:
Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa’s recent appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today has drawn fresh attention to his relationship with Minister of Interior Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, widely known as BTO, ahead of Ondo’s 2027 political cycle.

Speaking with host Seun Okinbaloye, Aiyedatiwa addressed the dynamic between the two APC heavyweights in notably formal terms, framing their relationship around party structure rather than personal closeness.

“He is a member of my party,” Aiyedatiwa said of Tunji-Ojo, adding that he is a minister and “we are all APC.”

The governor went further, stressing his constitutional authority within the state and essentially describing himself as governor and Tunji-Ojo as one of his subjects.

That phrasing has attracted some scrutiny. Rather than speaking to personal affinity, the governor centred his answer on offices and obligations, a choice some observers read as significant given the political stakes involved.

Aiyedatiwa was equally direct when dismissing concerns about the African Democratic Congress gaining ground in Ondo, questioning whether the party’s emergence carried any real electoral weight. According to him, politics is a game of numbers, so until ADC actually controls stuff, it will not be treated as a credible threat to established structures.

Meanwhile, both Aiyedatiwa and Tunji-Ojo hold significant power within Ondo’s APC. Aiyedatiwa commands the state’s executive machinery and civil service, while Tunji-Ojo brings federal backing and what party loyalists describe as a formidable grassroots network built around his home base.

A Federal High Court ruling has already found Aiyedatiwa ineligible for another term due to constitutional limits, intensifying succession conversations within the party well ahead of 2027.

Grassroots mobilisation tied to Tunji-Ojo, including the BTO Unit-to-Unit movement, has added to speculation about a quiet rivalry, even as both camps publicly insist the relationship remains cordial.

Whether Aiyedatiwa’s remarks are simple facts about political institutions or something closer to a cooling relationship remains, for now, a matter of interpretation rather than confirmed fact.

World.title: Wunti Warns Africa Against Repeating Its Oil Mistake
World.content:
Bala Wunti used the 2026 Concordia Annual Summit in New York to warn that Africa’s new mineral wealth, lithium, cobalt and rare earth elements, could easily repeat the mistakes of its crude oil era. Why should anybody listen?

One, because Wunti spent three decades inside Nigeria’s upstream oil sector, serving as Chief Upstream Investment Officer of NUIMS and managing director of NAPIMS and the Petroleum Products Marketing Company. These posts put him in charge of multibillion-dollar national portfolios.

Two, Wunti led the renegotiation of Nigeria’s Deep Offshore Production Sharing Contracts, ending a two-decade stalemate with international oil companies and securing a larger government share of offshore revenue, a rare case of translating resource wealth into measurable returns.

With that history in view, Wunti’s argument returns to focus.

In his opinion, exporting crude while importing refined petroleum creates poverty rather than prosperity; therefore, the same pattern must not define how Africa handles its critical minerals.

For 50 years energy was priced in barrels, he said; for the next 50, it will be priced in kilograms of lithium, cobalt, graphite and rare earth elements. Global demand for battery minerals is rising quickly, and processing capacity, not raw deposits, is becoming the real source of economic advantage.

Wunti also argued that Africa must become a processing partner rather than remain a source of raw material, calling the permanent export of unrefined minerals colonial economics even as he allowed that temporary concentrate exports may sometimes be commercially necessary.

Nigeria’s own gap is instructive. By Wunti’s reasoning, the country has identified 44 critical minerals, but geological indications are not proven reserves backed by internationally recognised data, and investors fund projects, not potential.

World.title: Celebrating Olufemi Salako at Another Milestone
World.content:
Otunba Olufemi Salako turned a year older on October 8, and anyone who has followed Nigerian media over the past decade will recognise why that date mattered beyond his immediate circle.

Salako is the Publisher of Triangle News International, a platform he built from its Ilaro, Ogun State roots into one of Nigeria’s more respected names in investigative journalism. What began as a Nigerian publication now has international headquarters in London.

For the past five years, Salako has organised the Face of Africa Leadership Awards in the United Kingdom, an annual event honouring Africans whose leadership shapes communities and institutions across the continent and its diaspora.

The 2025 edition, marking Triangle’s 10th anniversary, was hosted at the Great Hall of King’s College London’s Strand Campus, placing an African media brand inside one of Britain’s most storied academic venues. The next edition moves to Oxford in April 2027.

What makes Salako’s trajectory worth noting is how deliberately it has moved from reporting stories to convening the people those stories are about. He has presented award nominations directly to traditional rulers, including the Ooni of Ife, thereby placing himself inside rooms most journalists only cover from outside.

That shift from chronicler to convener is not very common in Nigerian media, where publishers often stay fixed to one side of the story. Salako appears to have built a platform flexible enough to do both without losing credibility on either side. His influence now shows up less in individual headlines than in the younger journalists who point to his career as proof that a small Nigerian publication can grow into something with genuine international reach.

As he marks another year, the fair measure of Salako’s milestone is not the awards he has collected but the model he has built: one where African excellence gets a stage, and the stories behind it get told properly.

World.title: Fidelis Ayebae’s Fidson Takes Nigeria’s Healthcare Story Global
World.content:
Fidson Healthcare Plc has been selected to develop and manufacture a generic version of Roche’s influenza antiviral drug, baloxavir marboxil, through a licensing arrangement backed by the Medicines Patent Pool. The deal places founder Fidelis Ayebae’s company among a small group of global manufacturers chosen for the programme.

Ayebae’s path to this point started with an unlikely combination. He earned a Higher National Diploma in Civil Engineering in 1976, later adding an Advanced Diploma in Business Administration from the University of Lagos, before spending years at Citibank ahead of founding Fidson in 1995. This grounding shows in what Fidson has built since.

The company became the first West African manufacturer of indigenous antiretroviral drugs for HIV, alongside proton pump inhibitors and complex infusion formats, the kind of technical record that makes a firm credible for an international deal like this one.

Fidson also became the first Nigerian pharmaceutical company to cross N100 billion in revenue, eventually reaching past N119 billion. Revenue of that size does not arrive from one product but buds off years of reinvestment in plants, regulatory systems, and staff.

Global partnerships followed the same pattern. Fidson worked with Japan’s Ohara Pharmaceutical Company on an oncology expansion and with three Chinese consortiums on an HIV-focused manufacturing hub in the Lekki Free Trade Zone, each deal adding to the track record regulators now rely on.

Under the Roche arrangement, Fidson will receive technical information and reference materials needed to pursue regulatory approval, with the aim of making the drug available in eligible markets at a lower cost.

Recognition has tracked the same climb. In 2025, Ayebae became the youngest person to receive the Nigeria Academy of Pharmacy’s Lifetime Achievement Award, nine years after becoming the first non-pharmacist admitted into the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria’s Hall of Honorary Membership.

World.title: Femi Soneye: The Quiet Force Making a Difference in Nigeria’s Oil and Gas Industry
World.content:
Femi Soneye’s name rarely makes headlines. Yet, for 20 months, he controlled how Nigeria’s national oil company explained itself to the public, serving as Chief Corporate Communications Officer at NNPC Limited during one of its most scrutinised periods.

Soneye took on that role carrying a journalism background built across three continents, having worked in Nigeria, Australia, and the United States before settling into Nigerian public relations, a breadth few domestic communicators can claim.

Before NNPC, he had already built his own media platform, founding and publishing Per Second News, a multimedia outlet that gave him firsthand experience running a newsroom rather than simply advising one. That record earned recognition.

In 2025, the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations named him Spokesperson of the Year, beating communications heads from Shell, NIMASA and the Nigeria Police Force for the title. His standing extends beyond Nigeria. Soneye holds membership in the National Association of Black Journalists and the Society of Professional Journalists in the United States, alongside the Nigerian Union of Journalists at home.

Colleagues trace his working style to ‘Omoluabi,’ the Yoruba standard of integrity and good character, and to his Ijebu Igbo roots, a calm disposition that stood out inside an industry known for aggressive public relations tactics.

The clearest marker of that discipline came in June 2025, when Soneye resigned from NNPC after 20 months in office, choosing to return to journalism and make more room for his family rather than extend a powerful state appointment.

Few communications executives walk away from that kind of post voluntarily. For Soneye, the spirit that drove that decision is the very same instinct that built his reputation in the first place: measured timing over visibility.

Clearly, the man, unlike many on the same path, knows that credibility in communication is built through consistency and restraint rather than constant presence in the news. Little wonder he is outstanding.

World.title: Joseph Tegbe Pushes for Better Electricity Supply, Modern Control Infrastructure
World.content:
Nigeria’s Minister of Power, Joseph Olasunkanmi Tegbe, has pointed to engagements with political stakeholders, advocacy groups, and industry players, along with the groundbreaking of an ultramodern National Control Centre, as proof the government is serious about fixing electricity delivery.

According to Tegbe, the initiatives are part of President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda. The value of a functioning control centre links to grid monitoring and coordination, sitting at the centre of reducing the outages Nigerians have lived with for years.

Tegbe’s background sets him apart from several predecessors who entered the ministry without technical training. He holds a first-class honours degree in Civil Engineering from Obafemi Awolowo University and has advised both the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission and the Nigerian Bulk Electricity Trading Company.

He also spent three decades as Senior Partner and Head of Advisory Services at KPMG Africa, work that exposed him directly to the kind of institutional restructuring Nigeria’s power sector still badly needs.

His early moves have leaned cautious. Rather than promising nationwide 24-hour power, he launched a 24/7 Energy Zones pilot in Lagos, aiming to fix localised failures first before attempting anything at national scale.

Of course, that caution has not shielded him from criticism.

Tegbe’s ministry had to publicly deny reports that he promised to end grid collapses within three months, an early stumble that undercut his carefully built technocratic image. Moreover, some analysts question whether his boardroom instincts favour polished corporate responses over urgent crisis management. Centralised call centres for electricity complaints, one of his first announcements, struck several commentators as too small for the scale of the problem.

A more awkward issue trails him politically. Tegbe ran for office before, including a 2019 Oyo governorship bid and a failed 2023 Senate run, switching parties along the way, a history that invites doubt about where his loyalties ultimately sit.

The deepest obstacle, though, predates him. Nigeria’s power sector carries over N100 billion in legacy debt and entrenched energy theft, the same structural weight that has worn down every technocrat who came before him.

All of this to say that with Tegbe, there is more to come. And a lot of it with careful thinking on his part.

World.title: Siya Kolisi has emotional reunion with Sharks pals [video]
World.content:
Siya Kolisi had an emotional reunion with his former Sharks colleagues, including “bestie” Eben Etzebeth, after recently returning to his home at the Stormers.

The 35-year-old made his comeback to the Cape Town club last week in Edinburgh. For the first time in five years, Siya donned a Stormers jersey at the DHL Stadium this weekend.

The Stormers beat the visiting team 39-22.

SIYA KOLISI HAS EMOTIONAL REUNION WITH SHARKS COLLEAGUES

After the final whistle blew, signalling the Stormers’ URC match victory against the Sharks, Siya Kolisi rushed over to embrace his opponents, who were once his colleagues.



The rugby hero warmly embraced players like Vincent Koch, Ox Nche, Jurenzo Julius, and his Springbok bestie, Eben Etzebeth.

Rugby fans commented that the moment signalled that the players were opponents on the pitch, but “brothers” off of it.

Take a look…

Just moments before, Siya performed cartwheels on the pitch after scoring a try in the first few minutes of the game.



RETURN TO STORMERS

According to Stormers boss John Dobson, Siya Kolisi cut short his Springbok break to fly across the world from Australia to join the Stormers in Edinburgh last week.

Siya had been released by Springboks coach Rassie Erasmus ahead of the national team’s match against the Wallabies last month.



The Boks captain used the opportunity to bond with his home team, who played Edinburgh Rugby. Siya managed to get in the game time, marking his 119th cap for the Stormers franchise and his first appearance for the club in over five years.

Dobson said of Siy Kolisia’s decision: “Actions speak louder than words. It came from him, the call to join us, and I think it’s been invaluable, because of the bridging with the Springboks, and just who he is. He is such a good presence in the team – cheerful, smiling, fooling around.”

World.title: First look: Meet Mr and Mrs Dricus du Plessis!
World.content:
Dricus du Plessis and Vasti Spiller are officially husband and wife! The couple tied the knot in a picturesque wedding in the Western Cape on Saturday, 10 October.

The MMA fighter and his boxing coach partner have been dating since 2023.

FIRST LOOK: DRICUS DU PLESSIS AND VASTI SPILLER WEDDING

On her Instagram Stories, Vasti Spiller has shared a first look at her wedding day to Dricus du Plessis.



The couple wed at a picturesque venue in Paarl in the Western Cape.

Vasti wore a custom Anel Botha creation during the ceremony, while Dricus wore a crisp black tuxedo.

The blonde bride changed into an Amara Bespoke gown, adorned with sequins and pearls, for the reception, and her husband donned a cream blazer to match her.

The wedding was attended by the couple’s close family and friends, with entertainment including the likes of Bobby van Jaarsveld and Ricus Nel.

Take a look at the first images from the day…

Inside Dricus du Plessis and Vasti Spiller’s wedding day.

Images via IG

PRAISE FOR ‘UNDERSTANDING PARTNER’

Dricus du Plessis and Vasti Spiller met at the CIT Boxing in Hatfield, Pretoria, in 2023, where he trained, and she worked as a boxing coach.



They crossed paths after Vasti pursued boxing coaching a year earlier.

Fast forward to 2025, Dricus and Vasti announced their engagement.

Speaking to KFM about their relationship, the former UFC World Champion praised his partner for being supportive and empathetic to his career.

He said: “I kind of feel sorry for her because it’s like she’s dating two different human beings… when a fight comes around, it’s such a selfish sport and everything needs to go around this fight, and what needs to happen for me, so everything else takes a backseat – family, friends, everything.

“Because you have to give it your all, and it’s amazing to have a partner understanding all of that.”

World.title: R10 million Cape Town townhouse listing goes viral [video]
World.content:
A R10 million Cape Town duplex listing has gone viral on social media. Images via IG

A R10,5 million listing for a property on the outskirts of Sea Point has gone viral. For many South Africans, the price tag is more proof of the city’s overpriced property market

CAPE TOWN PROPERTY LISING GOES VIRAL

On her social media accounts, Pasha Dos Santos, a luxury real estate agent of

Pasha Property Global shared a look inside her latest listing – a fully–furnished townhouse located on the outskirts of Sea Point and Green Point.



Pasha described the three-bedroom Victorian-style home as “the best of both worlds” in reference to its location

She revealed the property was currently operating as an Airbnb with a “4,89 star rating”.

In the comments section, South Africans unanimously agreed that the house was “overpriced” and would sell for much less in other parts of the city.



“This is satire, right?” commented a social media user, while another added, “Not even worth two million”.

A third shared: “We South Africans are not the target market”

Pasha liked a comment saying that real estate agents get the “flak” for “embarrassing” Cape Town property listings.



WHY IS IT SO EXPENSIVE?

Residential areas like Sea Point, Camps Bay, Clifton, and Green Point, ie on the Atlantic Seaboard, have seen a rapid rise in property values.

This can be attributed to the city’s gentrification, where in-demand real estate replaces and displaces lower-income, and typically non-white communities.

With the influence of foreign investors and digital nomads, living in Cape Town can cost a fortune.



According to Cape Business News, Sea Point, in particular, is an in-demand location for many South Africans and tourists, thanks to its proximity to both the beach and mountains.

The African Investor reported: “The type of people attracted to Sea Point is quite diverse. It appeals to young professionals, international expatriates, and retirees alike.

“The area’s cosmopolitan nature, combined with its accessibility to Cape Town’s business district, makes it ideal for those working in the city but wishing to live by the sea.



“Furthermore, its safety, amenities, and quality of life are factors that attract a more affluent demographic.”

Apart from serving as a residential area, the area is also home to retail, restaurants, and service facilities.

World.title: Lebo M campaigns for ActionSA, says ANC ‘destroyed’ South Africa
World.content:
Lebohang Morake, or Lebo M, is using his platform to campaign for ActionSA and its leader, Herman Mashaba, ahead of next month’s local government elections. The Lion King composer has withdrawn his support for the ANC, whom he claims he has voted for since the first democratic election in 1994.

LEBO M SHOWS SUPPORT TO ACTIONSA, HERMAN MASHABA

In videos posted on his X account, Lebo M officially endorsed ActionSA and its leader Herman Mashaba.

The 62-year-old spoke from Singapore, where he has joined fellow music composer Hans Zimmer on tour. He said: “I am voting and supporting ActionSA. I do hope ActionSA and ATM (African Transformation Movement) find a way to bridge the gap and release us from this treacherous last 32 years that have destroyed our country and put us in jeopardy”.



Lebo revealed he would no longer be voting for the ANC.

He continued: “Some of us have a role to play. Vote ActionSA. I’ve given over 20 years of my vote to these other brothers who have destroyed the country. I have a strong snse of anger against my government, I have earned the right to hold my government accountable.

The Lion King musical genius accused the ANC of “abusing the rights” of South Africans who voted for them and “creating billionaires from corruption”. 

I standby by my earned right to criticize my government in South Africa. Hyenas will always bring noise for diversion. I will defend my heritage and culture, my legacy. I will defend my children’s future and hold our politicians accountable. I LIVE in South Africa @actionsa 🇿🇦 pic.twitter.com/jy4NGhJ60q — Lebo M (@therealLEBO_M) October 10, 2026

HIGH-PROFILE PEOPLE WHO SUPPORT THE POLITICAL PARTY

Lebo M’s public support of ActionSA comes shortly after The Ultimatum South Africa reality star Lehlohonolo “Nolla” Moseko announced that he would have joined the political party and would be running as ward councillor in his local district.

Other notable ActionSA supporters include:

Moja Love presenter Xolani Khumalo, who is the mayoral candidate for the City of Ekurhuleni.

Muvhango actor Gabriel Temudzani

Prominent lawyer Tumi Sole

World.title: Alison Botha revisits her horror attack: ‘It’s a miracle I survived’
World.content:
Alison Botha has opened up about her attack, Images via IG

Alison Botha has bravely chosen to revisit her horror attack in 1994, where she was brutally raped, assaulted and left for dead, in the hopes of inspiring other women.

Her injuries were severe – the Gqeberha woman had been disembowelled and had her throat slit when she crawled for help through a remote field to a nearby road.

Shockingly, her attackers – Frans du Toit and Theuns Kruger – were released on parole in 2023. A few months later, their parole was revoked by the Minister of Correctional Services, Pieter Groenewald, following public backlash.



ALISON REVISTS TRAUMATIC ATTACK

On her social media platforms, Alison Botha has posted short clips of her recounting her 1994 ordeal

Thus far, she has released two parts: one about her abduction and another about the gruesome attack.

Alison recalled her sexual assault, being strangled and blacking out, during which time she was disembowelled and had her throat slit.

“It’s a miracle I survived these injuries..I just played dead while they moved around”, she recalled.

Of her decision to speak out about the traumatic incident, Alison has shared: “I don’t want to offend anyone, but I believe we can’t always shy away from the hard topics. We can’t move away from trauma unless we look at it and see what we can learn from it and move on

She hopes her words will inspire other women



ATTACK TO STRESS-INDUCED ANEURYSM

In 2024, Alison Botha suffered a brain aneurysm, caused by the stress that her attackers, Frans du Toit and Theuns Kruger, had been given an early release on parole just months before, after they kidnapped, raped and left her for dead.

According to Alison’s legal advisors, she was not consulted in the parole process. Instead, she was notified of the men’s release in 2023 by telephone.

Last year, Minister of Correctional Services Pieter Groenewald revoked the parole of Alison Botha’s attackers. Both offenders have been reincarcerated and will remain in custody.

The men were sentenced to life imprisonment in 1995, a year after their brutal attack.

At the time, Pretoria High Court Judge Chris Jansen, who sentenced them, said during his judgement: “I needed to make it clear they were a threat to society and should never be released.”

World.title: Roosevelt High School principal defended over ‘Hitler’ comment
World.content:
The public have defended Roosevelt High School's principal against racism allegations. Images via Facebook

Pastor Curt van Heerden’s comments chastising Roosevelt High School principal Cristèl Venter, who likened her actions in shutting down a Matric Dance disaster event to that of Adolf Hitler, have been met with strong resistance from the public.

The Johannesburg school has come under fire after Venter’s viral open letter condemning a handful of Grade 12 learners for underage drinking, drug use, and a firearm incident at the event, which took place at Avianto Hotel in Muldersdrift.

ROOSEVELT HIGH SCHOOL: PRINCIPAL QUESTIONED OVER ‘HITLER COMPARISON’

In a Facebook post, Pastor Curt van Heerden called for Roosevelt High School to refund ticket sales after principal Cristèl Venter shut down the Matric Dance early due to allegations of learner misconduct.



Van Heerden, a social media community activist, supported his argument by quoting Avianto Hotel, which claimed that Venter had decided to cut the event short.

The venue also disputed allegations that learners were served alcohol, damaged property or that a firearm incident involved minors.

He also quoted several parents and learners, who were left disappointed and frustrated at the sequence of events.

The preacher and social media influencer also chastised Venter over a screenshot of her WhatsApp status comparing herself to German dictator Adolf Hitler.

The status, which came after the principal learned of the Matric Dance fiasco, read:

“I am an extremely embarrassed principal, when parents pull firearms at the poor Avianto staff and Grad 12 learners pitch up drink as can be and vomit all over the bathroom 

“Stick a fork in me, I am done. This will be the last one. Class of 2026, can you be any bigger of a disappointment? Your marks are horrendous, and then you can’t even behave.

Venter added the hashtag “#Hitlerloading”

Curt van Heerden claimed that the hashtag hinted at racial undertones.

He asked: “Why would the principal of Roosevelt High School – who is white – put this on her status? What was she trying to say?”

PUBLIC DEFENDS PRINCIPAL

Curt van Heerden’s insinuation was met with opposition from many of his followers, who disagreed with his sentiment in the comment section.

Here’s what a few had to say…

Angelo Major: The hashtag was not intended to be racist. In my opinion, she was saying she would need to be ruthless in her actions, like Hitler was in his actions, in order to take control of the sh!t show that was going on. While the reference to Hitler is completely inappropriate, let’s not make this about a white woman being racist. This is about kids getting out of hand and the unfortunate reality that the consequences affected everyone”

Maxine Cero Louw: “I stand with the principal. Not everything has to be an issue. Things should not be taken out of context. Great job, principal”

Estelle Kriek Venter: “Why do you stand up for those children? This is why they behave so badly: no accountability. That woman teaches them a life lesson about consequences. Stop vilifying her”.

WHAT HAPPENED AT ROOSEVELT HIGH SCHOOL’S MATRIC DANCE?

In a lengthy open letter posted on the school’s official Facebook page last week, Roosevelt High School principal Cristèl Venter expressed her shock and disappointment at the behaviour of some learners who attended the Matric Dance at the Avianto Hotel in Muldersdrift.

Venter had initially skipped the event due to illness, but had been called in to intervene after things took a turn for the worse.

Venter revealed that learners had arrived under the influence of alcohol and drugs, and that one particular entourage had threatened staff with firearms during their rowdy procession and reckless driving into the venue. Intoxicated learners reportedly became violently ill, vomiting all over the five-star venue.

The principal decided to cut short the Matric Dance in a bid to de-escalate the deteriorating situation, but was met with contempt and verbal abuse from parents, who angrily confronted school staff.

Venter vowed to launch an investigation into the incident and hold a disciplinary hearing for those involved.

A few days later, podcaster Penuel Mlotshwa addressed the school learners, urging them to exercise responsibility and accountability.

When approached for comment, principal Cristèl Venter stated that she was not authorised to speak to the media.

The school has since disabled its social media platforms.

World.title: Sundowns star reveals his brother was stabbed
World.content:
Teboho Mokoena celebrates scoring for Mamelodi Sundowns against Orlando Pirates in the 2026 MTN8 final at the Moses Mabhida Stadium. Image: Official PSL

Following Sundowns’ triumph in the MTN8 final over Orlando Pirates, Mokoena revealed that he has been dealing with the emotional struggles.

The Bethlehem-born star dedicated his goal to his late grandfather and his brother who remains in hospital.

MAMELODI SUNDOWNS STAR TEBOHO MOKOENA ADMITS TO EMOTIONAL TURMOIL

“It’s been tough two weeks for me, I lost my grandfather two weeks ago,” Mokoena told SuperSport TV after the game.



“I almost lost my brother who got stabbed the day before we played Guinea. They stabbed him multiple times, it’s been tough, but I’d like to dedicate this game to him, he is in the hospital bed. I hope justice will be served.”

The 29-year-old admitted that he has struggled emotionally despite continuing to represent his country on the pitch.

“I’m happy that we but inside I’m not really okay because it’s sad what happened to my family and you always have to show up doesn’t matter how you’re feeling.”

“I dedicate this game to him, my brother and I hope he recovers.”

KEY PLAYER FOR THE AFRICAN CHAMPIONS

Mokoena has established himself as a key figure in the Sundowns midfield since joining the club from SuperSport United in January 2022. He has marked 110 appearances, scoring 14 goals and providing 9 assists across all competitions.

Operating as a deep-lying midfielder, Mokoena plays a crucial role in controlling the tempo, winning possession and transitioning the team from defence to attack.



During the 2022/23 season, Mokoena made 27 league appearances, scoring one goal and providing two assists. He improved his attacking output in the 2023/24 campaign, registering three goals and three assists in 18 league matches. He remained a regular in the starting lineup during the 2024/25 and 2025/26 seasons, adding a combined five league goals and three assists.

Mokoena’s contributions have also helped Sundowns enjoy considerable success. He has won three Premier Soccer League titles (2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24), one Nedbank Cup (2022) and the inaugural African Football League title in 2023. His outstanding performances during the 2022/23 season also earned him the PSL Footballer of the Season award.

World.title: Ouaddou explains why Lungu took penalty ahead of Appollis against Sundowns
World.content:
Orlando Pirates head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou has explained why Ghampani Lungu stepped up to take a penalty during the Buccaneers’ 2-0 defeat to Mamelodi Sundowns in the MTN8 final on Saturday.

The Zambian international had an opportunity to bring Pirates back into the game after Teboho Mokoena conceded a penalty. However, Lungu’s effort was saved by Sundowns goalkeeper Ronwen Williams.

At the time, Downs were leading 1-0 and had he scored, the goal would have changed the match.



Lungu’s decision to take the spot-kick raised questions among Pirates fans, with many believing Oswin Appollis should have stepped up instead, having regularly taken penalties last season.

After the match, Ouaddou clarified that Lungu was among the club’s designated penalty takers and was first in the pecking order for the opportunity.

Lungu’s penalty miss cost Pirates MTN8

“He [Lungu] is one of the designated takers. Of the players, he was first among the takers. After him, we have Appollis, we have…” Ouaddou said.

Despite the disappointment of losing the final, the Pirates coach acknowledged Sundowns’ victory and insisted his side would continue working hard.

“It’s moments like that, it’s football. We have to respect.

“Congratulations to Mamelodi Sundowns. Of course, we are disappointed, but in football, you have to be fair play.



“For us, we have to continue to work, and people are going to see a fantastic season because we are not going to give up.

“And we are going to try to keep our title,” he added.

Many Bucs fans feel Lungu should allowed Appollis to take the penalty given his experience. Appollis has scored crucial spotkicks for both club and country in the past.

Who should have taken that penalty?

World.title: Four killed in KwaMsane tavern
World.content:
ESHOWE – A police constable allegedly shot and killed three women and injured a man before turning the gun on himself at a tavern in KwaMsane, KwaZulu-Natal.

Police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said police responded to reports of a shooting at a liquor establishment at Nkodibe area in KwaMsane, and when they arrived they found four bodies with gunshot wounds, and one victim with a gunshot wound who was taken to hospital.

“It was reported that the off-duty police constable also disarmed another man of his firearm during the incident. Both firearms were found at the scene. The cause of the shooting is unknown at this stage.”

In a separate incident, police in Eshowe are tracing a suspect who allegedly shot and killed three people at a grocery chain store in Eshowe on Saturday.

“Reports indicate that the suspect, who is former employee of the store, had gone to the store for his internal disciplinary hearing. The suspect allegedly produced a firearm and shot three people who were declared dead at the scene. A manhunt for the suspect is underway.”

World.title: SANDF arrives in Durban
World.content:
DURBAN - The army has been spotted in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, amid tensions over asylum applications and illegal immigration.

Protests erupted after the Constitutional Court ruling that everyone must be given a fair chance to apply for asylum, regardless of documentation.

Violent unrest led to looting and the torching of vehicles.

Government has called for calm as tensions simmer.

World.title: Joburg Water warns of possible outages
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A power outage at the Zuikerbosch Water Treatment Plant has crippled pumping at the Palmiet Booster Station.

Johannesburg Water warns that parts of Sandton, Diepsloot, Rabie Ridge, and surrounding areas could face low water pressure or total outages.

The utility said it is monitoring the system and taking steps to stabilise supply.

Residents are urged to use water sparingly.

World.title: ‘Captured’ casts spotlight on prison life
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Ex-Pollsmoor Correctional Centre inmates are using visual art to depict the realities of life behind bars.

This they say helps them deal with past trauma, their reintegration into society, and also to make a living.

Dubbed "Captured", the visual storytelling project, is set to eventually become a coffee table book.

Life behind bars is often reduced to statistics, without the human factor.

Enrico Samuels, an artist, served sixteen years behind bars for armed robbery said art connected him with people helping him to navigate life now as a free man.

"I want to become a successful artist, doctor is helping me to get there with the projects...lovely projects and I enjoy myself in the projects and from there I see a brighter future from doc's side, because she is taking me that way, so I can see the sun on the other side already,” said Samuels.

Michael Sauls said art serves as a conduit in helping them deal with their past and educate the public.

“People have no an idea of what prison is like, they think that everything is happy go-lucky or it's like a journey to another paradise, it's not worth it being there...you see it's easy to commit a crime, but it's not easy serving the time."

Dr Suzette Leal, the founder of Words Set Free, said the art tells the stories of the people behind it.

"If you say the work is beautiful, that's a complement to our artists and their ability, but the story is not beautiful. It's real and true and painful and traumatic. So, I think if anything I hope it discourages someone from getting involved in crime, but I think we don't reduce crime by making prison sentences longer or by making the conditions within them worse. We reduce crime by creating opportunities for people to create a livelihood outside of crime.”

Another artist, Kleinbooi Hendricks said: "I said to myself, although the parole board gave me a date to go out of prison, I'm not going. I will either complete my entire sentence but I'm not going out if I haven't worked on myself being a changed man or a different person. I did that because I said I'd either eat out of a dustbin outside, but I'm not going to commit crime again."

World.title: Change living conditions – Ndlozi
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Real change begins with communities taking responsibility for their own development.

Those are the views of Dr Mbuyiseni Ndlozi, Founder of the Batho Pele Convention.

The initiative calls on South Africans to take the lead in improving their own living conditions.

“We are here to say you are the solution you are looking for. We are here to say you are the saviour, the developer, the healer and the builder you are looking for. We are here to vote for you to do it on your own.

“We are here to say you are the saviours you are looking for. We are not a corporate think tank. Long have we interpreted our misery from broadcast to podcast, think shops to talk shops.

“The point is to change our living conditions, one pothole at a time, one classroom at a time and one production hub at a time,” Ndlozi said.

World.title: Repairs delay Joburg's pool reopenings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Johannesburg's public pools are missing out on the summer rush.

And most are still closed despite the rising temperatures.

Community leader Dulton Adams said poor planning, lack of proper budgeting and no clear management plans, are leaving residents without these facilities.

The city has 57 public pools, but only 13 are open so far.

Ten more are expected to open on Monday.

"Every season there's just no budget.

There's just no management plan. There's no vision to make sure that the children come off the streets and you look at the pool. This is not the only pool.

"Remember spring day, pools must open first. Then the City Council asked for 1 October, pools would be open. That was missed and then now the 7th," Adams said.

World.title: ‘ANC could be the biggest loser’ - political strategist
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The ANC could emerge as the biggest loser in this year's municipal elections.

This is the view is political strategist Brutus Malada.

He said the party’s declining support could leave it with less influence across key metros and this could push it into a weakened position ahead of the 2029 elections.

“ANC will be the big loser in this. The trend is clear. It's clear that they are losing at a margin of 10 to 12 percent and that will actually mean the end of the ANC and it will become lame duck for this period in between the two elections.

“That it will sit, it will be a national government President Ramaphosa sitting in Tshwane. The Union Buildings which is led by another party and in Cape Town which is the legislative arm of the state which is led by the DA.

“So here is a political party that is running the country as the head of the State but it has no control of the economy hub, it has no control of administrative hub, it has no control of legislative hub,” Malada said.

World.title: Murdered teen twins buried in Mamelodi
World.content:
Mamelodi – The family and friends of the slain 14-year-old twins have gathered in Mamelodi West to bid farewell to the boys.

Bonolo and Botlhale Makena were found dead in their home a week ago. They had multiple stab wounds.

The boys' mother made the gruesome discovery at home, when she returned from work.

As police investigate, residents are demanding that this case does not become another unresolved killing.

Neighobour Padi Matlala said the Mamelodi West community is demanding justice.

“The community has been here before. The community is saying, ‘please justice system, don't take us there.’ We were there in 1982. Two members of the community were brutally murdered. 44 years later, nobody has been held responsible.

“The community is saying justice system never, never again should you go through this. The pressure that you put on the government throughout the week, the outrage you showed must bear fruit. Somebody or some people must be held responsible for this. We are better than this,” Matlala said.
