World.title: Say cheese: A guide to 5 iconic Mexican quesos and the regions that produce them
World.content:
In Mexico, an endless debate spills across social media and enlists everyone from linguists and historians to cooks and passionate eaters: What belongs in a quesadilla? While cheese is an optional topping for many Mexican dishes — from tacos and tortas to chilaquiles and sopes — there is one contentious item that, depending on who you ask, is non-negotiable.

Now, we are not here to solve the great quesadilla debate, but unveiling the passion behind it shows just how central cheese is to Mexican gastronomy. From north to south, every region has crafted its own variety of queso tailored to its local heritage. Here are five of Mexico’s most iconic cheeses:

Queso Oaxaca (or quesillo)

The cheese at the very heart of the debate — and a cornerstone of Mexican street food — is queso Oaxaca, locally known as quesillo. It is celebrated for its soft, buttery texture and its exceptional meltability over high heat, whether tucked into a sope, folded inside a quesadilla or pressed into a torta.

What differentiates quesillo from other cheeses is its distinct curdling method: It is hand-stretched into long, milky strands and wound into a ribboned ball. Achieving this pliable texture relies on warm preparation techniques that keep the cheese flexible enough to stretch and interlace without breaking.

Quesillo is indispensable in Mexican households as it can turn a simple tortilla (corn or flour) into a quick homemade quesadilla for dinner, transform refried beans and bread into crispy, freshly baked molletes, or serve as a quick, savory snack eaten straight from the fridge.

Originally from: Oaxaca

Queso de cincho

Loosely translated as “cinch cheese,” queso de cincho originates in the central state of Morelos and the southwestern state of Guerrero. Its name refers to the rigid mold used during pressing, which is bound tightly with woven ixtle palm fibers (the same durable rope material used in traditional horse tack and saddlery).

Also known as queso prensado estilo Guerrero, this firm, aged cheese carries a strong aroma and is typically rubbed with a paste of dried guajillo chiles. While frequently crumbled over enchiladas or chilaquiles, one of its most traditional preparations is simmered directly in salsa as a guisado. Thanks to its dense consistency and high protein content, it serves as a substantial centerpiece. Better yet, its low moisture content allows it to age naturally at room temperature for up to a year without spoiling.

Originally from: Guerrero and Morelos

Queso asadero

Just like quesillo, queso asadero is popular due to its creamy, melty texture and the gastronomic possibilities it offers. This type of cheese has similar uses to queso Oaxaca; it can be used in quesadillas, and it is common at northern cookouts, paired with a great steak. If you’ve been to one of those, the name “asadero” might sound familiar — it comes from the word asado (grilled), a clue on how to enjoy this cheese.

Originally from: Chihuahua

Queso fresco

View this post on Instagram A post shared by 𝑪𝒂𝒔𝒂𝒏𝒅𝒓𝒂 𝑺𝒂𝒍𝒊𝒏𝒂𝒔 🤠🌵 (@yo_soy_casandra)

Queso fresco is a crumbly, soft cheese that is high in moisture and protein. Due to its short aging process (which is where the name fresco — or fresh — comes from), it is difficult to keep for long periods. It must always be kept refrigerated and consumed within approximately two weeks.

Regarding its preparation and curdling, queso fresco is quite versatile, as it can be made with cow’s milk, goat’s milk or a blend of both. In contrast to meltable cheeses, queso fresco does not work as a quesadilla filling, but it is the perfect topping for side dishes, whether sprinkled over a salad, street corn or refried beans.

Originally from: Chihuahua

Queso Menonita

View this post on Instagram A post shared by ¡ah Chihuahua! (@ahchihuahua)

Last but not least is Mennonite cheese, a famous variety that also comes from the northern region of the country. As its name reveals, it originates from a specific community: the Mennonites. Groups of Mennonite immigrants arrived in Mexico during the 1920s, and their cattle-ranching techniques thrived in the north.

Mennonite communities settled mainly in the drylands of Chihuahua and relied on dairy products, especially cheese, for sustenance. Nowadays — although the name remains — this smooth, buttery cheese is no longer exclusively made by Mennonite communities. You can find it melting inside chiles rellenos, on Mennonite-style pizzas or in choriqueso (a dish of melted cheese combined with seasoned chorizo).

Originally from: Chihuahua

Cheese has been a companion to Mexican cuisine for centuries. One key to understanding its strong northern presence is the geographic distribution of agriculture and livestock in Mexico. As you travel from south to north, the climate becomes drier, making the land better suited for cattle ranching than crop cultivation.

It is no surprise, then, that cheese became a fundamental pillar of northern Mexico’s economy and gastronomy.

After all, what would a northern carne asada be without quesadillas (con queso)?

Lydia Leija is a linguist, journalist and visual storyteller. She has directed three feature films, and her audiovisual work has been featured in national and international media. She’s been part of National Geographic, Muy Interesante and Cosmopolitan.

World.title: Does having dual citizenship have any downsides?
World.content:
In 2016, my wife and I embarked on a road trip together across central Mexico — starting on Jalisco’s Pacific Coast and, over a month later, ending up on the Gulf Coast of Veracruz with innumerable side quests along the way in Michoacán, Guanajuato, Querétaro, Hidalgo, Mexico City, Estado de México and Puebla.

It wasn’t our first time in Mexico. We had, after all, spent our lifetimes visiting our extended families in Mexico as the children of immigrants.

But now we were able to see it on our own terms, as independent adults with our own incomes to spend and itineraries to plan. We rediscovered the country through our own eyes.

That summer, we had a revelation: We wanted to live in Mexico.

Three years later, in 2019, we prepared a similar trek around the southern part of the country, beginning in Oaxaca’s capital, then winding our way through mountain towns en route to the coast on a colectivo. Months prior, we had left our jobs as high school teachers with the intent to live in Mexico long term. Then, COVID-19 happened while we were staying in Mexico City’s central Narvarte Poniente neighborhood.

It was an uncertain and frightening time to be traveling. We ultimately decided, as U.S. citizens with a travel visa, to return to California after nearly half a year away. As tourists, we would have violated our 180-day limit and didn’t want to risk overstaying; had we been dual citizens, we would have had less pressure to return so suddenly.

Navigating the consulate and paperwork

But we hadn’t given up on our ambitions to live in Mexico as Mexican Americans. Shortly after returning to the San Francisco region, I began my application process to become a dual Mexican citizen.

In my case, I had a major advantage: My mom never rescinded her Mexican citizenship, despite having lived in the United States for more than 30 years after immigrating as a young woman. When she eventually moved back to Mexico, it inspired me to follow her southward. Through her, my direct path to citizenship had already been laid out.

The process took me a couple of years, though it could have been completed much more swiftly. I took my time and wasn’t in a rush during the pandemic. I visited different consulates in California, and after waiting in many lines and talking to many people, I gathered all of the documents — most importantly, proof of my mother’s citizenship and birth certificate — and approvals.

Then, it happened: I had become a Mexican citizen, and I had my Mexican passport. (I would eventually get my INE, but I opted to do it in Mexico, rather than at any Mexican consulate in the U.S.).

My wife had a trickier path. Her Mexican-born father’s documents had a typo. Therefore, some of his documents didn’t exactly match. If you aren’t yet familiar with the distress an aberrant punctuation mark can trigger in the imperfect machinery of Mexican bureaucracy, I pray you never have to.

Ultimately, my wife was forced to hire a specialist who helps Mexican descendants obtain their Mexican citizenship — it was frictionless and worth the price. To date, we highly recommend it for anyone who has the funding or has experienced any complications with the process.

A historic surge in binational applicants

During that time, we weren’t alone in our journeys toward Mexican citizenship. Many of our Mexican American friends had expressed a desire to do the same, and in some cases, a few had already started their processes as well. In fact, dual citizenship applications — particularly for the U.S.-born descendants of Mexican immigrants — are reaching a historic apex. De Los, a Latino-focused branch of the Los Angeles Times, recently reported that “Between 2024 and 2025, registrations for Mexican citizenship skyrocketed by 161% at the Los Angeles consulate.”

The trend is universal throughout the U.S. In Boise, Idaho, reports indicate a rise in applicants due to Mexico’s law change in 2023, which simplified the route to dual citizenship for anyone with at least one Mexican-born parent. Combined with the ongoing pressures of xenophobic turmoil, immigration raids and other sociopolitical factors, more people are looking to gain a sense of security and connection on both sides of the border through binational citizenship.

The benefits of dual citizenship are certainly ample: Traveling as a dual citizen offers financial breaks and accessibility perks (there are fewer foreign fees to be paid at Mexican airports and museums, for example); purchasing property in Mexico involves fewer legal hurdles; and at large, it grants unrestricted freedoms on both sides of the border, which is an ultimate privilege.

The unexpected costs of double bureaucracy

But that’s where things can get a little complicated, depending on your plans and lifestyle. In my case, I don’t use my Mexican passport solely for a beach getaway once a year; I live and work in Mexico as a dual citizen, with employers and responsibilities in both countries, and the implications are different.

Vehicle registration in California expired and needs to be updated in person? Guess who’s flying back for a visit to the California Department of Motor Vehicles? Navigating Mexico’s monthly tax payments? Might require a tax accountant. Of course, each scenario comes with a cost, and many life lessons.

When I applied for dual citizenship, I wasn’t necessarily thinking about those realities, or how I would have to pay and renew double the amount of things as someone fully integrated into two federal systems. Of course, in retrospect it makes complete sense. But it’s not the sort of thing that a bright-eyed applicant has at the forefront of their mind while pursuing dual citizenship — nor is it the kind of thing that parents or friends who are encouraging dual citizenship are thinking about, either.

Political debates and balancing two worlds

The issue of dual citizenship has even caused some political strife. Just weeks ago, President Claudia Sheinbaum proposed a ban on dual citizens being able to reach the highest levels of office within Mexico’s borders. “Why have dual nationality if you’re going to represent the people of Mexico?” she rhetorically posed. The bill has been criticized by the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) as a discriminatory human rights violation.

However, for the average person who doesn’t intend to run for the Mexican presidency, dual citizens generally don’t have much to shy away from. If you plan to work in both countries as a dual citizen, be prepared to pay the taxes (literally and metaphorically). If you don’t plan to work in Mexico for Mexican-based companies, you can simply declare your non-working status in Mexico when registering for your INE, and your biggest potential taxation headaches will disappear — at least in one of the two countries.

The benefits

For all of its potential downsides, there are double the benefits. On days when I enter the U.S. through California airports and switch over to using English with my U.S. passport, it feels like I’m home. I’m just as happy and relieved as soon as I arrive back in Mexico, activate my Spanish mode, and show my Mexican passport.

As someone who grew up around many undocumented Mexican immigrants in California, I don’t take that lightly. And I use it to constantly toggle my way between both worlds, as my fullest self.

Alan Chazaro is the author of “These Spaceships Weren’t Built For Us” (Tia Chucha Press, 2026), “Notes from the Eastern Span of the Bay Bridge” (Ghost City Press, 2021), “Piñata Theory” (Black Lawrence Press, 2020), and “This Is Not a Frank Ocean Cover Album” (Black Lawrence Press, 2019). He is a graduate of June Jordan’s Poetry for the People program at UC Berkeley and was selected as a Lawrence Ferlinghetti Poetry Fellow at the University of San Francisco. His work can be found in NPR, The Guardian, SLAM, GQ, L.A. Times, and more. He is currently based in Veracruz.

World.title: ‘A Pilgrimage Across Cultures’: Tamanna Bembenek on finding her third space in Mexico
World.content:
A couple of decades ago, I became fascinated by the concept of the “third place,” which Howard Schultz, then CEO of Starbucks, helped make popular. The idea came from sociologist Ray Oldenburg: a gathering place outside home and work. Maybe it was all marketing, but Starbucks wanted to define its cafés as neutral ground — a place to meet a friend, study or socialize without the usual expectations of home or work. Starbucks was never quite that place for me, but I remained fascinated by the concept. At the time, I interpreted it as a judgment-free space. As I grew older, the term stuck with me but I began to discover another meaning for myself — less about a place to go and more about the freedom to simply be. That is a feeling I have come to call “my third space.” Let me explain what I mean.

In the last few years, I’ve been thinking a lot about the concept in the context of belonging. I’ve always felt fortunate to have lived and worked in multiple countries, because it let me cherry-pick the best aspects and values from different cultures — and do so in a uniquely American way. Individuality is a value I’ve fiercely cherished, yet that same fierceness has made me feel more alone in recent years.

As the political divide has grown in the U.S., I felt I had to pick a political side to satisfy a psychological need to belong with a group of friends or family. As time passed, my identity became tethered to a party rather than to the values it claimed to represent. Social media compounded this, sorting everyone into ever-narrower boxes: age bracket, income bracket, zip code, follower count, which side of a hashtag someone landed on, or generational labels — Gen Alpha, Gen Z, millennials, Gen X, baby boomers, and I’m sure I’ve missed a few. It felt increasingly claustrophobic. Instead of feeling free to choose the values and characteristics that would nurture my own identity as a good human first — regardless of any other labels — I felt I had to fit into someone else’s box, under a category they had defined. Add geopolitical craziness and the current noise around artificial intelligence (AI), including claims that there is a 10% chance that AI will “kill all humans,” and I started feeling not only alone but increasingly anxious and hopeless!

So, I started reading books and listening to podcasts to figure out the root cause of this feeling and how to remedy it. I was already dedicating quality time to pursuing art but increasingly, I also found myself drawn to ancient history — Roman, Egyptian, Indian, Mesoamerican, just to start with. I noticed that exploring stories about ancient civilizations made me feel less alone. It felt soothing. Whether I was reading history or the myths woven through it, I was searching for common themes, a connection, a sense of belonging. There’s a timeless quality to such stories that reminds us of our own mortality and, paradoxically, makes us feel less alone in facing it.

Slowly, I found myself weaving these stories into my art through the use of icons, symbols and allegory. I started visualizing and composing art in my mind — integrating these concepts with my love and knowledge of art history and modern art, my reverence for the ancient craft of handwoven textiles, and my deep interest in astronomy and life sciences.

I have to admit that my current environment is what made all of this possible. Living in Mexico gave me the space I needed: regardless of nationality, identity, or age, I could simply live and let live. Maybe it helps to be geographically so close to the country I truly love and yet not feel so boxed in. Slowly, I began to understand that I wasn’t looking for a place where I could fit in. I was looking for the freedom to belong to something purposeful as I continue to grow as a person — my Indian heritage, my American values, and my old soul that keeps drawing me towards unfamiliar, ancient worlds — and perhaps to the wisdom and spirituality within them. Living in Mexico gave me the freedom to explore those connections, and painting became a medium to express that.

Allow me to show you what I mean, figuratively.

To create is human

Through trial and error, I have discovered that the antidote to my anxiety is not a massage or a spa day or a beach vacation (though they help from time to time) — it is creativity. Creating art in this way — finding connections between ancient cultures — has made me feel whole again, like I am part of something bigger. The more I paint, the more I realize how central creativity is to being human. That’s what my art is really about. There’s a narrative, a thought, a meaning behind every piece — observations, symbolic connections, and questions drawn from books and podcasts on history, archaeology, anthropology and astronomy. There are no political messages. Just a personal journey, trying to make sense of the world I live in today. Creativity is a process, not an outcome: It is a place where I lose my sense of time, immerse myself fully, get stumped, get frustrated, and still come out energized, rooted, grounded. In that space, I stop performing for others and follow my own curiosity.

Maybe that is why creativity makes me feel whole. I don’t have to settle into a single version of my identity. Pueblo life in Mexico, my American individuality, and the ancient civilizations that shape us all can coexist instead of competing. I can keep growing, changing, transforming — staying a “work in progress.” Creativity grants me that permission when society won’t. And while each painting begins with my own vision, it is also an invitation for the viewer to make it their own. You don’t have to see what I see or arrive at the same answers. That is the freedom I have found in my third space: I can be rooted in who I am and still have room to become someone new. Today, I am enough but I am not yet done growing.

A third space you can visit

That sense of wholeness — maybe even greatness — is exactly what I hope visitors feel walking through my upcoming show. If this speaks to you, please come see it in person: I have a collaborative exhibition with Mexican artist Miguel Cuauhtémoc called “A Pilgrimage Across Cultures,” running Nov. 1-15 at Galería Torres del Reloj in Polanco, Mexico City. Miguel grew up immersed in the symbols and rituals of ancient Mexico, and I grew up surrounded by the colors and deities of India. Separately, we both kept arriving at the same recurring image, the third eye, which we each use to explore higher consciousness. Neither of us knew the other was painting it until we saw each other’s work. That discovery felt like another kind of belonging — a connection we had painted before we had even spoken about it.

If you’re in town, please stop by and say hello. And if you’d like to browse the fuller portfolio first, here’s the link: www.tamannabembenek.com.

I’ve written about my personal journey at length elsewhere, if you want to 

Tamanna Bembenek was born in India, studied and worked in the U.S. and now lives in Mexico with her husband, Travis. They are the co-owners of Mexico News Daily.

World.title: Sheinbaum meets with US business leaders and ambassador amid controversy over US-backed police academy
World.content:
Listen to this article

During a week in which she has questioned intrusive U.S. security policies, President Claudia Sheinbaum met with U.S. business leaders at the National Palace, but avoided discussing security initiatives with U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson who was in attendance.

Sheinbaum said Thursday’s meeting with the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the American Chamber of Commerce of Mexico (AmCham) addressed issues related to the investment climate in Mexico, adding that she will address her concerns with Johnson at a later date.

“We focused on responding to the companies’ concerns, explaining the controversial new revenue law, discussing requests regarding trade and promoting the favorable environment for business investment in Mexico,” she said.

Also in attendance were the president of Mexico’s Business Coordinating Council, José Medina Mora, and the coordinator of the Advisory Council for Regional Economic Development and Relocation, Altagracia Gómez Sierra.

For its part, AmCham expressed interest in broader security issues, investment and greater private sector participation.

AmCham president Óscar del Cueto said his organization is eager for greater collaboration between the Mexican government and private enterprise, while also citing issues such as security, investment and greater private sector participation.

Several investment agreements were finalized (to be announced at a later date) and the U.S. contingent was given a detailed update on Plan México, Sheinbaum’s strategy for economic development, industrialization and regional growth.

The meeting took place amid an ongoing review of the Mexico-U.S. trade relationship as outlined in the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). AmCham has publicly stated that the USMCA should be used to deepen regional integration and preserve the competitiveness of the economies of Mexico, the United States and Canada.

Del Cueto insists the trade scenario presents a key opportunity for Mexico if the United States goes through a new stage of growth and industrialization and China loses dynamism.

“I firmly believe that next year we could be returning to the topic of nearshoring as the hot topic,” he said.

While Sheinbaum preferred discussing plans to allow for increased investment and greater North American productive integration, the kerfuffle involving Ambassador Johnson was a hot topic with the media.

After participating in a groundbreaking ceremony for an International Police Training Academy in the state of Querétaro on Oct. 2, Johnson — and Governor Mauricio Kuri — have faced criticism over the apparent failure to obtain federal authorization as required by law.

Sheinbaum publicly questioned the project several times, asserting that state governments cannot forge international security agreements or launch such academies without federal and Foreign Ministry authorization.

While clarifying that Mexico is not fundamentally against international cooperation, Sheinbaum explicitly demanded “cooperation with dignity and transparency” rather than “subordination,” adding that it is imperative that federal frameworks not be bypassed.

During a meeting with legislators on Thursday, Security Minister Omar García Harfuch addressed Mexico’s concerns about foreign interference in security matters, insisting that bilateral cooperation is subject to the provisions of Mexican law.

Sheinbaum said Johnson has agreed to meet soon with Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco to discuss the police academy and other issues related to security and the border.

With reports from Informador, Milenio, El Heraldo de México and Heraldo USA

COLOMBIA · FESTIVALS

Key Facts — The festival Estéreo Picnic is a large music festival in Bogotá, Colombia’s capital, and its 16th edition runs over three days.

— When Friday 19 to Sunday 21 March 2027; daily opening hours and set times are not out yet.

— Where Parque Metropolitano Simón Bolívar, a large public park in Bogotá’s Teusaquillo district.

— Headliners US rapper Travis Scott, British pop star Charli XCX and French DJ David Guetta lead more than 70 acts.

— Tickets Sold online only through Ticketmaster Colombia, the seller linked on the festival’s official website.

— Prices Three-day passes run from COP 1,299,000 (about US$401) for General to COP 3,489,000 (about US$1,078) for VIP, service charge included.

— Power Index Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in Colombia ranks 6th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 51.9 points (October 2026 edition).

Estéreo Picnic 2027 brings Travis Scott, Charli XCX and David Guetta to Bogotá from Friday 19 to Sunday 21 March. For US fans, the bill is full of American names, and three-day passes start at about US$401.

The festival revealed its line-up on Thursday 8 October, and tickets are sold online only through Ticketmaster Colombia. The official poster lists more than 70 acts, from US rap and British pop to Latin American rock and electronic music.

What Estéreo Picnic Is and Why It Matters

Estéreo Picnic is a large music festival in Bogotá that mixes pop, rap, rock and electronic music on several stages. Estéreo Picnic 2027 is the 16th edition, Noticias RCN and Vanguardia report, under the motto Un Mundo Distinto (A Different World).

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Colombia ranks 6th of 14 with 51.9 points. Strongest pillar: military means (91); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (28). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB-); 26 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.8 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The headliners are Travis Scott, the US rapper, Charli XCX, the British pop singer, and David Guetta, the French DJ and producer. Reggaeton star Arcángel, British electronic act The Prodigy and US metal band Avenged Sevenfold also sit near the top.

Other US acts on the poster include Khruangbin, The War on Drugs, Cage The Elephant, Leon Bridges and The Neighbourhood. Kasabian, RAYE, Lola Young and Four Tet add a sizeable British contingent.

Latin America has a big share of the bill, with Venezuelan band Rawayana and Argentine rapper Milo J among the main names. The official poster, also shown on Ticketmaster’s event page, runs to more than 70 acts in all.

Bogotá city hall expected more than 128,000 people at the 2025 edition, which ran over four days at the same park. Its economic development office projected more than 18,000 international visitors, a sign of the festival’s pull beyond Colombia.

Tickets, Prices and Sale Dates

Estéreo Picnic 2027 tickets are sold online only through Ticketmaster Colombia, which the festival’s official website links to for all ticket sales. Ticketmaster’s event page warns that it is not responsible for tickets bought anywhere else.

All Estéreo Picnic 2027 passes on sale so far are three-day combos covering Friday, Saturday and Sunday. General starts at COP 1,299,000 (about US$401), and General+ starts at COP 1,639,000 (about US$506).

General+ adds preferential entry and separate toilets, according to the festival’s guide to ticket zones. VIP starts at COP 3,489,000 (about US$1,078) and adds its own entry line, viewing areas at the main stages and exclusive bars.

Prices rise in stages, and the festival lists General at COP 1,699,000 (about US$525) in its fourth stage. Fans who bought before the line-up was announced paid COP 999,000 (about US$309) for General, Vanguardia reported.

A presale for clients of Grupo Aval, a Colombian banking group, opened on Thursday 8 October, Vanguardia reported. General sale was scheduled to start on Saturday 10 October at 10 a.m. Bogotá time.

Children aged seven and over can attend through Futuro Picnic, an alcohol-free zone for minors with access to the two biggest stages. Each minor needs at least one adult with a Futuro Picnic ticket, which starts at COP 1,089,000 (about US$336).

US dollar figures here use the rate of 3,237 Colombian pesos per dollar on Saturday 10 October 2026. Ticketmaster’s price table already includes its service charge, but a US card may add its own foreign transaction fees.

The Venue and How to Get There

Estéreo Picnic 2027 takes place at Parque Metropolitano Simón Bolívar, a large public park in Bogotá’s Teusaquillo district. IDRD, the city’s sports and recreation institute, puts its green space at about 910,000 square metres, or roughly 225 acres.

The park also holds a 10-hectare lake, a 37,000-square-metre events plaza and a 3.2-kilometre jogging track, according to IDRD. The institute lists public gates on Avenida Carrera 68, Calle 63, Carrera 60 and Carrera 53.

In 2025 the festival had five music stages in the park, plus food areas, rest zones and an entrepreneurs’ fair. Bogotá city hall described that layout when the 2025 edition opened on Thursday 27 March.

The US State Department advises against hailing taxis on the street in Colombia, suggesting a dispatch service or ride app instead. Agree on a pick-up point in advance, because tens of thousands of people leave the park each night.

In 2025, TransMilenio, Bogotá’s dedicated-lane bus network, pointed festival fans to Movistar Arena and Salitre – El Greco stations. Its main red buses ran until 11 p.m. that year, so plan the ride home before the last set.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

US citizens do not need a visa for tourist stays of 90 days or less, according to the US State Department. It recommends six months of passport validity, and Colombia may refuse entry without a return or onward ticket.

Before flying, travellers should fill in Check-Mig, Colombia’s free online migration form, between 72 hours and one hour before departure. The form sits on the website of Migración Colombia, the country’s immigration authority.

The State Department rates Colombia at Level 3, Reconsider Travel, but Bogotá is not among its Do Not Travel areas. Its wider safety advice warns about robberies, drugging and criminals who use dating apps to lure victims.

Keep phones, watches and jewellery out of sight on the way in and out, and never leave a drink unattended. The festival’s zone guide lists cashless top-up points inside the park, so a card without foreign transaction fees helps.

Beyond the Estéreo Picnic 2027 pass, budget for three nights of lodging, local transport, and food and drink inside the park. For 2025, Bogotá’s economic development office projected average spending of COP 1.7 million (about US$525) per festival tourist.

Bogotá sits at high altitude, the State Department notes, so plan an easy first day before three long nights in the park. For a sense of the city’s live-music calendar, see this guide to what to do in Bogotá in October 2026.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

Organisers of Estéreo Picnic 2027 have not yet said which artists play on which day, and no set times are out. Gate opening hours for each of the three days have not been published either.

Only three-day passes are on sale so far, and single-day tickets have not been announced. Festival entrances and any special TransMilenio service for 2027 have not been announced either.

The festival has not said how long each price stage lasts or how many tickets each one holds. A cheaper stage can therefore end without warning, so the price on the day you buy may be higher.

Artist cancellations are always possible at a large festival months away, so check the official website before you travel. Buy only through Ticketmaster, since the seller does not stand behind tickets bought elsewhere.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where is Estéreo Picnic 2027?

Estéreo Picnic 2027 runs from Friday 19 to Sunday 21 March 2027 at Parque Metropolitano Simón Bolívar in Bogotá. Daily opening hours and set times have not been published yet.

How much are tickets, and where can I buy them?

Tickets are sold online only through Ticketmaster Colombia. Three-day General passes start at COP 1,299,000 (about US$401), and General+ at COP 1,639,000 (about US$506). VIP starts at COP 3,489,000 (about US$1,078), and all prices include the service charge.

Do US citizens need a visa to attend Estéreo Picnic 2027?

No, not for tourist stays of 90 days or less, according to the US State Department. You also need a valid passport, a return or onward ticket and the free Check-Mig migration form. Fill in the form between 72 hours and one hour before your flight.

World.content:

PERU · CONCERTS

Key Facts — The night Colombian singer Karol G brings her Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour to Lima on Friday 22 January 2027.

— Where it is The Estadio San Marcos, on the main campus of San Marcos University in Cercado de Lima, the city’s central district.

— How to buy Tickets are sold only by Teleticket, the official seller, and general sale has been open since Thursday 30 April 2026.

— What is left On 10 October six of nine sections were sold out; seats left cost S/402.50 (about US$117) or S/862.50 (about US$250).

— Start time Teleticket says the show may start from 9 p.m. Lima time and last about two hours; no doors time is out yet.

— For US visitors No visa is needed for tourist stays under 90 days, but passports need six months’ validity on arrival.

— Power Index Peru ranks 5th of 14 in Peru ranks 5th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 54.7 points (October 2026 edition).

The Karol G Lima concert takes place on Friday 22 January 2027 at the Estadio San Marcos, a university stadium in Lima. US fans can see a star from this year’s Coachella main stage on a summer trip to Peru.

Tickets are sold only through Teleticket, the official seller, and on Saturday 10 October six of its nine sections were sold out. Seats still on sale cost S/402.50 (about US$117) or S/862.50 (about US$250), fees included.

Who Karol G Is and Why the Lima Show Matters

Karol G is the stage name of Carolina Giraldo, a reggaeton and Latin pop singer from Medellín, Colombia’s second city. Her album Tropicoqueta came out in June 2025 and gave her a fourth straight number one on Billboard’s Top Latin Albums chart.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 54.7 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Billboard is the US music magazine whose charts track sales and streams. It said the album’s debut was the biggest streaming week of 2025 yet for a Latin album by a woman.

In 2026 she played the main stage at Coachella, the big music festival in the California desert. She announced this tour from that stage, telling fans “¡Familia! ¡Nos vamos de tour!”, which means “Family, we are going on tour”.

The tour is called Viajando por el Mundo Tropitour, or “Travelling the World Tropitour”. Teleticket says the Lima show will mix songs from Tropicoqueta with the hits that made her name.

Teleticket’s listing promotes the Karol G Lima night as the most important event of early 2027. It names the Peruvian company Bizarro Entertainment y Servicios Perú as the organiser.

The show also lands in a busy season for big concerts at the same venue. BTS, the South Korean band, is playing three nights there this week, on 7, 9 and 10 October, RPP reported.

Karol G last played Peru in 2024, on her Mañana Será Bonito tour, La República reported. That tour filled stadiums across Latin America, the paper added.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Peru expat life Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Tickets, Prices and How to Buy

Karol G Lima tickets are sold online at Teleticket, the official seller. Sales opened with a presale for BBVA Mastercard holders on Wednesday 29 April 2026 at 9 a.m.

General sale followed on Thursday 30 April, and all prices below include Teleticket’s service fee. On Saturday 10 October, Teleticket marked six of its nine sections as sold out.

The cheapest seats, in the Tribuna Norte or north stand, cost S/172.50 (about US$50) and are sold out. The east and west stands, Tribuna Oriente and Tribuna Occidente, at S/632.50 (about US$184), are gone too.

The top tier, PIT Latina Foreva A and B, costs S/1,840 (about US$534) and is sold out as well. So is the right-hand Tropicoqueta section, priced at S/862.50 (about US$250).

Regular seats remain in Tropicoqueta left at S/862.50 (about US$250) and Viajando por el Mundo at S/402.50 (about US$117). Ten wheelchair places in the east and west stands cost S/575 (about US$167) each and remain on sale.

Each buyer may take up to six tickets. US$ figures here use 3.44 soles to the US dollar, the rate on Saturday 10 October 2026.

The Venue and How to Get There

The Estadio San Marcos stands inside the Ciudad Universitaria, the main campus of San Marcos University, in Cercado de Lima. Cercado de Lima is the central district that also holds the old town, inland from the seaside districts popular with visitors.

Door 8 of the stadium faces block 34 of Avenida Óscar R. Benavides, formerly Avenida Colonial, RPP reported. For the BTS shows this week, Lima’s city hall placed portable toilets there and in a nearby park.

Taxis and ride-hailing apps are the simplest way to reach the stadium from Miraflores or Barranco. Agree on a pick-up point away from the gates, because the whole crowd leaves at the same time.

Leave early, since Friday-evening traffic in central Lima can be slow. Teleticket says the Karol G Lima show may start from 9 p.m. and last about two hours.

Tips for US and Foreign Visitors

US citizens need no tourist visa for stays under 90 days, the State Department says. Passports must be valid for six months on arrival, with one blank page for the entry stamp.

Peruvian border officials decide how long you may stay when you arrive. The State Department rates Peru at Level 2, exercise increased caution, citing crime, civil unrest and kidnapping risk.

Before you travel, read what Peru’s new crime command means for visitors. In crowds, keep phones out of sight and agree on a meeting point with friends.

At night, use app rides or taxis booked through your hotel rather than hailing cars in the street. Buy only through Teleticket, whose rules ban resale, as tickets sold on social media or outside the gates may be fake.

Teleticket recommends the Karol G Lima show for all ages, but children under six are not admitted. Children from six need their own ticket in the same section as an adult, and staff may ask for ID.

Lima keeps the same time all year, five hours behind GMT, which matches New York in January. Teleticket charges in soles, so US cards may add a foreign transaction fee.

January is summer in Lima, which makes it an easy month to combine a concert with a longer stay. The city’s 2027 calendar is filling up, and Jay Wheeler plays Costa 21 on 1 May 2027.

What Is Not Confirmed Yet

No opening act has been announced for the Karol G Lima concert. Teleticket gives a possible start from 9 p.m. but no separate time for doors.

Teleticket lists one Lima date only, and no second night has been announced. It does not say how many tickets remain in the sections still on sale.

The setlist is not public, beyond the promise of Tropicoqueta songs and older hits. Teleticket lists current prices as valid until the day of the show or until each section sells out.

More: Peru news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Karol G concert in Lima?

The Karol G Lima concert is on Friday 22 January 2027 at the Estadio San Marcos, in central Lima. Teleticket says it may start from 9 p.m.

How much are tickets, and where can I buy them?

Teleticket, the official seller, still had seats at S/402.50 (about US$117) and S/862.50 (about US$250) on 10 October, fees included. Six of its nine sections were already sold out.

Do US citizens need a visa to visit Peru for the show?

No, not for tourist stays under 90 days, according to the US State Department. Your passport must be valid for six months on arrival.

World.title: Amr Diab Cairo Concert at Al Manara on Thursday 3 December
World.content: RT Ask Rio Times Latin American culture, food and life. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesWhat to do, where to go in Rio de Janeiro › RT Ask Rio Times Latin American culture, food and life. × This week Tonight Where to eat Before you go Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times → EGYPT · CONCERTS Key Facts — The night Egyptian pop star Amr Diab plays Cairo on Thursday 3 December 2026, with the start listed at 5 p.m. Cairo time. — Where it is Al Manara Arena, part of the Al Manara International Conference Center in New Cairo, on the capital’s eastern edge. — How to buy Tickets are sold online at TicketsMarche, the official seller, and the show is presented by Orange Egypt. — What it costs Early-bird tickets run from EGP 1,100 (about US$21) for Regular to EGP 7,500 (about US$143) for Premier Standing. — Doors and age Doors open at 3 p.m. and close at 10 p.m., and children under 10 are not admitted. — For US visitors US citizens need a visa for Egypt, and passports must be valid for six months, the State Department says. — The catch No support act or end date for early-bird prices has been announced, and the cheapest ticket has risen since 2 October. The Amr Diab Cairo concert is set for Thursday 3 December 2026 at Al Manara Arena in New Cairo. For US travellers, it is a chance to see the singer behind the album Nour El Ain play to a home crowd. Tickets are on sale at TicketsMarche, the official seller, from EGP 1,100 (about US$21). The seller lists doors at 3 p.m. and the start at 5 p.m. Cairo time, which is 10 a.m. US Eastern. Who Amr Diab Is and Why This Show Matters Amr Diab is an Egyptian singer born in Port Said in 1961, according to Egypt Today. His first album, Ya Tareeq, came out in 1983, and fans call him Al Hadaba, the plateau. His album Nour El Ain brought him recognition well beyond the Arab world, Egypt Today reported. By 2020, the same outlet said, he had won seven World Music Awards. The Cairo night is presented by Orange Egypt, the local arm of the French telecoms group Orange. The seller promises an evening of chart-topping hits, but no setlist has been published. Al Manara Arena has become a regular Cairo stage for the singer in recent seasons. Enterprise, an Egyptian business newsletter, listed his Friday 16 January 2026 show there, also presented by Orange. IQ Magazine, a live-music trade publication, wrote that he has played several sold-out concerts at the venue. One of them, Manara Live Volume 3, took place in February 2025. Egyptian outlets Akhbar El Yom and Egypt Telegraph reported the 3 December date and prices on Friday 2 October. That leaves almost eight weeks to plan a trip around the Amr Diab Cairo concert. Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Egypt expat life Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy Tickets, Prices and Age Rules Tickets for the Amr Diab Cairo concert are sold online at TicketsMarche, the official seller. On Saturday 10 October, it listed six categories, from standing areas to private lounges. Early-bird Regular tickets cost EGP 1,100 (about US$21), and the Fanpit costs EGP 2,500 (about US$48). Front Row costs EGP 7,000 (about US$134), and Premier Standing costs EGP 7,500 (about US$143). Lounges are sold whole, for 10 people at EGP 150,000 (about US$2,864) or for 15 people at EGP 250,000 (about US$4,773). The seller assigns each lounge by the best place still free at the time of purchase. Prices have already risen since the 2 October announcement. That day, Akhbar El Yom listed the cheapest ticket at EGP 1,000 (about US$19), under a super-early-bird tier. A full ticket is needed from the age of 10, and younger children are not allowed in. TicketsMarche lists doors at 3 p.m., the show at 5 p.m. and doors closing at 10 p.m. US$ figures here use about 52.4 Egyptian pounds to the US dollar, the rate on Saturday 10 October 2026. Your bank may add its own foreign-transaction fee when you pay in pounds. The Venue and How to Get There The Amr Diab Cairo concert takes place at Al Manara Arena, in New Cairo, a newer district on the capital’s eastern edge. The arena belongs to the Al Manara International Conference Center, which the seller says covers over 30,000 square metres. IQ Magazine puts the arena’s seating capacity at over 20,000 and calls it one of North Africa’s largest indoor music venues. The seller lists parking, food services and security on site. On the map, the venue sits about 15 km (9 miles) east of Tahrir Square, the main square of downtown Cairo. It is about 12 km (7.5 miles) south of Cairo International Airport. Real journey times are much longer, because Cairo traffic is heavy on weekday evenings. Thursday evening also starts the Egyptian weekend, so leave downtown or Giza hotels well before the doors open. Taxis and ride-hailing apps are the simplest way for most visitors to reach New Cairo. Agree on a pick-up point before the show, because thousands of people leave at the same time. Tips for US and Foreign Visitors US citizens need a visa to enter Egypt, according to the US State Department. It lists a 30-day tourist e-visa on arrival at Cairo International Airport for US$36, paid by card. Egypt also sells e-visas in advance on its official portal, visa2egypt.gov.eg. Your passport must be valid for six months and have at least one blank page. The State Department rates Egypt at Level 2, exercise increased caution, citing terrorism, crime and health. Its advisory, issued on 15 July 2025, does not list Cairo among the areas to avoid. Those no-go areas are North and Middle Sinai, the Western Desert without a licensed tour company, and border zones. A night in New Cairo falls outside all of them. TicketsMarche asks buyers to register with an email address and a phone number, and the form starts with Egypt’s +20 code. Switch it to your own country code, and set up the account well before you plan to buy. Cairo is seven hours ahead of US Eastern time in early December. So the 5 p.m. start of the Amr Diab Cairo concert is 10 a.m. in New York, for friends following from home. What Is Not Confirmed Yet The promoter behind the show is not named on the ticket page, which credits only Orange as presenter. No support act has been announced, and no setlist has been published. TicketsMarche has not said when the early-bird tiers end or what later prices will be. Buying early is the only way to lock in the current prices. The seller has not published rules on cameras, bags or re-entry for this show. Check the event page again in the week before Thursday 3 December. TicketsMarche lists no other Amr Diab date in Egypt besides the Amr Diab Cairo concert. Earlier visitors can try the Cairo Jazz Festival, Thursday 5 to Saturday 7 November. Comedy fans can also look at the Cairo shows of Iranian-American comedian Max Amini in mid-November. Both are separate events with their own tickets and rules. The Amr Diab Cairo concert is on Thursday 3 December 2026 at Al Manara Arena in New Cairo. TicketsMarche lists doors at 3 p.m. and the start at 5 p.m. Cairo time. Early-bird prices for the Amr Diab Cairo concert run from EGP 1,100 (about US$21) to EGP 7,500 (about US$143). Do US citizens need a visa to visit Egypt for the show? World.title: South Africa Asylum Rules After the Unrest
World.content:
SOUTH AFRICA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening South Africa’s Home Affairs withdrew a directive that had opened asylum applications to people who entered irregularly, after violence in Durban and Soweto.

— Why it matters The Constitutional Court ruling of 7 July 2026 remains binding, so Home Affairs must still find a way to accept asylum claims without triggering further unrest.

— The numbers Soweto police are investigating nine cases of malicious damage to property, three of common assault and one of public violence from the 8 October protests.

— Who is who The Director-General of Home Affairs issued the directive on 28 September 2026 and withdrew it on 9 October, reportedly without the minister’s knowledge; Cyril Ramaphosa is President.

— What to watch Any new directive will signal how the government balances court compliance with public order.

— What it means for you US investors and travellers should expect continued localised unrest risk in Durban, Soweto and near refugee reception offices, with possible disruption to logistics and staff movement.

South Africa asylum seekers are caught between a binding Constitutional Court ruling and a withdrawn Home Affairs directive that sparked violence in October 2026. For US readers, the episode shows how quickly migration politics can disrupt operations in a major emerging market.

South Africa is a key destination for foreign investment, but it also carries a long history of anti-migrant tension. This analysis explains what the court actually decided, why the directive failed, and what the unrest means for business and travel. It draws on the Africa Intelligence Brief dated 10 October 2026.

What the Constitutional Court Actually Decided

On 7 July 2026, the Constitutional Court ruled in the Scalabrini Centre of Cape Town matter that parts of South Africa’s refugee framework were unconstitutional. The court found that procedural barriers could prevent a person from accessing the asylum system before the substance of the claim was assessed.

File photo: the Constitutional Court courtroom in Johannesburg, where the asylum ruling was handed down on 7 July 2026.

The ruling addressed three specific barriers: entering South Africa irregularly, failing to possess an asylum transit visa, and failing to report to an immigration officer within the prescribed period. The court’s practical legal principle is that these failures cannot, by themselves, prevent an applicant from lodging an asylum claim. The state must provide access to the process and assess the claim on its merits.

Crucially, the judgment does not automatically confer refugee status, permanent residence, citizenship or an unconditional right to remain in South Africa. Each application still requires assessment under the refugee system, and an unsuccessful applicant can remain subject to immigration enforcement. The ruling changed the gateway to the process, not the outcome of every claim.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Directive That Sparked Violence

On 28 September 2026, the Director-General of Home Affairs issued, as an operational measure, a directive to refugee reception offices to operationalise the Constitutional Court’s judgment. The directive instructed offices to accept asylum applications that previously might have been rejected at the door because the applicant had entered unlawfully, lacked the required transit documentation, or had not reported within the prescribed time.

Home Affairs said the directive was an operational measure designed to implement the court order, not to create a new immigration status. Within days, however, reception offices were overwhelmed. In its statement of 9 October, Home Affairs said its officials had been placed at risk and that “serious threats to public safety and order had emerged.”

The department announced that it would develop a new operational approach. The withdrawal did not suspend or overturn the Constitutional Court’s judgment. Home Affairs remains legally bound to comply with the ruling, meaning it cannot simply reinstate the old procedural exclusions.

Why the Directive Collided With Local Anger

The directive collided with three existing pressures. First, a sharp increase in visible demand at reception offices: once applicants understood that previous procedural obstacles could no longer automatically block them, large numbers went to refugee reception offices. The department said offices were overwhelmed within days.

Second, a longstanding political narrative linking migration to crime, jobs and pressure on public services. The court’s procedural ruling was widely interpreted by opponents as opening the door to “illegal migrants,” even though it did not grant status automatically. Third, existing anti-migrant mobilisation: protesters gathered outside the Durban refugee reception centre, complaining that foreigners were being favoured, and the protests later spread to Soweto in Johannesburg.

On 8 October 2026, violence in Durban and Soweto included burned vehicles, looting and clashes. The political and legal distinction was crucial: the court protected access to an application process, while protesters treated the implementation as evidence that the government was permitting unrestricted settlement.

How the Asylum Process Works in Principle

A person seeking protection must approach a designated Refugee Reception Office and lodge an application. The process is not equivalent to receiving a visa or permanent residence. The key stages are: access to the application system, registration and documentation, substantive assessment, decision and review, and immigration consequences.

After the Constitutional Court ruling, irregular entry, lack of a transit visa or late reporting cannot automatically prevent the application from being received. Home Affairs records the applicant and issues the relevant documentation for the pending claim, subject to the department’s operational procedures. Officials then assess whether the applicant meets the legal definition of a refugee or otherwise qualifies for protection.

A claim may be accepted or rejected, with statutory review or appeal mechanisms available. A rejected claim does not create a right to remain indefinitely; the person may become liable to ordinary immigration enforcement. The Constitutional Court ruling changed the gateway to the process, not the outcome of every claim. That distinction was central to Home Affairs’ public explanation after the unrest.

Business and Investor Risks

For companies operating in South Africa, the episode creates four immediate risk categories. Operational disruption: reception-office closures, road blockades, damaged vehicles and localised unrest can interrupt logistics and staff movement. Security costs: companies may need additional transport controls, site security, employee communication and business-continuity measures.

Reputational exposure: firms employing migrants or serving migrant communities can become politically visible, particularly in retail, logistics, construction, hospitality and informal-market supply chains. Regulatory uncertainty: the government must now design a replacement process that complies with the court ruling while controlling demand at reception offices.

The legal uncertainty is narrower than the political uncertainty. The court ruling remains binding, but Home Affairs had not yet announced the replacement operational arrangements in the material available through 10 October 2026. Companies should therefore distinguish between a person’s right to have an asylum claim received and assessed, a person’s right to work or remain permanently, and the employer’s separate obligations under immigration, labour and compliance law.

For US-listed investors, exposure is most relevant where a company has South African staff, stores, mines, factories, warehouses, banks, telecom infrastructure or consumer operations. A US listing does not insulate an issuer from South African disruptions: the risks would normally appear through operating interruptions, security expenditure, insurance claims, lost trading days, supply-chain delays or changes in local regulation. Any investment analysis should use the company’s latest filing and investor-relations disclosures for South African revenue, assets, employees and country-risk language rather than infer exposure from the listing venue alone.

What It Means for the United States and Latin America

The broad legal principle is comparable to the US distinction between access to an asylum process and ultimate eligibility for protection: allowing a person to present a claim does not mean the claim will succeed. The South African controversy illustrates how quickly that procedural distinction can disappear in public debate.

The systems are not interchangeable. South Africa’s immediate dispute concerns access through Home Affairs refugee reception offices and the consequences of irregular entry or missed reporting requirements. The United States operates a different statutory, border, detention and adjudication framework. Comparisons should therefore focus on process design, not on assuming that a South African court ruling creates a US-style automatic right to remain.

For Latin American readers, the episode offers a cautionary parallel. Several Latin American countries host large Venezuelan and Haitian migrant populations and face similar tensions between legal access to asylum procedures and public pressure for stricter enforcement. South Africa’s experience shows that even a court ruling protecting procedural access can trigger backlash if administrative capacity is weak and migration is politicised.

Scenarios: What Could Stabilise or Tip the Crisis

One stabilising scenario is that Home Affairs develops a phased intake system with clear appointment scheduling, security at reception offices, and public communication that distinguishes access to a process from automatic residence. If the department can show that claims are being assessed individually and rejected claims lead to enforcement, the political temperature could cool.

A tipping scenario is that the replacement approach is perceived as either too permissive or too restrictive. If offices remain overwhelmed, anti-migrant groups could mobilise again. If the department imposes new administrative hurdles that contradict the court ruling, litigation could resume and the government could face contempt proceedings. Either outcome would prolong uncertainty for businesses and travellers.

A third scenario is that the unrest spreads beyond Durban and Soweto to other urban centres with large migrant populations. The October incidents reportedly included attacks on small foreign-run stores and vehicles, not only confrontations at refugee offices. That pattern could recur if economic conditions worsen or if political actors use migration as a campaign issue ahead of future elections.

What It Means for You

If you are a US investor with exposure to South Africa, review your portfolio companies’ latest filings for South African revenue, assets and employees. Pay attention to any mention of operational disruption, security costs or regulatory uncertainty in their risk factors. The unrest is localised but the underlying drivers are national, so do not assume that a company with no presence in Durban or Soweto is insulated.

If you are a traveller, avoid protests, counter-protests and large gatherings, even when they appear peaceful. Monitor local police, municipal and transport notices before travelling. Use secure transport and avoid spontaneous route changes through affected townships. Keep identification and immigration documents available. Do not photograph crowds, police operations or damaged property. Maintain a contingency plan for airport, hotel and business transfers.

The principal travel risk is not that every foreign visitor will be treated as an asylum seeker or migrant. It is that unrest can spread quickly, disrupt roads and public transport, and turn nationality or perceived foreignness into a targeting factor. Ask employers or accommodation providers about localised risks rather than relying only on national travel advisories.

What Is Not Known

As of 10 October 2026, Home Affairs had not announced a replacement operational approach. The department said it would embark on a fresh process to find an operational approach that complies with the court order, but gave no timeline or details.

It is also not known how many asylum applications were lodged during the period the directive was in force, or how many people were turned away after the withdrawal. The available official material does not provide a verified October 2026 national total for asylum applications, asylum-seeker visas, or refugee permits.

Finally, it is not known whether the unrest will lead to legislative changes. Any legislative amendments would require parliamentary consideration.

What to Watch

Watch for any announcement from Home Affairs on a replacement operational approach. The timing and content of that announcement will signal whether the government can balance court compliance with public order. If the announcement is delayed beyond a few weeks, expect continued legal and political pressure.

Watch for further unrest in Durban, Soweto and other urban centres. The October incidents followed a pattern of anti-migrant mobilisation that has recurred in South Africa. Any new protests near refugee reception offices or migrant-owned businesses should be treated as elevated-risk events.

Watch for parliamentary action on migration policy. Any legislative process will be a key indicator of the government’s longer-term direction on migration policy.

Watch for company disclosures from US-listed firms with South African operations. If the unrest continues or spreads, issuers may update their risk factors or provide operational updates. Those disclosures will be the most reliable source of information on business impact.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did South Africa’s Constitutional Court rule on asylum seekers?

On 7 July 2026, the Constitutional Court ruled that irregular entry, lack of an asylum transit visa, or failure to report within five days cannot automatically prevent a person from lodging an asylum claim. The state must provide access to the process and assess each claim on its merits. The ruling does not automatically confer refugee status or permanent residence.

Why did South Africa withdraw its asylum directive in October 2026?

Home Affairs withdrew the directive on 9 October 2026 after refugee reception offices were overwhelmed and anti-migrant protests turned violent in Durban and Soweto. The department said the directive was designed to implement the court order, not to create a new immigration status. The withdrawal did not overturn the Constitutional Court ruling.

Does the withdrawn directive mean asylum seekers can no longer apply in South Africa?

No. The Constitutional Court ruling remains binding, so Home Affairs cannot simply reinstate the old procedural exclusions. The department must develop a new operational approach that complies with the court order while controlling demand at reception offices.

How does South Africa’s asylum process work?

A person must approach a designated Refugee Reception Office and lodge an application. After the court ruling, irregular entry or missed deadlines cannot automatically block the application. Officials then assess whether the applicant meets the legal definition of a refugee. A rejected claim does not create a right to remain indefinitely.

What are the risks for US investors in South Africa after the unrest?

The main risks are operational disruption, security costs, reputational exposure and regulatory uncertainty. Companies with South African staff, stores, mines, factories or logistics operations could face interruptions from road blockades, damaged vehicles or localised unrest. Investors should review company filings for South African exposure and country-risk language.

Is it safe to travel to South Africa after the October 2026 unrest?

The unrest was concentrated in parts of Durban and Soweto, but the underlying drivers are national. Travellers should avoid protests, monitor local notices, use secure transport and keep identification available. The principal risk is that unrest can spread quickly and disrupt roads or public transport.

Who issued and withdrew South Africa’s asylum directive?

The Director-General of Home Affairs issued the directive on 28 September 2026 as an operational measure and withdrew it on 9 October 2026. President Cyril Ramaphosa is the head of state and government. The Constitutional Court ruling binds the department regardless of who holds office.

World.title: Mainland Block Party Returns to Lagos on 1 January 2027
World.content: RT Ask Rio Times Latin American culture, food and life. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesWhat to do, where to go in Rio de Janeiro › RT Ask Rio Times Latin American culture, food and life. × This week Tonight Where to eat Before you go Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times → NIGERIA · PARTIES Key Facts — The date Friday 1 January 2027, from 8 p.m. until 5 a.m. on Saturday 2 January, Lagos time. — Where it is Ikeja, the capital of Lagos State on the city’s mainland; the ticket page still lists the exact venue as to be announced. — Tickets Sold through the official site, mainlandblockparty.com, where earlybird tiers are on sale now. — What it costs Entry from ₦7,500 (about US$6); the Legend tier is ₦50,000 (about US$38); group sections reach ₦3 million (about US$2,250). — Who runs it The party began in 2018, founded by Asa Asika and Bizzle Osikoya of the music agency Plug NG. — For US visitors Americans need a Nigerian visa before travel, six months’ passport validity and yellow fever and polio certificates. — Still open No headliner, exact venue or doors time has been announced for this edition. The Mainland Block Party returns to Lagos on Friday 1 January 2027, with earlybird tickets already on sale. For US visitors in Nigeria for the December concert season, it is the party that opens the new year. The official site calls this edition Mission 27k and lists it from 8 p.m. until 5 a.m., Lagos time. Entry starts at ₦7,500 (about US$6), but the venue and the headliner have not been announced. What the Mainland Block Party Is and Why It Matters The Mainland Block Party began in 2018 as a local gathering in Ikeja, the capital of Lagos State. Its founders, Asa Asika and Bizzle Osikoya, also founded the music agency Plug NG, OkayAfrica reported in July 2025. The idea was to celebrate the Lagos mainland, which OkayAfrica described as rich in culture but often dismissed. The mainland is the inland part of Lagos, across the lagoon from the business districts of Victoria Island and Ikoyi. Recent New Year’s Day editions have carried a “Mission” name and a major Nigerian headliner. Singer Adekunle Gold led Mission 24k and the street-pop singer Seyi Vibez led Mission 25k, the Nigerian daily ThisDay reported. The last edition, Mission 26k, was set for Thursday 1 January 2026, with the rapper Olamide announced as headliner. ThisDay reported that it aimed to draw 26,000 people, its most ambitious target yet. The brand has also travelled, with recent editions in Abuja, Accra, London and New York, according to ThisDay. In New York, the rapper ODUMODUBLVCK headlined a 2025 show staged with OkayAfrica, the African culture website. For US readers, the Mainland Block Party is a Lagos brand that has already staged shows for Nigerian fans in New York. It comes at the end of Detty December, the Lagos concert season that includes Detty December Fest. Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Nigeria expat life Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy Ticket Tiers and Prices in US Dollars The official Mainland Block Party website sells five tiers, from ₦7,500 (about US$6) to ₦3 million (about US$2,250). US$ figures here use about ₦1,331 to the US dollar, the rate on Saturday 10 October 2026. The cheapest tier, Rockstar Earlybird, costs ₦7,500 (about US$6) and gives general entry. Legend Earlybird costs ₦50,000 (about US$38), with a platform view, private entry, free merchandise and a cocktail shot. Group sections start with District 6 at ₦1 million (about US$750), a standing area for six with two premium bottles. District 9 costs ₦2 million (about US$1,500) and seats eight with four premium bottles. District 12 costs ₦3 million (about US$2,250) and seats ten, with a ₦1.5 million (about US$1,130) drinks allowance and a food platter. Each of the three District sections also includes a shisha pot and one free merchandise item. The two cheapest tiers carry an earlybird label, and the site does not say when or by how much prices will change. Buy only through the official site, since tickets from resellers cannot be checked in advance. The Venue, Ikeja and How to Get There The Mainland Block Party ticket page lists the venue as TBA, meaning to be announced, on the Lagos mainland. Its event description places the party in Ikeja, the district where the first edition was held in 2018. NotJustOk, a Nigerian music site, reported in December 2025 that the party has traditionally been held at the Police College in Ikeja. ThisDay called the site of the last edition Mainland Wonderland, and the organisers have not said where Mission 27k will be held. Murtala Muhammed International Airport, the main gateway for international flights into Lagos, sits in Ikeja. For December, the airport authority asks travellers to arrive three to four hours before departure. The US State Department says ride-hailing apps are widely used in Lagos and are seen as safer than ordinary taxis. Agree on a pick-up point in advance, because finding a car can take time when a large crowd leaves at once. Staying on the mainland near Ikeja shortens the trip back when the party ends at 5 a.m. on Saturday. Visitors based on the islands should plan the return journey before the night begins. Tips for US and Foreign Visitors Americans need a Nigerian visa before they travel, according to the US State Department. Passports must be valid for six months beyond the arrival date, with one blank page per entry stamp. Nigeria also requires yellow fever and polio vaccination certificates from all travellers older than nine months. Any amount above US$10,000 must be declared on arrival and on departure. The State Department rates Nigeria at Level 3 of 4, “Reconsider travel”, in an advisory issued on Friday 12 June 2026. Lagos State is not on its list of states where Americans should not travel at all. The advisory warns that violent crime is common and that Americans, seen as wealthy, are often targets of crime and kidnapping. It adds that US help in emergencies is limited outside Abuja and Lagos. At a large night-time party, keep phones and cash out of sight and stay with people you know. Decide in advance where to regroup if anyone gets separated in the crowd. Budget for a ride-hailing trip each way to the Mainland Block Party, which ends at 5 a.m. on Saturday 2 January. Carry some cash in naira as well as cards, and tell your bank before you travel. What Is Not Confirmed Yet The organisers have not named a headliner for Mission 27k or published a line-up. They have also not confirmed the exact venue beyond Ikeja on the Lagos mainland. The ticket page gives no doors time, no age limit and no end date for the earlybird prices. It links to a refund and cancellation policy but does not summarise the terms. Each recent Mainland Block Party had a major Nigerian headliner, but no name has been given for this edition. Fans planning a trip around one artist should wait for that announcement before booking flights. Tickets are on sale even though the venue is still listed as TBA. Visitors should keep hotel bookings flexible until the address is published. More: Nigeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times. Frequently Asked Questions When is the Mainland Block Party 2027? The Mainland Block Party runs from 8 p.m. on Friday 1 January 2027 until 5 a.m. on Saturday 2 January, Lagos time. The official site places it in Ikeja, with the exact venue still to be announced. How much are Mainland Block Party tickets in US dollars? Earlybird general entry costs ₦7,500 (about US$6) and the Legend tier costs ₦50,000 (about US$38). Group sections cost from ₦1 million (about US$750) to ₦3 million (about US$2,250). Do Americans need a visa to attend? Yes, US citizens need a Nigerian visa before travelling, plus a passport valid for six months beyond arrival. Nigeria also requires yellow fever and polio vaccination certificates on arrival. World.title: Erie, Pennsylvania, Shooting Leaves 8 Dead
World.content:
Nine people are dead, including the suspected gunman, after a shooting at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania. It happened on Friday 9 October 2026, at about 5 p.m. Eastern time, on the city’s East Side.

Police say there is no ongoing threat to the public, which matters to anyone in Erie or travelling around the Great Lakes region. For readers across the United States, it is also a reminder to rely on official police and city updates while identities are confirmed.

Key Facts —Who. Nine people died, including the suspected gunman; the gunman has not been identified. —What. A shooting at a home left eight victims dead, including at least two children, and the suspected gunman dead of an apparent self-inflicted wound. —Where. 722 Perry Street, near East 7th and Perry streets, on the East Side of Erie, Pennsylvania. —When. Friday 9 October 2026, at about 5 p.m. Eastern time. —Status. As of 10 October 2026, 20:40 GMT

What We Know

Erie is a city of Pennsylvania on Lake Erie, about 117 miles north of Pittsburgh. The shooting took place at a home at 722 Perry Street, near East 7th and Perry streets.

Officers went to the scene after a ShotSpotter alert, a system that uses sensors to detect gunfire and tell police where it came from. Police dispatch was at about 4:50 p.m., and officers arrived within minutes.

The Art Deco clock tower atop a downtown Erie building. File photo: Don O’Brien, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

Two women were found dead on the sidewalk and street outside the home. Police and SWAT officers, a specially trained tactical team, then surrounded the house and obtained a search warrant.

When officers entered, they found more victims dead inside, including at least two children. In total, eight victims and the suspected gunman died.

Police say all of the deaths happened before officers arrived. No shots were fired after police got there, and the loud bangs heard nearby were police flash-bang devices, which make a loud noise and bright flash to disorient people.

The suspected gunman was found dead with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound. Police have said there is no ongoing threat to the public.

Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah described “a horrific scene” and called it the “most difficult and heartbreaking” of his nearly 30 years in law enforcement. He added that “the loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing.”

Lorah also said he had not seen anything like it in more than 28 years in law enforcement. Mayor Daria Devlin said: “Our thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and everyone impacted by tonight’s tragedy.”

Governor Josh Shapiro offered his administration’s full support to Mayor Devlin on Saturday. He is the governor of Pennsylvania.

Shapiro said: “My heart breaks for this family.” He added: “Lori and I are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community.”

A news conference with the mayor and police was scheduled for 4 p.m. Eastern on Saturday. We had not seen its details at the time of writing.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Is Not Known

Police have not released the identity of the suspected gunman. They have also not named the victims or given their ages.

Officials have not said whether the gunman and the victims knew each other. No motive has been given, and we will not speculate on one.

Police have not given a count of any injured people. Further details are expected from official briefings, and we will add confirmed facts as they are released.

What It Means for Readers in the United States

Readers should wait for official identification from police before sharing names or images online. Unverified posts can cause further pain for grieving families.

Visitors to Erie and the wider Great Lakes region should follow guidance from the city and Erie police, who say there is no ongoing threat. The city and police are the best place to check for changes.

Shootings of this kind often prompt debate in the United States about gun laws and public safety. We report the facts here without taking a side, and we will keep the focus on what officials have confirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened in Erie, Pennsylvania?

A shooting at a home at 722 Perry Street on Erie’s East Side on Friday 9 October 2026 left eight victims and the suspected gunman dead. Police responded at about 4:50 p.m. Eastern after a ShotSpotter gunshot-detection alert.

How many people died?

Nine people died, including the suspected gunman. Police say at least two of the victims were children.

Is there still a danger to the public?

Police say there is no ongoing threat to the public. They say all the deaths occurred before officers arrived and no shots were fired after police arrived.

Have the gunman and the victims been identified?

Not yet. Police have not released the identity of the suspected gunman, or the names and ages of the victims, and no motive has been given.
