World.title: ‘I don’t feel fear’: Fulham boss Arbeloa hits back as pressure mounts
World.content:
Ipswich – Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa hit back at his critics after a 2-1 defeat against Ipswich on Saturday extended their winless run in the Premier League to six matches.

Former Real Madrid manager Arbeloa was denied his first win in the English top-flight in painful fashion as Fulham conceded twice in the final moments at Portman Road.

Ryan Sessegnon’s 55th-minute strike for Fulham was cancelled out by Abdoul Ouattara’s long-range rocket in the 88th minute before Dara O’Shea headed home in stoppage-time.

Fulham are mired in the relegation zone as questions mount about Arbeloa’s ability to save his club from a relegation battle.

“I never worry about my position. I don’t feel fear. You cannot be a coach if you feel it,” he said.

“You have to work, take the decision and you need to show confidence to your players.

“It’s not about my position, it is about Fulham’s position. That is the most important thing. Obviously it is just six games, but it is true we need points.”

It is four league losses in six games this season for Arbeloa, whose team have conceded after 75 minutes in matches with Sunderland, Crystal Palace, Manchester United and now Ipswich.

Although Arbeloa had a brief spell at Real last season following Xabi Alonso’s sacking, the former Liverpool defender has never managed in the Premier League before.

His only managerial experience prior to Real came with the Spanish club’s second team.

But the 43-year-old pointed to his impressive playing career with Real, Liverpool and Spain as proof he is equipped to handle the heart.

“Me? No, maybe you don’t know me but I played for the best team in world. I have coached the best team in the world,” he said.

“Maybe you don’t know, but just to let you know, that pressure is part of my life since I was a kid.

“So, it is normal in football. It is normal for players, it is normal for coaches and everybody that is around a team. I think pressure is something that is important for me and I like it.”

World.title: Iraq and US discuss post-coalition ties and dinar exchange rate in Istanbul
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein met with US Special Envoy Tom Barrack in Istanbul on Saturday to discuss the future of Iraq-US ties after the departure of American soldiers, as well as regional security problems and the Iraqi dinar exchange rate.

The meeting comes less than two weeks after the US-led coalition officially terminated its military operation in Iraq on September 30, thereby ending the country’s security connection with Washington.

According to Iraq’s Foreign Ministry, the conversations centered on increasing bilateral cooperation as part of Baghdad and Washington’s new partnership, as well as the effect of continuing regional crises on Iraq’s security and stability.

The two officials also discussed Iraq’s financial and economic condition, especially changes in the Iraqi dinar exchange rate; however, the ministry did not offer specifics on any suggested steps or agreements.

The inclusion of the dinar in the negotiations emphasizes Iraq’s economic link with Washington, especially given the country’s dependence on the US dollar for international commerce and the significance of its banking relationships with the US.

The group also discussed larger regional trends and the need of sustained diplomatic cooperation as Iraq strives to improve its security and economic ties after the coalition exit.

Barrack, who also serves as the US ambassador to Turkey, greeted Hussein in a post on X, praising the connection between Iraq, the US, and Turkey as durable and emphasizing the significance of regional collaboration in solving common difficulties.

The American ambassador also emphasized Istanbul’s historical position as a diplomatic meeting place between East and West, emphasizing the need for holding the meetings at Tersane on the Golden Horn.

Both parties agreed to keep frequent contact and conversations on matters of mutual interest.

The summit underscores the transition in Iraq-US ties from a coalition-led military mission to wider bilateral collaboration, with economic stability, regional security, and diplomacy emerging as key areas of interaction.

World.title: Alonso hails Henderson ‘beauties’ as Chelsea star rolls back the years
World.content:
London – Xabi Alonso praised Jordan Henderson after the Chelsea midfielder rolled back the years with a double in the 5-1 demolition of Bournemouth on Saturday.

Henderson took just 68 seconds to put Chelsea ahead at Stamford Bridge with his first goal for the club.

The 36-year-old set the tone for Chelsea’s stroll in the west London sunshine with a precise finish from Cole Palmer’s pass.

Henderson turned provider two minutes later as his pass reached Morgan Rogers, whose shot deflected in off Antonio Silva.

It was the second-fastest goal and assist combo in Premier League history.

Joao Pedro struck twice, either side of Evanilson’s reply for Bournemouth, before Henderson capped his impressive performance in the 70th minute.

Henderson whipped a superb free-kick past Bournemouth goalkeeper Djordje Petrovic to the delight of Chelsea fans, who urged the hat-trick chasing midfielder to shoot every time he got the ball in the closing stages.

The former Liverpool captain’s influential display came in just his second appearance for Chelsea following his close-season arrival on a free transfer.

Alonso had made Henderson one of his top targets to add experience to a largely youthful side following the England international’s departure from Brentford at the end of last season.

“We signed him for everything and if he is able to score two beauties like today we are more than happy for him,” Alonso said.

“Apart from the goals he has done many good things. He was always involved in the action, giving instructions to the team-mates, he needs to communicate a lot. It was a very good midfield performance.”

– ‘A complete performance’ –

After failing to win any of their previous three league games — including a dismal 3-0 loss at Brentford before the international break — this was a much-needed result for Alonso.

The Spaniard is in his first season in charge but can expect scrutiny if he fails to assemble a cohesive unit from Chelsea’s expensively assembled squad.

“Today was a very complete performance, we were in control for most of the game. We had good stability,” Alonso said.

“Overall happy with the game, many positives to take for the future and we have to keep going.”

The former Real Madrid boss was surprised to see Chelsea strike twice in the first three minutes, adding: “We always try to start the game with good energy, but I have no explanation, no credit to me.

“It has never happened to me to score so many early goals. Let’s see if we can keep doing that.

“Maybe I prefer to score the first one in the last minute! It will happen one day.”

Alonso’s hopes of challenging for Champions League qualification and eventually competing for the Premier League title were boosted on Saturday when England forward Palmer signed a new contract keeping him at the club until 2034.

“Happy for him and very happy for the club as well. I’m sure the fans are happy to have Cole for years,” Alonso said.

“We need to push, we need to help him to have success. He is important in what we are building.

“When you are young you want to keep the best ones for years. We believe Cole is going to be a top-class contract for many years. The longer he is here the better.”

World.title: Thousands join pro-Palestinian marches in London, Berlin
World.content:
London – Several thousand pro-Palestinian protesters marched through central London and Berlin on Saturday, calling for an end to Israeli strikes on Gaza, three years after Hamas’s October 7 attack.

Marchers carried placards reading “End the genocide” and “Free Palestine” as they made their way along the route near the British parliament.

“We are here today to mark three years of the ongoing genocide in Gaza,” Aimee Shalan, director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, told AFP.

She said Western sanctions over settler violence did not go far enough, calling for “full sanctions on Israel”.

A ceasefire began a year ago and although Israel has reduced its level of attacks it has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.

Strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza’s health ministry.

Police said they had made “several arrests” including a man and a woman with placards supporting the organisation Palestine Action, banned under UK law.

Recent graduate Hibo Hassan, 23, said she was there to show her solidarity.

“Although it is happening in the Middle East, it affects us here now,” she said.

“It’s extremely dystopian and that is something we should be all scared about,” she added.

Another protester, a 32-year-old Kosovar immigrant who gave his name as Kobe, said his own experience of war made him want to “stand up today and not let history repeat” itself.

A small counter-demonstration was organised by Stop The Hate UK, a Jewish-led, pro-Israel campaign group.

Ahead of the protest, organised by the Palestine Coalition, London’s Metropolitan Police said it would be using powers under public order legislation to require anyone wearing a face covering to deliberately hide their identity to remove it.

“We will take a zero-tolerance approach to hate crime and other offending,” said senior Met officer Carl Galvin.

– ‘Really terrible’ –

In Berlin, a similar march organised by the group United for Palestine drew around 3,500 people as it set off from a square between the chancellery and parliament, according to police.

Many called out Germany’s arms exports to Israel, carrying banners and placards condemning Berlin’s military support.

For decades, Germany has seen resolute support for Israel as a fundamental duty largely because of Nazi Germany’s responsibility for the genocide of millions of European Jews during the Holocaust.

“I find it really terrible that Germany finds it so difficult to criticise Israel,” a student told AFP, requesting not to be named.

The protests in London and Berlin came three days after the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023 attack.

The attack was the deadliest in Israel’s history, resulting in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.

Militants also dragged 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of them already dead.

In response, Israel launched a military offensive that has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry.

World.title: US dollar eases to 164,000 IQD range across Iraqi parallel exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNewscom) – Parallel market rates for the U.S. dollar retreated slightly across Iraqi trading floors on Saturday, October 10, 2026, pulling back from earlier highs above 170,000 to settle in the low-to-mid 160,000 range.

The downward correction follows days of sharp market adjustments that followed the federal government’s revision of the official benchmark to 152,000 Iraqi dinars per $100 for retail transactions, narrowing the parallel spread against the newly established official baseline.

Data showed that exchange counters and trading hubs in Baghdad posted cash selling rates at 164,000 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 162,000 dinars, registering a drop of several thousand dinars from midweek peaks.

In Erbil, the commercial capital of the Kurdistan Region, parallel counters quoted greenbacks at a selling rate of 162,750 dinars per $100 alongside buying bids of 162,000 dinars.

In the southern trade center of Basra, trading activity balanced at similar levels, with cash sales quoted at 163,500 dinars per $100 and buying bids settling at 163,000 dinars.

The easing across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra reflects tentative price consolidation as currency traders, wholesale merchants, and financial counters adjust to the new statutory pricing framework.

While the initial announcement triggered an immediate liquidity shock across wholesale districts like Shorja, the modest pullback suggests parallel market participants are recalibrating cash demand against the Central Bank of Iraq’s updated sales platform parameters.

World.title: Iraq halts tariffs on poultry and eggs amid rising food inflation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture announced on Saturday, October 10, 2026, the implementation of emergency market interventions aimed at curbing food inflation across domestic retail sectors, with a targeted focus on soaring table egg prices.

In coordinated moves overseen by the General Secretariat of the Council of Ministers, the federal government suspended customs duties and import taxes on imported table eggs, poultry, and live livestock under direct instructions from Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi to expand food supplies and stabilize consumer prices.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Ministry of Agriculture spokesperson Qusay Al-Hattab stated that the Minister of Agriculture directed rapid administrative interventions to neutralize sudden price spikes hitting household staples.

The waiver on customs and border levies is designed to streamline clearance procedures at border checkpoints, allowing immediate inflows of essential poultry and livestock products to increase market competition and protect consumer purchasing power following recent currency fluctuations.

Al-Hattab noted that the ministry had previously imposed strict import bans on specific greenhouse and open-field vegetables—predominantly eggplant, tomatoes, and cucumbers—to safeguard domestic farmers during high-yield harvest seasons.

These seasonal harvest cycles span between 40 and 50 days, during which specialized monitoring teams from the Department of Planning and Follow-up survey major wholesale terminals in Baghdad, including the Jamila, Al-Rasheed, and Zweini wholesale markets. Field inspectors monitor commodity volumes and price fluctuations, submitting real-time assessments to state authorities to determine when supply thresholds justify lifting import restrictions.

The spokesperson attributed current retail price volatility, particularly the recent surge in table egg cartons, to a combination of merchant speculation and the upward adjustment of the U.S. dollar exchange rate.

Al-Hattab stressed that the ministry is not remaining passive amid price increases, maintaining active oversight across wholesale distribution hubs, publishing daily comparative commodity price indexes on its official portal, and balancing the protection of domestic poultry producers with consumers’ access to reasonably priced food.

World.title: Iraq pursues oil-for-funding pact with Turkey for development road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport announced on Saturday, October 10, 2026, active diplomatic and financial maneuvers to conclude an oil-for-financing bilateral pact with Turkey.

The proposed framework aims to establish a dedicated sovereign investment vehicle to fund the construction of the multi-billion-dollar Development Road project by Turkish contracting conglomerates, while international multilateral lenders anchor the initiative’s foundational phase.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Fadhil Abbas, Director of Projects at the General Company for Railways of Iraq (GCRI), explained that the Development Road corridor has entered detailed engineering and design phases.

The transnational initiative aims to overhaul Iraq’s domestic rail grid, integrate internal provincial passenger transit, and establish a high-capacity freight transit land bridge channeling trade flows directly between the Grand Faw Port in Basra and European destinations via Turkey.

Abbas outlined that bilateral talks are progressing toward a binding bilateral accord with Ankara to create a project funding pool backed by Iraqi crude allocations, ensuring seamless capital deployment for Turkish construction firms tasked with building core rail, terminal, and highway segments.

In parallel, Abbas disclosed that the first operational stage of the corridor is advancing under World Bank loan financing. This foundational phase focuses on rehabilitating and upgrading existing mainline rail infrastructure stretching from Baghdad south to Basra and Umm Qasr, as well as north from the capital through Mosul.

The program will physically link these tracks with the deepwater terminals at Grand Faw Port and the northern Turkish international boundary crossing at Fishkhabur.

On the western rail network, GCRI is finalizing restoration work on the strategic Baghdad–Akashat line, bringing critical industrial and mineral transit corridors back online following extensive damage inflicted by Islamic State militants.

Abbas noted that most sectors along the alignment alongside key rail bridges have been restored, leaving only the minor Wadi Fatm bridge, which is currently undergoing final contract awarding.

Addressing urban mass transit, Abbas confirmed that administrative oversight of the Baghdad Metro project has been transferred from the railway company to the Mayoralty of Baghdad, which is currently managing its private investment tendering process.

He clarified that GCRI does not currently retain any tram or inner-city metro portfolios within its active infrastructure mandate.

World.title: Zelensky blasts diesel deal after Russian strikes kill 15
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Saturday that Russia was expressing its “thanks” for a diesel deal agreed with the United States by attacking Ukraine, after fresh Russian attacks killed 15 people, according to authorities.

The deal, which US President Donald Trump announced on Friday after a call with Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin, would see Moscow release large amounts of diesel onto global markets in exchange for sanctions relief.

Zelensky told reporters on Friday that the deal was “unworthy of our partners” and described it as a “weak decision”.

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said on Saturday that lifting sanctions on Russian diesel would help fuel the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine.

“This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won’t,” she wrote online.

Germany also said it would continue to push for new EU sanctions on Russia, despite the agreement.

Moscow has intensified its deadly bombardment of Ukraine in recent months, sending civilian casualties soaring, while US-led efforts to broker an end to the more than four-and-a-half year conflict remain deadlocked.

Early Saturday, Russia targeted residential neighbourhoods in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia with “five guided aerial bombs”, according to Ukraine’s national police service.

At least 15 people were killed, among them three children, Ukraine’s state rescue service said.

“Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia,” Zelensky said in a post on X.

An AFP correspondent at the scene saw people being pulled from the rubble by Ukrainian emergency services.

“We saw people under the rubble — a woman, her husband and a child,” one rescuer, Daniil Pishkin, told AFP.

He added that he saw two people rescued from the wreckage but “unfortunately there was a little girl who died”.

A resident of one of the buildings that was hit, who identified herself as Iryna, 69, said she just had time to seek refuge in the toilets after receiving an air raid warning.

She said her two neighbours were killed.

“They were 75 years old. They were simply thrown out there, onto the street. They didn’t make it to the hospital,” she told AFP.

Ukraine’s capital Kyiv meanwhile suffered “large-scale power outages” on Saturday due to Russian strikes, the country’s largest private energy provider, DTEK, said.

AFP reporters heard booms over the capital earlier Saturday, as the city’s mayor reported that a restaurant had been hit.

– Deal ‘needs to be corrected’ –

The strikes came as Ukraine expressed mounting frustration at Washington’s diesel agreement with Russia.

Prices at US gasoline and diesel pumps have surged since late February, when the United States and Israel launched joint military strikes on Iran.

Announcing the deal on Friday, Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform that diesel prices would be “coming down, in record numbers, and fast”, in all caps.

“I want to thank President Putin, to be honest with you,” he later told reporters.

In a post on Facebook on Saturday, Zelensky said the deal needed to be reversed.

“Russia’s choice is war. And they will be ready to end it only when they feel that their ability to drag the war out is diminishing,” Zelensky said.

“Unfortunately, the signals Russia received yesterday were entirely different – signals suggesting that it could simply keep attacking. This needs to be corrected,” he added.

– Trump’s talk with Putin –

US, Ukrainian and European officials meanwhile met in Miami on Friday in a renewed diplomatic push to end the war.

Trump, who has repeatedly touted his credentials as a peacemaker, has long sought to broker a deal since taking office last January.

US envoy Steve Witkoff posted to X after the meeting that the “constructive discussions” tackled “potential avenues to de-escalate and conclude the war with Russia ahead of winter and advance efforts toward a durable and lasting peace”.

Witkoff said the meeting included “the E3, the European Commission, Ukraine and NATO”.

The Kremlin said Saturday that Trump had conveyed his ideas about how to de-escalate the war to Putin during a phone call on Friday.

Putin received the proposals “with understanding”, the Kremlin said, without elaborating on what the proposals were or the Russian president’s response.

Russia, which launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, now occupies roughly one-fifth of Ukrainian territory.

World.title: Personality rights: HC asks Amitabh Bachchan to appear if settlement fails
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has asked

to appear in person if a settlement with several defendants in a personality rights case remains incomplete and he still wishes to pursue his claims.

Justice Purushaindra K Kaurav passed the direction after the court was informed an amicable settlement had been reached with some defendants through mediation, but could not be formally signed due to logistical issues on Bachchanâs side.

The court granted time to the actor to complete formalities and place the formal agreement on record. The next hearing will be on Nov 16.

The HC said in the event of a non-settlement or incomplete settlement, Bachchan would have to be personally present if he wished to pursue any of his claims. His presence would enable the court to exercise its powers under provisions of Code of Civil Procedure and Section 168 of BSA, the order underlined. Section 168 empowers a judge to ask any question about any fact s/he considers necessary.

World.title: CJP leaders' detention: Here’s all that happened on board AI 2428
World.content:

NEW DELHI: Soon after touching down at Delhi Airport around 10.30 am Saturday with Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) representatives Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on board, the pilots operating AI 2428 were asked to head to a remote bay instead of a parking stand that is connected to an aerobridge. As directed by air traffic control, the ex-Vistara Airbus A320 (VT-TQL) headed to a bay closer to the international wing of T3 and parked there.Then, sources say, the pilots were informed that a team of security personnel would board the aircraft. A passenger stair car (vehicle with a step ladder) got attached and a team of Delhi Police personnel boarded the aircraft and went to the row where CJP representatives were seated. They asked the three to accompany them as they were being detained.âI have come here to be arrested; arrest me,â Dipke is heard telling the police team in videos shot inside the aircraft. The police personnel are heard responding: âNo, this is not an arrest. Please cooperate.â Once the security personnel and the three CJP representatives left the aircraft, the process began for other passengers who had to remain seated for 10-15 minutes to do so.With changed wind direction, aircraft at that time were landing from Dwarka side (this one touched down on IGIAâs fourth runway 11L/29R) and it takes a much longer taxi to reach T3 as they land towards Shivji statue side and then taxi back towards the terminal from taxiway.Air India did not comment on what happened onboard AI 2428. While it is not uncommon for criminals and unruly passengers to be escorted out of aircraft after landing by security agencies, political or social activists getting this treatment is not something that happens frequently.Bay allocation is done by the airport operator, in this case Delhi InternaÂ­tional Airport Ltd. In âspecial circumstancesâ like that Saturday, govt agencies can direct the operator to allocate a remote bay to aircraft. That also happens to aircraft for which a bomb threat has been received.Pilots of AI 2428 were asked to proceed to the remote bay after they landed. Air traffic control guides pilots to the bay they have been allocated by asking them to take taxiway routings.âAviation in general and airports in particular operate in a highly regulated environment. We just get instructions from govt agencies from time to time and have to follow them,â said aviation industry long timers.

World.title: Parliament, not streets, will govern country: BJP; govt is rattled, says oppn
World.content:
BJP says protest a flop; oppn puts united front

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Opposition parties on Saturday lashed out at govt over wide security curbs to foil the Cockroach Janta Party's call for protest at Jantar Mantar but a defiant BJP backed the clampdown, saying Parliament, and not streets, will run the country.BJP president Nitin Nabin alleged two anarchic groups - one of the INDIA bloc and another led by Arvind Kejriwal and his "associate" CJP, were seeking to stoke unrest in the country and were in a battle of one-upmanship over spreading chaos: "They are working in collusion with foreign forces to destabilise India."Congress, which kept away from Saturday's protests, lent its support to the agitating youths and said their "peaceful" stir has left govt rattled and nervous.Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi said, "Youth of India, I am proud of you. Keep protesting. We are standing with you. I have been fighting Narendra Modi and the RSS for over a decade now. The core characteristic of these people is cowardice.""Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Mohan Bhagwat, Gyanesh Kumar and Ajit Doval, the villains of this story, are slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space," he added, claiming that govt may further ramp up security measures but protests over the SIR issue will continue.A combative BJP was, however, categorical that CJP, which had "broken" the conditions under which their members were allowed to launch their stir in July, could not have been allowed to "hijack" Jantar Mantar again. "Democracy has prevailed over anarchy. The country will be governed through Parliament, not the streets. The country cannot be run by spreading anarchy on the streets," Ravi Shankar Prasad said.Speaking at the sixth edition of his youth outreach programme, 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' at Chennai's Island Grounds, Rahul said "Mogambo Modi" was destroying India's democracy, referring to the PM. "Mr Modi doesn't understand that the game is over," he added. "I want to tell all the students in Delhi, do not worry. Stand up for everything you believe in and never stop asking questions," Gandhi said, asserting, "We are standing with you. "SP president Akhilesh Yadav said, "Now, the nation will unite in Delhi! We stand with the youthful energy of the nation. If BJP govt thinks it can halt the people through the might of power, this will prove to be an even greater mistake on its part." Left leaders, including M A Baby of CPM, D Raja of CPI and Dipankar Bhattacharya of CPI(ML), condemned the "widespread repression" unleashed by Delhi Police on peaceful protesters.BJP fielded an array of functionaries to counter the opposition, with Sambit Patra saying the protest turned out to be a flop show by "anarchist forces" and asserting that the national capital cannot be allowed to be held hostage by those stoking disorder.Patra alleged Rahul's show of support to the world's richest person, Elon Musk, over his potshots at the Indian govt's policy is part of his wider efforts, including the campaign against SIR to "help" infiltrators, to draw backing from foreign players to destabilise India and called him Mir Jafar, an 18th-century military commander synonymous with treachery.'

World.title: Restrained, detained, contained: Clampdown foils stir, thousands confined to home, nabbed on way
World.content:
Security arrangements may not see let-up today

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Unprecedented security arrangements from central Delhi to the borders, phalanxes of 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel and a virtual choke on metro services and trains foiled Cockroach Janta Party's march to Jantar Mantar on Saturday. The city, however, remained on edge, with young protesters being detained on their way to the protest site and bundled into buses and vans, kicking and screaming, through the day.With CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das detained at the airport, the outfit's national organisation in-charge, Ajinkya Shinde, was named to lead the protests. The computer science grad, a former AAP worker, said protests would continue till Gyanesh Kumar resigned as CEC.With top CJP functionaries being kept away from Jantar Mantar, small groups dodged security personnel and staged flash protests at Safdarjung flyover, Dilli Haat and Gurdwara Bangla Sahib complex, among other places.The impromptu gathering near Safdarjung flyover by AISA national president Neha Bora, lawyer Prashant Bhushan, political commentator Yogendra Yadav, and several others caught police off-guard momentarily around 1pm.The protesters were eventually detained.It was obvious since Thursday that the call by CJP, supported by some political outfits, for a protest against the CEC and SIR at Jantar Mantar at 10am on Saturday would be met with stiff resistance. New Delhi was divided into 20 zones, with 1-2 companies of CAPF and Delhi Police deployed at every nook and corner. BSF was also present at the city's borders.Water cannons and tear-gas vehicles were kept ready. Multiple layers of barricades were erected and police personnel closely questioned people heading towards the New Delhi area, particularly in the direction of Jantar Mantar. Police said there were only some isolated incidents of minor confrontations. While three or four personnel, including women, were injured in incidents of stone-pelting and other skirmishes, a DCP fractured his hand, they said.Police claimed they had detained 2,500 people in the city â 600-700 people on stretches leading to Jantar Mantar, and others from different parts of Delhi, including the borders. The police figures were, however, hotly contested, with sources saying around 7,000 people were detained, counting those who were not allowed to leave their homes and were put under preventive detention.CJPâs Ajinkya Shinde, who will lead the protests now, alleged more than 15,000 people, including students, civil society members and political functionaries, had been illegally detained across the country. An undeclared emergency had been imposed in Delhi, he said.Police said apart from the fact that permission had not been given for the protest, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force, making the proposed gathering illegal.Four former chief ministers â Aam Aadmi Party convener Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, Keralaâs Pinarayi Vijayan, and Manik Sarkar of Tripura â were detained. CPM veteran Brinda Karat, Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas, and TMC functionaries Derek OâBrien and Dola Sen were also detained.Detained protesters were taken in buses to Chhatrasal Stadium, Rajiv Gandhi Stadium, Yamuna Sports Complex and Surajmal Stadium, all designated earlier for this purpose. Around 600 buses, including some from Third Battalion used to transport prisoners, were used to ferry those detained.Around 9pm, police claimed they had released everyone, but refused to respond when asked about Dipke, Ranka and Das. Multiple cases will be registered in connection with violation of prohibitory orders and assault, besides other sections, police said.With CJP sources saying they will continue their protests and Congress and other INDIA bloc parties planning a march in the city Monday, the security paraphernalia is likely to remain in place for the next few days.

Internet restrictions and arrests during Cockroach Janta Party-led anti-SIR protests in New Delhi triggered sharp political reactions Saturday, as J&K CM Omar Abdullah said the "Kashmir model" had reached the capital, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti called the restrictions a reminder of Kashmir's 2019 lockdown, and CPM described the atmosphere as "akin to the Emergency".Omar said the "Kashmir model has been exported to Delhi. Deputy CM Surinder Choudhary questioned whether the situation was any less serious than during the Emergency and called for chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. National Conference spokesperson Sarah Hayat Shah said New Delhi was witnessing "barely .1% of what was done to Kashmir on Aug 5, 2019. "People were locked in their homes, the internet was shut down, and an entire region was placed under siege," she said, recalling her detention for 14 months after Centre revoked J&K's special status and split it into two Union territories in Aug 2019.Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk gave govt 24 hours to release those detained during the New Delhi protest, warning he could launch a sit-in, hunger strike or march in Leh or the capital city."It appears an undeclared emergency has been imposed across the country," he said, urging govt to resolve the dispute through dialogue.In Punjab, CM Bhagwant Mann slammed Union govt over the detentions. "Where is democracy? Around 80,000 to 90,000 security personnel have been deployed. It is only short of deploying Army to stop them. They are students, they are unarmed. They have come for the sake democracy so that their votes are not deleted... if Gen-Z is coming forward, they should be allowed. Why is Centre scared of Jantar Mantar now?" he said.AAP workers, led by Punjab party in charge Manish Sisodia, held a "vote chori" protest against Kumar outside the chief electoral officer's office in Chandigarh. "If Narendra Modi were genuinely popular and had won elections honestly, he would not be afraid of a few young people sitting at Jantar Mantar. But he is afraid because he has become PM by stealing votes, deleting genuine voters and adding fake votes," Sisodia alleged.In Chennai, DMK president and former Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin condemned the detention of politicians and students protesting against SIR, while Kumar continued to enjoy Z+ security. "Barricading #Delhi, shutting down the internet and detaining politicians cannot crush the uprising of India's youth," he said, demanding Kumar's removal, a halt to SIR and the release of detainees.In Keralam, CPM condemned the detentions as creating an atmosphere "akin to the Emergency" and accused Delhi police of acting like "RSS-BJP goons". Top CPM functionaries along with MPs and functionaries of the party's women's, student and youth wings were detained while trying to join the Jantar Mantar protest. CPM called for demonstrations across Keralam.Congress general secretary KC Venugopal accused PM Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of protecting Kumar at political cost. He said the closure of Delhi Metro stations to curb protesters reflected BJP-led NDA govt's anxiety and announced a large INDIA bloc protest in the capital Monday.

World.title: Anxiety treatable, but 83% of affected did not get help
World.content:
Whenever Thane businessman Shekhar travels to south Mumbai for a meeting, he sets off over three hours early. This is because he plans his route carefully to ensure he is never more than five minutes from a hospital in case he "suffers a heart attack while driving".

Karthik (32), an IIM graduate with a high-powered marketing job, dreads routine meetings. "There is this heaviness in my stomach and my legs seem leaden. It's a paralysing fear that stays until the meeting is over," he says.

Shekhar and Karthik (names changed) have anxiety disorders, a group of conditions that can turn ordinary journeys, workplace interactions and social situations into emotional ordeals.

The invisible burden

National Mental Health Survey, conducted by National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS) across 12 states between 2014 and 2016, found that 2.57% of adults had an anxiety disorder at the time of assessment.

Around 83% of those affected were not receiving treatment, while nearly 60% experienced disability of varying severity, according to the study published in the Indian Journal of Psychiatry in 2022.

"Anxiety disorders are frequently under-recognised and inadequately treated. Stigma surrounding mental illness and a lack of awareness contribute to the problem," said psychiatrist Dr Kedar Tilwe of Fortis Hospital, Mulund.





Child psychiatrist Dr Kersi Chavda said anxiety can take many forms, from social anxiety and academic stress to persistent, intrusive thoughts.

In children, it may manifest as school refusal. Among adolescents facing examinations, anxiety can also present as headaches, body aches or backaches.

Social anxiety is another concern, said Dr Chavda. The pressure to appear perfect, amplified by curated virtual lives on social media, can intensify the fear of being judged or found wanting.

When the body's alarm won't switch off

Everyday anxiety is a normal response to uncertainty or danger. An anxiety disorder involves persistent or disproportionate fear that interferes with daily life.

A senior psychologist from a civic hospital linked anxiety to the body's built-in alarm system. The alarm is meant to respond to a threat, but sometimes it reacts to a gust of wind as though an intruder were approaching.

Psychiatrist Dr Harish Shetty said, "Crowded trains, inadequate sleep, workplace demands, educational pressures, financial worries and concerns about personal safety can keep people in a state of heightened stress."

Weakening support systems and reduced emotional connectedness may also be contributing, said Dr Shetty.

Life in the slow lane

In adults, panic disorder can be accompanied by agoraphobia - fear of situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable if a panic attack occurs.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Patients may avoid bri-dges, crowded trains, flights or traffic jams. Some will not travel without their spouses or may turn down promotions or jobs that require them to venture beyond familiar surroundi-ngs," said Dr Tilwe.

As a result, he added, it's a life lived in second gear: not ready to take up new challenges as one prefers to stick to known schedules.

It's treatable

Anxiety disorders are treatable, but a trained physician is needed to recognise the problem. Treatment depends on the type and severity of the disorder and may involve psychotherapy, medication or both. "A person with a severe anxiety disorder may need counselling along with medication for up to six months to be able to cope," said Dr Tilwe.

Dr Shetty recommends attention to sleep, time management, breathing exercises and meditation. Doctors said reducing excessive caffeine and smoking would help some people manage symptoms.

World.title: Understand, don't just hear out a child in conflict with law: CJI
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant Saturday said a child in conflict with law must not only be heard but also be understood, since few young people can speak up for themselves before the police or any authority.

Speaking on 10 years of the framing of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, Kant said very often, the child in conflict with law today was, only a little earlier, a child in need of care and protection whom we did not reach in time and that should be kept in mind while dealing with them.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Our answer to such a predicament is restoration, not retribution. The Act presumes everyone below 18 to be innocent of any criminal intent, treats institutional care as a last resort, encourages diversion from formal proceedings, and prefers counselling, community service, and probation to confinement, while promising a fresh start.

These choices flow from the Constitutional philosophy discernible from Articles 15(3) and 39 and also from the Convention on the Rights of the Child, which looks to the young assuming a constructive role in society.

The 2015 Act thus makes a wager that a child given a second chance is far more likely to become a productive member of society than one branded as a criminal," he said.

Supreme Court judge, Justice B V Nagarathna, who is heading SC's Juvenile Justice Committee, said adults have a duty to understand the anxieties of children. "We cannot be dismissive of their concerns, lest they feel alienated and rejected. The true measure of a society and its elders lies in how they deal with their children. We must ensure that we do not fail on that count. All children are ours and their distress is our distress too," Nagarathna said.

World.title: 'Tata bye-bye': 2-term BJP MP quits party over Rajya Sabha ticket snub
World.content: MEERUT: Former two-term BJP MP from Aonla in Bareilly, Dharmendra Kashyap, resigned from the party's primary and active membership, alleging that members who worked against BJP during Lok Sabha polls were being rewarded while backward and most backward communities were denied adequate representation and respect. His resignation came days after BJP announced its RS nominees, prompting Kashyap to post "Tata bye-bye" on social media.Kashyap announced his decision through a social media post addressed to BJP national president, state president, Braj region chief and district chief.He did not name anyone in his resignation, but his decision followed BJP's nomination of Shruti Gangwar to RS. Speculation had been growing that he was unhappy with the choice as he had been expecting a nomination himself.The party has not announced whether it has accepted Kashyap's resignation or plans to address his grievances.

World.title: Contract health staff in Andhra Pradesh pause their strike after discussion with officials
World.content:
The A.P. Medical and Health Contract Employees’ Joint Action Committee has decided to pause their ongoing strike following discussions with officials on Saturday, October 10.

The JAC had called for a boycott of duties from October 6 after their demands for regularisation of their services and payment of gross salary remained unmet despite several discussions with the government.

The Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare had earlier conceded to grant a few non-financial requests put forth by the association, including payment of ex gratia to families of contract health staffers who lost their lives in the line of duty during the pandemic, grant of radiation leave for radiographers, among others.

However, since the government maintained that their chief demands of regularisation and payment of gross salaries could not be granted due to the financial situation of the State, the nurses and other contract staff went on a strike.

On Saturday, the JAC members were called for a discussion with the health officials, including Commissioner K.V.N. Chakradhar Babu. The JAC also demanded an incentive of 30%, based on the existing basic pay of contract employees. According to a release from the JAC, the officials had indicated that a special committee would examine this demand.

Considering the positive response, the JAC decided to call off their strike temporarily. The JAC said it did not withdraw its major demands, and that the decision only provided an opportunity to the government to resolve issues through discussions. All the contract staff in the department across the State would resume duties from October 11.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh govt. accepts Dedicated Commission’s recommendations on BC reservation
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet, at its special meeting on Saturday, accepted the recommendations of the Dedicated Commission headed by Rajeev Ranjan Mishra with regard to the provision of reservation for the Backward Classes (BCs) and the total reservations for SC, ST and BC categories put together not exceeding 50% in any local body (rural and urban), as mandated in the triple test by the Supreme Court and in compliance with its judgment in the SLP dated October 9 and with the preceding High Court order.

In the G.O. MS No.17 issued to this effect later, it was stated that the Dedicated Commission had been constituted in compliance with the triple test / conditions required to be complied with as per the judgments of the apex court in the ‘Dr. K. Krishna Murthy & Others Vs. Union of India & Another’, ‘Vikas Kishan Rao Gawali Vs. State of Maharashtra & Others’, and ‘Suresh Mahajan Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh & Another’ with the following terms of conditions: to conduct a contemporaneous and rigorous empirical inquiry into the nature, extent and implications of the backwardness in relation to local bodies with respect to BCs in Andhra Pradesh and to undertake comprehensive empirical assessment for the purpose of determining and specifying the proportion of reservations to be provided to them strictly in conformity with the provisions of the Constitution and adherence to the principles laid down by the Supreme Court in the given judgments.

The G.O. said that the Dedicated Commission submitted its report with necessary recommendations regarding the provision of reservation to BCs local body-wise in due compliance with the triple test mandate laid down by the Supreme Court and other constitutional provisions after conducting a rigorous empirical inquiry into the nature and extent of backwardness of BCs on the basis of the Unified Family Survey, data collected from the Ward and Village Secretariats Department, National Family Health Survey, reports of various commissions, records of Panchayat Raj & Rural Development and Municipal Administration & Urban Development Departments, Census of India etc.

The G.O. mentioned that while implementing the recommendations of the Dedicated Commission, it should also be scrupulously ensured that Articles 243T was complied with, and that the population arrived at by the Commission based on empirical and contemporaneous data from the Unified Family Survey and Ward and Village Secretariats data be taken as the norm for providing reservation to the BCs.

World.title: Anti-CEC protest Highlights, Oct 10: CJP calls for another protest on Sunday amid police crackdown; UNHRC demands immediate release of demonstrators
World.content:
Despite heavy security arrangements, severe transport restrictions, and an Internet shutdown, protesters on Saturday (October 10, 2026) managed to reach locations near Jantar Mantar in central Delhi to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities.

With the designated protest site inaccessible, protesters led by All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora attempted to assemble at Dilli Haat in south Delhi before being detained.

Also Read | Anti-CEC protest: Dilli Haat becomes Jantar Mantar for a day

According to Delhi Police sources, nearly 2,500 protesters were detained across the capital during the day, indicating a high turnout despite the absence of prominent Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders on the ground.

The Supreme Court on Sunday (October 11, 2026) will hear a petition filed by Rajya Sabha MP and senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy against the indiscriminate detentions of leaders, former Chief Ministers, students, youths, journalists, lawyers, and others by the Delhi Police, against the rule of law and democratic dissent.

World.title: Gunman shoots dead 7 relatives, family friend in Pennsylvania
World.content:
A 45-year-old man shot and killed seven relatives and a family friend at a home in Pennsylvania, U.S., before apparently taking his own life, authorities said on Saturday (October 10, 2026).

The victims in the city of Erie included two young children and a woman who was eight months pregnant.

Police responded on Friday evening to reports of shots fired and discovered two women dead in the street, Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah told reporters.

Video evidence showed the pair arriving at the residence appearing distressed, then attempting to contact neighbours and enter the house, Mr. Lorah said.

The gunman exited the house, shot them, and returned inside, he said.

The man barricaded himself inside the home as police surrounded the building and ordered him to exit. He was later found inside with an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound, Lorah said.

The shooter and seven of his victims were related, Mr. Lorah said. The eighth victim was a family friend.

Dead inside the home were a five-year-old boy and a one-year-old girl. The others were men and women ranging in age from 19 to 51. One of the women was eight months pregnant.

Local news outlet Erie News Now said responding officers were being offered counselling over the horrifying incident.

“Many people across our community are hurting today: the neighbours who witnessed what happened, the families and friends of those who were killed, the officers and first responders who answered these calls, and others struggling to make sense of something so terrible,” Erie Mayor Daria Devlin told reporters on Saturday.

“We cannot undo what happened last night, and we cannot take away the grief that these families are carrying, but we can make sure that they don’t have to carry it alone,” she said.

Mass shootings occur frequently in the United States, where guns vastly outnumber people and efforts to increase firearm restrictions face steep political and legal hurdles.

World.title: Anthropic’s Claude AI submits false tip on Philadelphia unsolved homicide case
World.content:
An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false tip to a Philadelphia police website in the U.S. about an unsolved homicide case, authorities and Anthropic said.

It's the latest example of AI models acting in unintended ways and manipulating government and other websites during tests. In a report on Friday, Anthropic also disclosed a separate incident in which its AI model submitted forms to an undisclosed government website instead of stopping before submission.

The incident in Philadelphia occurred on July 18 when the AI model Claude Haiku 4.5 was tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages, Anthropic said.

Claude filled out a form on the police site PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, indicating it might have information regarding an unsolved murder listed on the site.

Philadelphia Police said in a statement they were unaware of the incident until Anthropic notified them on Wednesday. Then they found the submission in the website’s tip records and confirmed it was marked spam and never forwarded to police.

There are rising concerns about AI companies’ unchecked AI agents meddling with everything from U.S. government websites to healthcare data. Critics have been calling for more regulation.

In September, another AI company, OpenAI, disclosed six reports of “unexpected or concerning” behaviour in artificial-intelligence models.

“Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers," the Philadelphia Police Department said in a statement. “Technology companies must take all appropriate steps necessary to prevent their systems from submitting false information to law enforcement.”

Anthropic said in its report that most of the reported behaviors are forms of what it calls “persistence" — “in which Claude, when it cannot complete a task as given, works around a restriction instead of stopping.”

The company said it was modifying its training to “reduce the likelihood of further misbehavior.”

Anthropic said it briefed the White House on cases that involved U.S. government agencies at the federal, state and local levels, and notified each agency involved.

World.title: Missile strikes passenger terminal at Riyadh airport; 12 killed, over 300 wounded
World.content:
An attack on the international airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital killed 12 people and injured over 300 others, civil aviation authorities said early Sunday (October 11, 2026), with some in critical condition.

The attack was the deadliest in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war, whose fronts have expanded to include the recent surge in fighting between the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen and Saudi-backed government forces there.

The statement, which did not assign blame for the attack, said the dead included four Saudi citizens as well as two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a U.S. citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said the injured were being treated at several hospitals.

The attack — the latest of several in the past week on King Khalid International Airport — is expected to increase Saudi pressure on allies including the United States to provide military support for the kingdom.

Shortly after the attack on Saturday afternoon, President Donald Trump said he was evaluating whether the US should join Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

The Houthis claimed attacks earlier in the week on King Khalid International Airport that killed three Saudis, including a pilot. On Saturday, a missile struck a complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media.

“We may. We’re going to look at it,” Trump said of intervening. “We just found out about the recent attack. So we’ll make a decision. We move very quickly.”

The surge in attacks, including against other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis. There was no immediate statement from the rebels, who earlier Saturday accused Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa International Airport in the Houthi-held Yemeni capital.

Riyadh airport operations suspended

Saudi civil aviation authorities earlier said airport operations were suspended and the extent of injuries and damage was being assessed. An official notice to aviators said the suspension was through midnight. The airport had a heavy police presence, with all entrances blocked, and lights around the complex were dimmed.

Flights diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said. Countries including the United States, Britain, Germany, Australia and Canada warned citizens to avoid the airport.

The attacks on Saudi Arabia, the world’s top oil exporter, have rattled markets and the region. And yet the Saudi energy ministry hours after the latest one was still promoting a major international energy conference set to begin in Riyadh on Sunday.

Fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for government forces attempting to reverse recent Houthi gains along the Red Sea. Those gains gave the rebels better surveillance of shipping on a corridor that is a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships.

Though the Houthis have told the AP and others they are only targeting Saudi shipping as part of a blockade in retaliation for one imposed on them, concerns about wider attacks persist. The Houthis previously attacked other ships after the war in Gaza began, calling it solidarity with Palestinians. A U.S. bombing campaign sharply limited that.

Saudi Arabia has run low on interceptors, officials say

Saudi Arabia is running low on missile interceptors and has asked France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt to deploy air defense support to the region, regional officials told the AP last month, with one noting that the U.S. has seen its own stock dwindle during the war with Iran.

Officials have said U.S. assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive against the Houthis.

On Saturday, Saudi Arabia said its foreign minister and Omani counterpart spoke by phone about the importance of “supporting diplomatic solutions to de-escalate tensions” in the region. Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, has played a mediator role at times in the region.

Meanwhile, Saudi authorities warned the public this week that “filming, publishing or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability.”

World.title: Protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls | Full Coverage
World.content:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijit Dipke on October 3 called for a Jantar Mantar protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and the Election Commission of India’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

The CJP has called for criminal action against Mr. Kumar and also demanded his resignation.

Ahead of the large protest, authorities have imposed strict security measures and traffic restrictions across New Delhi, with police personnel and Border Security Force (BSF) jawans deployed at key points.

More than 55 Delhi metro stations have been closed, several rail services reduced and cancelled, citing the likelihood of “unruly crowd movement towards sensitive locations”. Several groups, including the CJP, alleged that protesters were being picked up from across the country.

The Ministry of Home Affairs has approved a temporary Internet suspension and also provided the Delhi Police with additional Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel to strengthen security arrangements.

Security forces started blocking more roads along key routes in New Delhi, such as Janpath and Ashoka Road, on October 10. Police personnel and security forces held debriefing sessions with large numbers of officials who were seen carrying tear gas munitions.
